attributes.name: Unified Viewer — Filter Infrastructure
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Manages user-controlled filter state for the Unified Viewer, narrowing the rendered graph and footer entity count across multiple categorical dimensions ("Ontology Class", "Project/System", "COMPONENT"). The Zustand store (`viewer-store.ts`) is the single source of truth; all filter components read and write state through it.

## Architecture
- **State store**: `viewer-store.ts` — Zustand store; single source of truth for all filter dimensions
- **Filter dimensions**: "Ontology Class", "Project/System", "COMPONENT" — each independently controlled
- **`[]` sentinel pattern (critical invariant)**: Empty array `[]` means "all items in this category are visible" — never "none selected"; any handler that modifies item-level visibility **must** expand `[]` to the full item list before adding or removing an entry; failure produces incorrect state transitions
- **Canonical reference implementation**: Per-item checkbox handlers in `OntologyFilter.tsx` correctly implement the `[]` materialization pattern — treat as the reference for all filter component implementations
- **Dev server**: Vite dev server runs on port 5173; use `lsof -i :5173` to confirm the active process and working directory before editing filter source files

## Key Files
- `viewer-store.ts` — Zustand filter state store; single source of truth
- `OntologyFilter.tsx` — canonical reference implementation of the `[]` sentinel expansion pattern for per-item checkbox handlers

## Usage
- Filter components in the Unified Viewer UI read active filter state from `viewer-store.ts` and dispatch updates through it
- Graph rendering and footer entity count both derive from the same filter state — changes propagate to both consumers automatically
- New filter dimensions must implement the `[]` sentinel expansion pattern as demonstrated in `OntologyFilter.tsx`

## Troubleshooting
- **Incorrect entity count in footer**: Usually caused by a filter handler that skips `[]` expansion before modifying item-level visibility; audit the handler against the `OntologyFilter.tsx` reference implementation
- **Filter appears to select nothing when toggling from "all visible"**: `[]` was not expanded to the full item list before removal — handler is missing the materialization step
- **Dev server not found at port 5173**: Run `lsof -i :5173` to find the active process; if missing, start Vite from the correct working directory before editing filter source files

metadata.scope: The Zustand-backed filter state management layer for the Unified Viewer graph and entity count display
metadata.summary:
## Purpose
Manages user-controlled filter state for the Unified Viewer, narrowing the rendered graph and footer entity count across multiple categorical dimensions ("Ontology Class", "Project/System", "COMPONENT"). The Zustand store (`viewer-store.ts`) is the single source of truth; all filter components read and write state through it.

## Architecture
- **State store**: `viewer-store.ts` — Zustand store; single source of truth for all filter dimensions
- **Filter dimensions**: "Ontology Class", "Project/System", "COMPONENT" — each independently controlled
- **`[]` sentinel pattern (critical invariant)**: Empty array `[]` means "all items in this category are visible" — never "none selected"; any handler that modifies item-level visibility **must** expand `[]` to the full item list before adding or removing an entry; failure produces incorrect state transitions
- **Canonical reference implementation**: Per-item checkbox handlers in `OntologyFilter.tsx` correctly implement the `[]` materialization pattern — treat as the reference for all filter component implementations
- **Dev server**: Vite dev server runs on port 5173; use `lsof -i :5173` to confirm the active process and working directory before editing filter source files

## Key Files
- `viewer-store.ts` — Zustand filter state store; single source of truth
- `OntologyFilter.tsx` — canonical reference implementation of the `[]` sentinel expansion pattern for per-item checkbox handlers

## Usage
- Filter components in the Unified Viewer UI read active filter state from `viewer-store.ts` and dispatch updates through it
- Graph rendering and footer entity count both derive from the same filter state — changes propagate to both consumers automatically
- New filter dimensions must implement the `[]` sentinel expansion pattern as demonstrated in `OntologyFilter.tsx`

## Troubleshooting
- **Incorrect entity count in footer**: Usually caused by a filter handler that skips `[]` expansion before modifying item-level visibility; audit the handler against the `OntologyFilter.tsx` reference implementation
- **Filter appears to select nothing when toggling from "all visible"**: `[]` was not expanded to the full item list before removal — handler is missing the materialization step
- **Dev server not found at port 5173**: Run `lsof -i :5173` to find the active process; if missing, start Vite from the correct working directory before editing filter source files

attributes.name: ObservationExporter — km-core Data Sourcing
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Renders the km-core knowledge graph as an interactive node graph with filter panels (including the Online filter for entity ancestry traces). Connects to obs-api at `:12436` for all graph data. `ApiClient.ts` mediates every fetch between the frontend and the obs-api REST layer.

## Architecture
- **Node fetch layer**: `listEntities()` in `ApiClient.ts` is the primary data fetch call; it carries a silent 1000-entity cap — when the graph exceeds 1000 nodes, the viewer renders whatever subset is returned, causing disconnected "island" artifacts where edges reference nodes that were not fetched. The cap is not surfaced as an error or warning.
- **Fix for node cap**: remove or raise the limit in `listEntities()` to request the full node set; rebuild `integrations/unified-viewer/dist/` after the change
- **Filter panels**: include the Online filter for ancestry trace display; ancestry correctness depends on both complete node fetch and correct `ontologyClass` assignments in km-core (see km-core Ontology Hierarchy Root Enforcement insight)
- **Data source**: all entity and edge data served by obs-api (`:12436`); viewer dist must be rebuilt after any `ApiClient.ts` or source change

## Key Files
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/ApiClient.ts` — `listEntities()` method; 1000-node fetch cap; primary data fetch entry point
- `integrations/unified-viewer/dist/` — compiled viewer artifacts; must be rebuilt after any source change; mtime used as rebuild confirmation signal
- obs-api at `:12436` — backend data source for all `listEntities()` and related calls

## Usage
Viewer is accessed via HTTP on its exposed Docker port. `listEntities()` is called on graph load and on filter interaction. Any knowledge graph exceeding 1000 nodes requires the cap to be removed before rendering is reliable. After modifying `ApiClient.ts`, rebuild `integrations/unified-viewer/dist/` and confirm the mtime has advanced.

## Troubleshooting
- **Disconnected node "islands" in viewer after data repair**: primary suspect is the 1000-node cap in `listEntities()` in `ApiClient.ts`; confirm node count exceeds 1000 by querying obs-api directly, then remove/raise the cap and rebuild viewer dist
- **Islands persist after cap fix**: secondary cause may be stale or race-clobbered `general.json` (see km-core multi-instance write race); verify obs-api is the sole active `GraphKMStore` writer
- **Ancestry trace truncates in Online filter**: `ontologyClass` misclassification on a root entity (e.g., CK entity tagged `"Detail"`); see km-core Ontology Hierarchy Root Enforcement insight for repair procedure
- **Viewer dist not reflecting code change**: dist must be rebuilt after any source change; verify mtime on `integrations/unified-viewer/dist/`
- **`listEntities()` returning partial dataset with no error**: silent cap is the cause — no warning or truncation signal is emitted; the only indicator is comparing returned node count against total node count from obs-api

attributes.name: ObservationConsolidator — Synthesis Pipeline and LLM Token Budget
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Manages the full LLM call lifecycle for insight consolidation: constructs prompts, submits them to the proxy, detects truncation or empty-response failures, and decides whether to retry, abort early, or defer digests to the next healthy trigger. Two primary failure modes — prompt token bloat and proxy unavailability amplified by a long per-call timeout — are mitigated by summary truncation, debug logging, and a proxy-aware circuit breaker.

## Architecture
- Routes all LLM calls through `rapid-llm-proxy/proxy-bridge/server.mjs` via `/api/complete`
- **`_buildInsightPrompt`**: embeds up to `RELEVANT_K=10` existing-insight summaries per chunk; raw summaries are 5–13 KB each; without truncation, combined input reaches 26–32k tokens
- **Token budget constraint**: 16,384 max-output cap; exceeded prompts cause silent empty responses (copilot/sonnet backends) or multi-minute gateway hangs on other backends
- **360-second per-call timeout**: when the proxy is down, each queued call ties up a timeout slot before failing; concurrent pending calls can produce long apparent backlogs

## Key Files
- `rapid-llm-proxy/proxy-bridge/server.mjs` — LLM proxy endpoint; all consolidation calls route here via `/api/complete`

## Usage
- Invoked by the observation consolidation pipeline when enough new digests have accumulated to warrant a synthesis pass
- Outputs persisted insight articles consumed downstream by the memory system

## Troubleshooting
- **Silent empty responses**: Likely prompt token bloat exceeding the 16,384 output cap; verify `RELEVANT_K` and per-summary truncation are active in `_buildInsightPrompt`
- **Multi-minute hangs per call**: Proxy is likely down; the 360-second timeout will expire per call — check proxy health before queuing large consolidation runs
- **Insight content truncated in output**: Raw summaries may exceed the per-insight size budget; confirm `_buildInsightPrompt` applies truncation before embedding existing summaries

attributes.name: `/loop` Skill — Self-Paced Event-Driven Scheduling
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Provides a `/loop` skill that enables agents to schedule recurring or event-driven wake cycles with flexible pacing. Supports explicit timed intervals, trailing duration clauses in task descriptions, and dynamic event-gated mode that reacts to log signals rather than polling on a fixed timer.

## Architecture
Three input patterns drive the skill's behavior:

- **Leading token interval** — explicit fixed cadence (e.g., "every 5 minutes"); values must align with cron syntax; non-divisible intervals are rounded and the user is notified of the adjustment
- **Trailing "every" clause** — interval appended to a task description (e.g., "check status every 10 minutes")
- **Dynamic (event-gated) mode** — triggered when no explicit interval is specified; arms a persistent `Monitor` targeting log patterns plus a `ScheduleWakeup` safety-net fallback (typically 25 minutes)

**Interval routing for long/daily periods (≥ 60 min):**
- `AskUserQuestion` presents a cloud-vs-session choice to the user
- **Cloud path**: delegates to the `schedule` skill via `CronCreate` for durable loops that persist across session restarts
- **Session path**: uses `ScheduleWakeup` with fallback heartbeat delays; state is session-local only

**Dynamic mode lifecycle:**
1. `Monitor` is armed on defined completion-signal strings (e.g., progress markers, terminal status messages)
2. `ScheduleWakeup` serves as a safety-net fallback window
3. Upon signal detection: agent processes results and terminates the loop by omitting the next `ScheduleWakeup` call and stopping the `Monitor`

Edge cases (empty prompts, daily-only patterns in session mode) are skipped without error.

## Key Files
This skill is implemented within the Claude agent runtime as a skill definition; no filesystem paths are applicable.

## Usage
Invoked via the `/loop` command with optional interval or task description. Best suited for:
- **Dynamic mode**: monitoring long-running batch jobs with unpredictable completion times; most token-efficient because it reacts to events rather than polling
- **Interval mode**: recurring scheduled tasks with known, predictable cadence
- **Cloud mode**: durable background loops that must survive session restarts (via `schedule` skill and `CronCreate`)

## Troubleshooting
- **Loop never fires after arming**: Verify that Monitor trigger patterns match actual log output exactly; matching may be case-sensitive or whitespace-sensitive
- **Loop fires repeatedly without advancing**: Dynamic Monitor may be matching intermediate progress events instead of terminal completion — refine the trigger pattern to a unique completion string
- **Safety-net `ScheduleWakeup` fires before Monitor signal**: Normal fallback behavior; if recurring, confirm the Monitor is correctly armed and log patterns are actually emitted by the target process
- **Long-interval loop lost after session restart**: Session-local `ScheduleWakeup` does not persist across restarts — use cloud path (`CronCreate` via `schedule` skill) for durable loops
- **Non-divisible interval accepted silently**: Interval is rounded to the nearest valid cron expression with user notification; supply a clean divisor (e.g., 5, 10, 15 min) at invocation if the rounded value is unacceptable

attributes.name: Truthfulness Verifier — Insight Claim Verification
attributes.description:
## Purpose
The Coverage page in `system-health-dashboard` visualizes per-project claim verification status using a strict, unambiguous color-to-state mapping. Tiles deep-link to individual insight records using the native km-core UUID `id` as the canonical public identifier. All tile rendering, legend swatches, project-header badge, and deep-link href logic are co-located in a single file.

## Architecture
- **Single rendering file**: all Coverage page visual logic lives in `src/pages/coverage.tsx` within `integrations/system-health-dashboard/`
- **Canonical tile state → color mapping:**
  - `pending` → grey (verifier has not yet run; grey is **reserved exclusively** for this state)
  - `unverifiable` / `no claims` → beige/tan (`totalClaims = 0` or non-repo content); explicit high-contrast Tailwind text/background overrides applied; **intentionally distinct from grey** to prevent visual ambiguity with pending
  - `hallucinated` → distinct non-grey color (claims reference content not present in repo)
- **Legend**: present in page header with swatches for each claim state; legend text uses `text-muted-foreground` Tailwind class, which may produce insufficient contrast on light page backgrounds — a targeted style override is the known remediation
- **Deep-linking**: tile `href` uses the native km-core UUID `id` field as the canonical public identifier
- **Refresh semantics**: the "Refresh" button re-reads cached insight metadata only; it does NOT re-execute the verifier pass

## Key Files
- `src/pages/coverage.tsx` — all tile rendering, color mapping, legend, deep-link href logic, contrast overrides

## Usage
Accessed via the system-health-dashboard UI. Coverage states reflect the last explicit verifier pass, not live computation. The "Refresh" button reloads cached data only.

## Troubleshooting
- **Low-contrast `unverifiable`/`no claims` tiles**: verify the explicit Tailwind text and background class overrides are present in `coverage.tsx` for these tile states; the defaults produce near-illegible white-on-light-grey
- **Illegible legend text on light background**: `text-muted-foreground` provides insufficient contrast against the page's light gray background; apply an explicit foreground color override directly to the legend text elements — this is a known open issue
- **Grey tiles appearing for non-pending items**: grey must be reserved exclusively for `pending`; if `unverifiable`/`no claims` renders grey, the beige/tan override has been removed or overridden

attributes.name: Insight Claim Verification — Dual-Mode Design
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Establishes the per-variant snapshot state foundation for experiments, enabling deterministic snapshot identity and deduplication across variant runs. All code review findings (CR-01 blocker and WR-01–WR-04 warnings) have been resolved, verified at code/test/live levels, and the phase is formally closed.

## Architecture
**Core function**: `digestRestoredState` in `experiment-restore.mjs` computes a deterministic hash for snapshot identity.

**Critical design constraint — LevelDB non-determinism**:
- Raw LevelDB store files are **not** byte-deterministic across process runs: internal compaction, SST file layout, and MANIFEST ordering vary between runs for identical logical content.
- `digestRestoredState` hashes the **canonical JSON export** of LevelDB state — not the on-disk LevelDB directory or files. This is the only reliable basis for state identity and deduplication.
- Hashing raw LevelDB files directly produces divergent hashes across runs even when logical content is identical.

**Resolved findings**:
- **CR-01 (Blocker, resolved)**: Hashing target corrected from raw LevelDB files to canonical JSON export in `experiment-restore.mjs`.
- **WR-01 – WR-04**: Four warnings resolved alongside the blocker.

**Test suite baseline**: 45 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip.

## Key Files
- `experiment-restore.mjs` — contains `digestRestoredState`; implements canonical JSON-export-based state hashing for snapshot identity

## Usage
The snapshot digest is consumed by the experiment execution pipeline to establish stable per-variant snapshot identity. Used for deduplication and as the stable anchor for experiment spec tracking across variant runs.

## Troubleshooting
- **Non-deterministic digests across runs for identical logical state**: Verify `digestRestoredState` hashes the JSON export path, not the LevelDB directory or raw SST files.
- **Digest divergence after process restart**: A known symptom of hashing LevelDB files directly — the JSON export is the only byte-stable representation.
- **Test regression detection**: Baseline is 45 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip; deviations indicate a regression in snapshot hashing or restore logic.

attributes.name: /loop Command — Lifecycle and Parser
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Provides a repeating monitoring command that re-evaluates a prompt on a schedule until an explicit stop condition is reached. Used to watch long-running tasks (consolidation runs, verification jobs, etc.) and terminate automatically when the target condition is met.

## Architecture
The `/loop` spec defines a **three-rule parser** evaluated in strict order:
1. **Leading token rule**: a recognized leading keyword in the command triggers that mode directly.
2. **Trailing `every` clause**: an explicit interval (e.g., `every 5m`) sets a fixed-schedule repeat.
3. **No interval detected**: falls through to **dynamic mode**.

**Dynamic mode behavior (no interval provided):**
- Arms a persistent Monitor.
- Executes the prompt immediately on first invocation.
- Re-arms via `ScheduleWakeup` with a **1200–1800 second fallback heartbeat** between evaluations.
- Continues indefinitely until explicitly stopped.

**Termination mechanic**: Omit the `ScheduleWakeup` call on the evaluation where the stop condition is satisfied — its absence is the termination signal.

## Key Files
- Loop spec is defined in command configuration (exact path not confirmed in available data).

## Usage
Invoked as `/loop [prompt] every [interval]` for fixed-schedule monitoring, or `/loop [prompt]` for dynamic mode with the 1200–1800 second heartbeat. Commonly used to watch consolidation jobs, verification pipelines, or other long-running background tasks.

## Troubleshooting
- If the loop does not stop when expected, verify that `ScheduleWakeup` is being omitted on the evaluation where the stop condition triggers — the loop continues as long as `ScheduleWakeup` is called.
- If fixed-interval mode fires at unexpected intervals, verify the `every` clause is syntactically present — if absent, the parser falls through to dynamic mode (1200–1800 second heartbeat), which may appear as irregular firing.

## Purpose
`PROJECT.md` and `ROADMAP.md` serve as the canonical source of truth for the GSD project's current position, completed work, and upcoming phases. They are the first documents to consult when orienting to the project state.

## Architecture
The project organises work into numbered **Plans** (granular implementation units) and **Milestones/Phases** (larger feature or subsystem deliverables). A `km-core` Git submodule exists as a dependency that must be updated in lockstep with host-repo changes. The current known backlog contains three major remaining areas:

- **Phase 33** — Health Monitoring Consolidation
- **Milestone 37** — km-core-foundation
- **Milestone 38** — ontology-registry

## Key Files
- `PROJECT.md` — top-level project description and status overview
- `ROADMAP.md` — milestone/phase tracking; authoritative list of completed and pending work
- `km-core/` — Git submodule; changes here require coordinated commits in both the submodule and the parent repo

## Usage
Consult `ROADMAP.md` at the start of any work session to confirm the current phase and identify the next actionable item. When completing a Plan or Milestone, update both `ROADMAP.md` and any relevant submodule references before merging to `main`.

## Troubleshooting
- If the repo appears out of sync after a merge, run `git submodule update --init --recursive` to realign `km-core`.
- If `ROADMAP.md` and commit history disagree on what has landed, treat the commit history on `main` as ground truth and update `ROADMAP.md` accordingly.
- Unresolved phase ordering questions should be reconciled in `ROADMAP.md` before starting implementation, not during.

attributes.name: D3GraphCanvas — Unified Viewer Graph Interaction Component
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Provides the D3-based interactive graph canvas in the unified viewer. Responsible for atomic node selection, background-click deselection, bidirectional hover with pulse effect, history-row-driven pan-zoom centering, multi-ring halo rendering, selection-history stacking, and layer fit-to-bounds transitions. Serves as the graph endpoint of the bidirectional selection and hover synchronization loop across all viewer panels.

## Architecture
- **Atomic node-click handling**: all selection state fields updated in a single `setState` call; mirrors the same pattern used in `LslTimelineStrip.tsx`
- **Sibling-clear invariant R2**: node-click must clear `selectedSessionId` and `selectedSessionStartAt` together in the same atomic `setState`; clearing one without the other violates CR-02
- **Bidirectional hover with pulse**: store-driven hover signals propagate in both directions — graph node hover → store → sidebar highlight; sidebar item hover → store → D3 pulse effect on corresponding node; entities filtered out of the current view receive a visual indicator when hovered from the sidebar
- **Background-click (`clearSelection`) routing**: dispatches through `viewer-store.ts`, clearing active selection across all panels
- **History-row-to-graph pan-zoom centering**: reactive effect monitors history-row selection state and pans/zooms the D3 canvas to center the corresponding node
- **Multi-ring halo rendering**: rings rendered on all graph nodes touching the selected tick(s) via `selectedBucketEntityIds` and `selectedNodeTickKeys`; `nodeToBuckets` reverse index stored in `useRef`, read at click time to eliminate stale closures
- **Selection-history stacking**: node selection history maintained in the store; back-navigation across selection states is supported
- **Layer fit-to-bounds transitions**: on layer switch, D3 canvas animates to fit the bounds of the new layer's visible nodes
- **Phase 45 invariant (critical)**: `selectedNodeId` MUST NOT appear in the main render-effect dependency list — causes render loops if violated
- **Zero console.log policy**: `D3GraphCanvas.tsx` contains no `console.log` statements (enforced)
- **Audit contract**: 0 improper `useViewerStore.setState` calls confirmed across all unified viewer components
- **Test coverage**: unit tests (including dedicated hover tests) + 4 Playwright E2E tests; E2E tests drive the store directly and bypass real D3 paint — visual rendering correctness requires human smoke testing

## Key Files
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/components/D3GraphCanvas.tsx` — D3 graph canvas; atomic node-click; bidirectional hover + pulse; `clearSelection`; history-row pan-zoom; multi-ring halo; selection-history stack; layer fit-to-bounds; Phase 45 invariant enforced; zero console.log
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/components/D3GraphCanvas.hover.test.tsx` — hover behavior unit tests; graph→sidebar and sidebar→D3 signal paths
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/store/viewer-store.ts` — selection slice including `selectedBucketEntityIds`, `selectedNodeTickKeys`, `selectedBucketKeys`; hover signal fields; `clearSelection` action; `selectedSessionId`/`selectedSessionStartAt` sibling fields
- `tests/e2e/unified-viewer/` — E2E test suite (4+ tests, store-driven, bypass D3 paint)
- `.planning/phases/56-unified-viewer-bidirectional-selection-timeline-scale/56-PATTERNS.md` — 6 state-model contracts; Phase 45 render-effect invariant

## Usage
Rendered within the unified viewer at `localhost:5173/viewer/coding`. Node clicks trigger atomic selection; canvas background clicks clear selection; graph node hover emits a store hover signal consumed by the sidebar; sidebar item hover emits a store hover signal consumed by the D3 pulse renderer; history-row selections trigger pan-zoom centering; tick selection triggers multi-ring halo rendering; layer transitions trigger fit-to-bounds animation. Visual rendering must be verified via human smoke test — E2E tests bypass D3 paint. Use port 5174 when 5173 is occupied.

## Troubleshooting
- **`selectedSessionStartAt` persists after node-click cleared `selectedSessionId`**: sibling-clear R2 violated; both must be cleared in the same atomic `setState`
- **Hover pulse not appearing on graph node when sidebar item hovered**: sidebar→store hover signal not emitted, or D3 pulse effect not subscribed to the store hover field; verify the hover action and the D3 effect dependency
- **Sidebar item not highlighted when graph node hovered**: graph→store hover signal not emitted or sidebar not reading the store hover field
- **Multi-ring halos not rendering on tick selection**: `selectedBucketEntityIds` not populated, or `nodeToBuckets` index stale — verify `useRef` read pattern at click time
- **Layer fit-to-bounds not animating on layer switch**: reactive effect for fit-to-bounds not triggered; inspect its dependency on the layer-switch event
- **Selection-history not enabling back-navigation**: history stack not pushed on node selection — verify push logic in the atomic `setState` block
- **Selection-history or fit-to-bounds absent unexpectedly**: these features were previously reverted by a phantom agent session; confirm commits are present in git history before diagnosing at the code level
- **Render loops after selection changes**: Phase 45 invariant violated — `selectedNodeId` added to render-effect dependency list; remove immediately
- **Background click does not clear selection**: click handler not distinguishing D3 canvas background from nodes; verify `clearSelection` dispatch path
- **E2E tests pass but visual behavior is wrong**: E2E tests bypass D3 paint; only a human smoke test surfaces visual rendering defects
- **Console logs in `D3GraphCanvas.tsx`**: violates zero-log policy; remove before merging

attributes.name: D3GraphCanvas — Bidirectional Graph Selection Component
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Prevents timeline tick clicks from dispatching graph node IDs that are not rendered in the D3 canvas (phantom IDs). When a clicked entity ID has no corresponding rendered node, the system walks the entity's ancestry via BFS to return the nearest visible ancestor. The primary LLS-domination bug — an inverted `capturedBy` edge walk direction in `ancestry.ts` — has been corrected; Option B2 suppression provides defense for residual data-defect cases.

## Architecture
**Root cause of phantom IDs:**
- `LslTimelineStrip.onTickClick` sources the raw entity ID from `entities[0]`, which is a Detail-level Observation entity
- The D3 render pipeline explicitly excludes Observation/Digest/Detail-layer nodes and materializes only structural nodes (Project/Component/SubComponent)
- The sidebar renders phantom entities correctly because it reads directly from the store; `applySelectionStyling` and edge rendering fail silently

**BFS traversal (corrected):**
- `ancestry.ts` previously walked `capturedBy` edges in the inverted direction, causing BFS to terminate at `LiveLoggingSystem` in ~49/75 non-empty buckets
- The corrected walk direction resolves the majority of LLS-fallback misresolutions

**Residual data defect:**
- All Observation nodes carry only a single outgoing relation (`capturedBy → LiveLoggingSystem`); semantic-content edges (`discusses`, `mentions`, `references`) linking Observations to Insights/Components are absent from the ingest pipeline
- For buckets where the data defect applies, even the corrected BFS terminates at LLS; Option B2 (`noiseAncestors`) suppression handles these cases

**Resolution layer:**
- `resolveToVisibleAncestor(entityId, visibleIds)` — entry point in `ancestry.ts`; delegates to `pickFirstResolvable`
- `pickFirstResolvable` — BFS deepest-first traversal with corrected edge direction; returns deepest entity in the ancestry chain present in the visible set
- `pickAllResolvable` — BFS diamond-hierarchy-safe traversal returning all visible ancestors; used for Phase 56.1 many-to-many paths
- `visibility-predicate.ts` — encapsulates the "is this entity rendered?" test
- `useVisibleEntityIds.ts` — React hook exposing the currently-rendered node ID set
- Wiring: `D3GraphCanvas.tsx` and `LslTimelineStrip.tsx` invoke resolution before dispatching to `viewer-store.ts`
- 6th design contract locked in `56-PATTERNS.md` as a permanent architectural constraint

## Key Files
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/graph/ancestry.ts` — `resolveToVisibleAncestor`, `pickFirstResolvable`, `pickAllResolvable`; corrected `capturedBy` BFS walk; `noiseAncestors` Option B2 suppression
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/graph/visibility-predicate.ts` — visibility predicate layer
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/graph/useVisibleEntityIds.ts` — React hook; currently-rendered node ID set
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/graph/ancestry.test.ts` — unit tests for BFS direction, suppression, and `useNodeToBucketsIndex`
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/components/D3GraphCanvas.tsx` — click handler wired to resolution
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/panels/coding/LslTimelineStrip.tsx` — `entities[0]` raw Detail-level entity source; zero net-new setState calls
- `.planning/phases/56-.../56-PATTERNS.md` — 6th design contract documentation

## Usage
Invoked automatically at click time within `D3GraphCanvas.tsx` and `LslTimelineStrip.tsx` before writing to `viewer-store.ts`. No direct external API — resolution is an internal click-handling step. The corrected BFS direction handles the majority of cases; Option B2 suppression handles residual LLS-fallback. Resolved IDs propagate through selection state to `SidePanel` and the D3 ring/trace renderer.

## Troubleshooting
- **LLS still dominates bucket resolution after BFS direction fix**: verify `ancestry.ts` has the corrected `capturedBy` walk direction; if correct but LLS still appears, Option B2 suppression is not filtering or the data defect applies (no alternate path in stored data)
- **Ring/edge rendering fails silently despite sidebar showing entity correctly**: phantom ID reached the store unresolved; verify `resolveToVisibleAncestor` is called before store dispatch
- **Phantom node IDs reaching the store**: click handler not calling resolution upstream of `setState` dispatch; raw ID from `entities[0]` is Detail-level and will never match a rendered D3 node
- **Visibility predicate returns false for all entities**: `useVisibleEntityIds` returning empty set — verify graph has completed its first render cycle before the hook is consulted
- **Traversal returns shallow (root-side) ancestor**: `pickFirstResolvable` not iterating deepest-first; verify BFS iteration order in `ancestry.ts`
- **Sidebar shows only `LiveLoggingSystem` with no per-tick differentiation**: ring/sidebar decoupling enhancement (show original bucket entity in sidebar while ring anchors to resolved ancestor) is not yet implemented

attributes.name: Unified Viewer Keyboard Shortcuts
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Manages global keyboard shortcuts for the unified viewer. The primary responsibility is the Esc key handler, which clears the full 5-field viewer selection state atomically and enforces the Phase 45 contract that Esc is a no-op when no selection is already active.

## Architecture
- **Hook file**: `integrations/unified-viewer/src/hooks/useKeyboardShortcuts.ts`
- **Esc handler guard**: evaluates all 5 selection fields before any mutation; fires only if at least one is non-null/non-empty:
  - `selectedNodeId` — graph node selection
  - `selectedSessionId` — session selection
  - `selectedEdgeId` — edge selection
  - `lslSessionFilter` — LSL session filter
  - `lslFilterEntityIds` — LSL entity ID filter set
- **Atomic clear**: all 5 fields cleared in a single `setState` call when the guard passes
- **Phase 45 Esc contract**: if all 5 fields are already cleared, Esc dispatches no state update (no-op); this is distinct from the Phase 45 render-effect dependency rule in `D3GraphCanvas.tsx`
- **Known regression pattern (CR-03)**: a refactor reduced the guard to check only `selectedNodeId !== null`, breaking sidebar-only mode — a mode where `selectedNodeId` is `null` but `lslSessionFilter`/`lslFilterEntityIds` remain populated; the 5-field guard is the correct and required implementation; any deviation from it must be treated as a regression
- **Test structure** (21 vitest tests total):
  - Test 13: genuine no-selection case — all 5 fields cleared; verifies no-op is not triggered
  - Test 15: sidebar-only mode — `lslSessionFilter`/`lslFilterEntityIds` populated but `selectedNodeId` null; verifies these fields alone trigger a clear

## Key Files
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/hooks/useKeyboardShortcuts.ts` — Esc guard; 5-field check; atomic clear; Phase 45 no-op contract
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/hooks/useKeyboardShortcuts.test.tsx` — 21-test vitest suite; Test 13 (no-op case); Test 15 (sidebar-only LSL/session fields case)
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/store/viewer-store.ts` — source of truth for all 5 selection fields

## Usage
Registered at the unified viewer top level and intercepts `keydown` events globally within the viewer. On Esc, the hook reads current state from `viewer-store.ts`, evaluates the 5-field guard, and if any field is set clears all 5 atomically. The cleared state propagates to `D3GraphCanvas` (removes ring/trace), `SidePanel` (unmounts), and `LslTimelineStrip` (removes tick highlight). No-op enforcement prevents spurious re-renders when Esc is pressed in an already-cleared state.

## Troubleshooting
- **Esc no-ops in sidebar-only mode (selectedNodeId is null but filters remain set)**: the 5-field guard was narrowed to check only `selectedNodeId !== null` — this is the CR-03 regression pattern; verify the guard evaluates all 5 fields, restore the full check if any field was removed
- **Esc clears only `selectedNodeId` and leaves LSL/session fields set**: guard was not widened — verify the hook checks all 5 fields, not just `selectedNodeId !== null`; this exact pattern indicates the CR-03 regression is present
- **Esc fires a state update in an already-cleared state**: guard is not evaluating correctly or a field is unexpectedly non-null; verify all 5 store fields are truly cleared before the guard runs
- **Test 13 failing**: genuine no-selection fixture has a field unexpectedly set — verify all 5 fields are cleared in the test fixture
- **Test 15 failing**: sidebar-only mode not recognized as requiring a clear; verify the guard detects non-empty `lslSessionFilter`/`lslFilterEntityIds` even when `selectedNodeId` is null
- **Type errors after adding a new selection field to viewer-store**: the 5-field guard and atomic clear in `useKeyboardShortcuts.ts` must be updated in lockstep with new store fields

The cleared state propagates to `D3GraphCanvas` (removes ring/trace), `SidePanel` (unmounts), and `LslTimelineStrip` (removes tick highlight). No-op enforcement prevents spurious re-renders when Esc is pressed in an already-cleared state.

## Troubleshooting
- **Esc no-ops in sidebar-only mode (selectedNodeId is null but filters remain set)**: the 5-field guard was narrowed to check only `selectedNodeId !== null` — this is the CR-03 regression pattern; verify the guard evaluates all 5 fields, restore the full check if any field was removed
- **Esc clears only `selectedNodeId` and leaves LSL/session fields set**: guard was not widened — verify the hook checks all 5 fields, not just `selectedNodeId !== null`; this exact pattern indicates the CR-03 regression is present
- **Esc fires a state update in an already-cleared state**: guard is not evaluating correctly or a field is unexpectedly non-null; verify all 5 store fields are truly cleared before the guard runs
- **Test 13 failing**: genuine no-selection fixture has a field unexpectedly set — verify all 5 fields are cleared in the test fixture
- **Test 15 failing**: sidebar-only mode not recognized as requiring a clear; verify the guard detects non-empty `lslSessionFilter`/`lslFilterEntityIds` even when `selectedNodeId` is null
- **Type errors after adding a new selection field to viewer-store**: the 5-field guard and atomic clear in `useKeyboardShortcuts.ts` must be updated in lockstep with new store fields

## Purpose
Implements the token-usage reconciliation layer that closes measurement gaps identified in Phase 82. Covers proxy-side hardening, reconcile-matcher primitives, reconcile-mode dispatch from `captureForegroundTokens`, span-close invocation, and three verified gap-closure bug fixes (CR-01, CR-02, CR-03). All 9 plans (83-01 through 83-09) are merged to `main`; the phase is fully closed.

## Architecture
**Wave structure (all plans CLOSED):**
- **Wave 1** (parallel): Proxy-side hardening, schema/dedup/routing
- **Wave 2** (parallel): 83-02 (proxy prerequisites, build/kickstart deploy) · 83-04 (reconcile-mode dispatch, D-01/D-02/D-04); 83-04 merge gated on 83-02 completing first
- **Wave 3 / gap-closure** (83-08): Queued until Wave 2 complete; scope driven by independent verification audit in `83-VERIFICATION.md`; no infrastructure rebuild required
- **Wave 4 / final gap-closure** (83-09): Generated after `VERIFICATION.md` was finalized; targeted CR-01, CR-02, CR-03; 8 secondary warnings explicitly deferred as follow-ons

**Three gap-closure CRs fixed by 83-09:**
- **CR-01 (fuzzy matcher scoping)**: Pre-loop wire snapshot guards against fallback-inserted rows and double consumption
- **CR-02 (copilot provenance stamping)**: Proxy-side `user_hash` fix applied at the source in `rapid-llm-proxy`
- **CR-03 (regression lock test)**: Regression test locking the corrected behavior

**Surface classification (3 categories):**
- **Proxy-side**: `rapid-llm-proxy` hardened with crash guards, unified task-ID sanitization, copilot `user_hash` provenance stamping
- **Reconcile-matcher**: fuzzy matcher scoped with pre-loop wire snapshot; fallback-row insertion and double-consumption guards
- **Reconcile-mode dispatch**: `captureForegroundTokens` dispatches reconcile mode at span-close

**83-09 commit breakdown:** 7 total — 5 in `coding` worktree (`fuzzy-scoping` fix, CR-01 tests, CR-02 contract lock, SUMMARY, self-check); 2 in `rapid-llm-proxy` main (CR-02 copilot feature and test).

**Deployment:** No dist/docker rebuild required for gap-closure; daemon restart was sufficient.

## Key Files
- `83-VERIFICATION.md` — independent audit artifact; drove scope of gap-closure plans 83-08 and 83-09
- `.planning/phases/83-token-reconciliation/83-09-PLAN.md` — final gap-closure plan; targets CR-01/CR-02/CR-03
- `rapid-llm-proxy/` — receives CR-02 copilot provenance fix and test; committed as 2 of 83-09's 7 commits

## Usage
Phase 83 is a closed implementation phase. Its outputs — reconcile-matcher, proxy hardening, and reconcile-mode dispatch — are production infrastructure consumed by all downstream phases (84+). Gap-closure plans 83-08 and 83-09 were executed via `gsd-execute-phase` with `--gaps-only`, which gates dispatch to plans carrying `gap_closure: true` in frontmatter.

## Troubleshooting
- Verify all reconciliation and envelope suites are green via `npm test` in both `coding` and `rapid-llm-proxy` repos before declaring closure.
- If fuzzy matcher produces double-counted tokens, confirm the pre-loop wire snapshot guard (CR-01) is present and executes before any fallback row insertion.
- If copilot turn provenance is missing from reconciled output, check the proxy-side `user_hash` injection (CR-02) in `rapid-llm-proxy` — the fix lives at the proxy write site, not in the matcher.
- If daemon fails to pick up changes, a restart (no rebuild) is sufficient — no dist or Docker layer changes are required for gap-closure deploys.

attributes.name: VKB Graph Viewer — Ontology Bleed and Entity Integrity
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Provides theme-aware color resolution for system-health-dashboard UI components across both light and dark themes. Operates at two complementary layers: CSS utility overrides for standard HTML elements, and a programmatic JS palette for SVG elements that cannot natively resolve CSS variables. Prevents dark-on-dark rendering artifacts (invisible headings, bright status banners, white SVG fills) when dark mode is active.

## Architecture
**Layer 1 — CSS/Tailwind:**
- `src/index.css`: defines semantic CSS custom properties; a `.dark`-scoped override block remaps ~280 hardcoded status utility classes (backgrounds, text, borders, fills) to the dark palette; explicit bridge rules cover `text-gray-700/800/900` heading classes automatically. Specificity-based targeting — no `!important`; light-mode styles untouched.
- `tailwind.config.ts`: registers semantic status tokens (`status-success-subtle`, `status-warning-subtle`, `status-error-subtle`, etc.) as first-class Tailwind utilities consumed by health status components.

**Layer 2 — Programmatic JS palette:**
- `src/lib/colors.ts`: exports light and dark color palettes plus the `useWorkflowColors()` React hook. The hook observes the `.dark` class on `<html>` and returns resolved concrete hex/rgb values. **Required for all SVG elements** — SVG `fill=` and `stroke=` attributes cannot resolve `CSS var()` references at render time; this is a confirmed browser constraint, not a limitation to be worked around differently.
- `src/components/workflow/constants.ts`: workflow-specific color constants; theme-sensitive values should use `useWorkflowColors()` rather than raw constant references.

**Component migration status (complete):**
- `multi-agent-graph.tsx`: migrated to central palette; hardcoded `fill="white"` legend leak fixed.
- `health-status-card.tsx`, `system-health-dashboard.tsx`: migrated to semantic tokens.
- `ukb-workflow-graph.tsx`: deleted (3,470-line dead component; was never imported anywhere).

## Key Files
- `src/lib/colors.ts` — central programmatic palette + `useWorkflowColors()` hook; authoritative source for all SVG color consumers
- `src/index.css` — CSS custom properties; `.dark` override block; heading bridge rules
- `tailwind.config.ts` — semantic status token registration
- `src/components/workflow/constants.ts` — workflow color constants (non-SVG fallback values)
- `src/components/workflow/multi-agent-graph.tsx` — canonical reference implementation for SVG components using `useWorkflowColors()`
- `src/components/health-status-card.tsx` — semantic token consumer
- `src/components/system-health-dashboard.tsx` — semantic token consumer

## Usage
- **New SVG components** needing theme-responsive fills/strokes: import and call `useWorkflowColors()` from `src/lib/colors.ts`; never reference `var(--color-*)` in SVG attributes.
- **New HTML/Tailwind components**: use `status-success-subtle`, `status-warning-subtle`, `status-error-subtle` semantic tokens from `tailwind.config.ts`.
- **Heading text**: `text-gray-700/800/900` classes auto-adapt via the `.dark` bridge in `src/index.css`; no manual `dark:` variant needed on standard headings.

## Troubleshooting
- **SVG fill ignores theme toggle**: `fill=` cannot resolve `var()` — switch to `useWorkflowColors()` for any SVG color attribute; this is the only correct fix.
- **Dark-mode artifact (white/bright element)**: component uses hardcoded hex or raw Tailwind utilities bypassing the `.dark` override block; migrate to semantic tokens or add explicit `dark:` variants.
- **Status banner wrong color**: verify the component references `status-success-subtle` / `status-warning-subtle` / `status-error-subtle` tokens, not hardcoded utility classes.
- **Heading invisible in dark mode**: confirm `text-gray-700/800/900` is present — the `.dark` bridge handles inversion automatically; no additional code required.
- **Amber "Degraded" / green "OK" / gray headings**: all confirmed rendering correctly in both themes as of latest migration; regressions indicate a component bypassing the token system.

attributes.name: VKB Ontology — Two-Tier Architecture
attributes.description:
## Purpose
A planned redesign of the VKB knowledge model that separates the current flat ontology into two tiers: a generic upper ontology reusable across knowledge bases, and a project-scoped lower ontology isolating domain-specific terminology. The redesign enables structural pattern reuse and coherent topic-area grouping in the VKB viewer, and establishes the principled ontology boundaries required to resolve active cross-domain bleed issues.

## Architecture

**Upper ontology (generic, cross-KB reusable):**
- Entity types: `component`, `sub-component`, `detail`, `diagnosis`, `interface`
- Applicable to any knowledge base; not scoped to a single project
- Provides the structural skeleton to which lower-ontology terms attach

**Lower ontology (project/domain-specific):**
- Scoped to the `coding` project
- Terminology: `LSL`, `constraints` (and other project-specific terms to be confirmed from planning document)
- Organized by topic area for coherent grouping in the unified VKB viewer

**Design motivation:**
- The current flat model conflates generic structural patterns with domain-specific terms, making structural reuse across knowledge bases impossible and topic grouping incoherent in the viewer
- Establishes a principled ontology boundary that determines the correct resolution for all active VKB cross-domain bleed issues (Evidence/Pattern filter controls, legend contamination, Observation/Digest entity bleed) — individual patches should not be applied before the tier boundaries are established

## Key Files
- `2026-06-14-ontology-rework-lower-ontology-and-project-grouping.md` — planning document; canonical reference for upper/lower tier definitions, lower-ontology term list, and topic-area grouping requirements

## Usage
Not yet implemented; currently in the planning phase. Once the tier boundaries are established, the redesign will drive: updates to entity types in the knowledge graph, revised filter controls in the VKB viewer, a corrected legend (actual edge types: `parent_child`, `related_to`, `has_insight`, `captured_by`), and restructured topic-area grouping in the unified viewer. All active cross-domain bleed issues tracked in "VKB Graph Viewer — Ontology Bleed and Entity Integrity" are gated on this design decision.

## Troubleshooting
- **Unclear whether an entity type belongs in upper or lower ontology**: upper = generic programming concepts applicable to any codebase; lower = `coding`-project-specific terms scoped to VKB; consult `2026-06-14-ontology-rework-lower-ontology-and-project-grouping.md` for the canonical term lists
- **Cross-domain bleed issues being patched individually**: individual fixes (filter logic, legend text, entity purges) should not be applied before the ontology tier boundaries are finalized; the tier boundaries determine the correct fix for each bleed category
- **Topic-area grouping incoherent in viewer after implementation**: lower-ontology terms must be organized by topic area in the unified viewer; verify the viewer's grouping logic consults the lower-ontology topic-area mapping established in the planning document

attributes.name: Concurrent Agent Session Management — Phantom Commits and Inter-Session Communic
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Defines the standard integration workflow for the coding project: no pull requests; all work is merged directly to `main` locally and pushed.

## Architecture
- Work on a feature/fix branch, then fast-forward or merge to `main` locally.
- Push `main` directly to `origin`.
- Delete merged branches both locally (`git branch -d`) and remotely (`git push origin --delete`).

## Key Files
- `memory/feedback_coding_no_pr_merge_direct.md` — persisted workflow preference
- `memory/MEMORY.md` — project-level memory index referencing this preference

## Usage
Applied for every branch integration. No GitHub/GitLab PR is opened. Reviewer approval gates do not exist in this workflow.

## Troubleshooting
- If `origin/main` has advanced before local merge, run `git pull --rebase origin main` before merging the feature branch to avoid divergence.
- After pushing, confirm remote branches are deleted to keep `origin` clean.

attributes.name: Knowledge Graph Ancestry — capturedBy BFS Traversal
attributes.description:
## Purpose
`ancestry.ts` implements BFS traversal for resolving ancestors and descendants within the knowledge graph. A known pending defect causes incorrect traversal results for `capturedBy` relationships due to an incorrect edge direction assumption in the BFS logic.

## Architecture
- **BFS traversal**: `ancestry.ts` walks graph edges in a specified direction (inbound/outbound) to resolve lineage chains; the `capturedBy` edge direction is the identified failure point
- **Raw export as ground truth**: `general.json` is the authoritative source for inspecting raw edge structures, including `capture`-type relations; `jq` is the standard tool for counting and sampling these edges
- **Edge representation**: `capture`-type relations appear in the export with inspectable structure (relation type, source, target, attributes); sampling the first several matching edges is the recommended baseline approach before modifying traversal logic
- **Schema caution**: the `.Class` field does not exist in the KG export; always sample a raw record to confirm actual field names before writing filter expressions
- **VKB surface**: `captured_by` is one of the five actual edge types rendered in the VKB graph viewer (`parent_child`, `related_to`, `has_insight`, `capturedBy`, `contains`); the traversal bug may affect VKB-level query correctness

## Key Files
- `ancestry.ts` — BFS traversal implementation; `capturedBy` edge direction is a confirmed pending fix; exact path to be confirmed from project source layout
- `.data/exports/knowledge-export/general.json` — raw edge export; query with `jq` to count and sample `capture`-type relations before applying the direction fix

## Usage
`ancestry.ts` is invoked wherever the knowledge graph must resolve the lineage of a node. The pending `capturedBy` direction fix must be preceded by a `jq`-based audit of `general.json` to confirm the actual source/target orientation of `capture` edges, ensuring the fix corrects to the canonical direction rather than inverting to a different wrong direction.

## Troubleshooting
- **`capturedBy` traversal returns wrong ancestors or descendants**: BFS edge direction for `capturedBy` in `ancestry.ts` is a confirmed pending defect; verify canonical edge orientation by querying `general.json` with `jq` (adapt field names from a sampled raw record — `.Class` does not exist in the schema) before applying the fix
- **Uncertain which field name the export uses for relation type**: sample the first raw edge object (`jq '.[<edge-collection-key>][0]'`) to inspect all top-level keys before writing filter expressions
- **`capturedBy` fix interacts with VKB viewer rendering**: `captured_by` is a rendered edge type in the VKB viewer; after fixing traversal direction, verify that viewer-level edge display and legend entries still reflect correct directionality

attributes.name: Knowledge Graph Semantic Edges — Online Ingest Pipeline
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Observation nodes produced by the online ingest pipeline are persisted with only a single outgoing relation (`capturedBy → LiveLoggingSystem`). Semantic-content edges (`discusses`, `mentions`, `references`) that should link each Observation to the specific Insights and Components it references are not written. This gap causes all graph traversal from Observation nodes to terminate at `LiveLoggingSystem`, preventing meaningful ancestry resolution and knowledge graph attribution.

## Architecture
- **Affected data scope**: all Observation nodes produced by Pipeline 1 (online ingest); each carries exactly one outgoing relation: `capturedBy → LiveLoggingSystem`; no semantic-content edges are present on any node
- **Missing edge types**: `discusses`, `mentions`, `references` — semantic-content relations that should link each Observation to relevant Insights and Components
- **Three implicated code locations**:
  - **`persistence-agent.ts`** (lines 928–944) — writes relations per Observation; currently writes only `capturedBy`; the primary target for adding semantic-content edge writes
  - **`coordinator.ts`** — suspected of not classifying Observations against the Insight/Component graph before or during persistence; classification is a prerequisite for resolving correct edge targets
  - **`insight-generation-agent.ts`** — suspected of not creating back-edges from generated Insights to their source Observations; back-edges are required for bidirectional traversal
- **Downstream symptom**: BFS ancestor traversal in the viewer returns `LiveLoggingSystem` for every Observation because no alternate path exists; the traversal logic is correct — the data is deficient
- **Ingest path context**: online ingest flows `ObservationConsolidator.js` → VKB HTTP PUT with `source: 'online'`; the gap is in what relations are written during this path, not in the transport mechanism

## Key Files
- `integrations/mcp-server-semantic-analysis/src/persistence-agent.ts` — lines 928–944; primary fix target; needs to write `discusses`/`mentions`/`references` in addition to `capturedBy`
- `integrations/mcp-server-semantic-analysis/src/coordinator.ts` — Observation classification logic; must classify against Insight/Component graph to produce valid edge targets before persistence
- `integrations/mcp-server-semantic-analysis/src/agents/insight-generation-agent.ts` — Insight generation; needs back-edge writes from each generated Insight to its source Observation(s)
- `~/Agentic/coding/src/live-logging/ObservationConsolidator.js` — Pipeline 1 orchestrator; VKB HTTP PUT entry point
- `general.json` (e.g. `.data/exports/knowledge-export/general.json`) — raw graph export; use `jq` to confirm absence of `discusses`/`mentions`/`references` edges with Observation sources

## Usage
This is an open defect in the online ingest pipeline. All downstream consumers — viewer graph traversal, VKB queries, timeline-to-entity attribution — receive degraded results until semantic-content edges are added. Recommended fix sequence: (1) audit `coordinator.ts` to understand or implement Observation classification against the Insight/Component graph; (2) pass resolved target IDs into `persistence-agent.ts` for writing semantic-content edges; (3) add back-edge writes in `insight-generation-agent.ts`. Do not modify traversal logic in `ancestry.ts` or viewer components to work around this defect — the fix must be applied upstream.

## Troubleshooting
- **Confirming edge absence**: query `general.json` with `jq` — e.g. `jq '[.edges[] | select(.relation == "discusses" or .relation == "mentions" or .relation == "references")] | length'`; expected result is `0` until the fix is applied
- **Graph traversal always returns `LiveLoggingSystem` for Observation nodes**: confirmed data defect; do not fix by adjusting BFS direction or traversal logic — add the missing edges upstream
- **Identifying correct edge targets**: `coordinator.ts` classification determines which Insight/Component IDs are semantically linked to a given Observation; audit this logic first to ensure targets are well-defined before writing edges in `persistence-agent.ts`
- **Back-edge direction for `insight-generation-agent.ts`**: edges should point Insight → source Observation(s); verify directionality before adding to avoid inverting the semantic relationship
- **Fix interacts with VKB viewer rendering**: after adding semantic-content edges, verify that the VKB graph viewer's filter and legend logic handles the new edge types correctly; `discusses`/`mentions`/`references` are not currently in the viewer's declared legend

attributes.name: Phase Code Review Workflow
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Per-file, language-specific code quality review executed after all phase execution waves complete. Chains `gsd-code-reviewer` analysis with optional automated fix application via `gsd-code-fixer`. Produces a severity-classified `{phase}-REVIEW.md` that gates downstream phase progression at step 1 of the Phase Close-Out Protocol.

## Architecture
**Invocation**: `/gsd-code-review [phase] [--depth <standard|deep>] [--files <list>] [--fix] [--all]`

**Two mutually exclusive routing modes:**
- **Fast-dispatch**: `{phase}-REVIEW.md` already exists on disk with `issues_found` status → `gsd-code-fixer` invoked immediately; `gsd-code-reviewer` skipped entirely.
- **Standard-dispatch**: `{phase}-REVIEW.md` absent or clean → `gsd-code-reviewer` runs first (~5–15 min at standard depth), then optionally chains `gsd-code-fixer` when `--fix` is passed.

**Typical severity distribution and fix pattern** (observed across phase closures): findings classified into critical / warning / info tiers; each finding or tightly-coupled group of findings is resolved in its own atomic commit rather than one bulk commit; pre-commit verification specifically re-targets the highest-risk findings (e.g. a dropped metadata field, an incorrect unit conversion) before merge.

**Closure requires live verification, not just static fix**: after fixes are committed, affected services are redeployed and the full regression suite (unit + e2e) is re-run; for security-class findings (e.g. path traversal, unauthorized process control), live rejection proofs are captured to confirm the exploit path is actually blocked end-to-end, not just patched in code.

## Key Files
- `{phase}-REVIEW.md` — severity-classified findings artifact, gates Phase Close-Out step 1
- `{phase}-REVIEW-FIX.md` — remediation record documenting each commit, fix scope, and rationale per finding

## Usage
Run automatically (or manually invoked) once all execution waves of a phase are complete, before the Phase Close-Out Protocol can advance the state machine to the next phase.

## Troubleshooting
- If `{phase}-REVIEW.md` shows `issues_found` on a later `/gsd-code-review` invocation, it fast-dispatches straight to `gsd-code-fixer` — confirm this is intended before re-running the full reviewer.
- If phase close-out stalls at step 1, check for unresolved critical findings or a missing `{phase}-REVIEW-FIX.md`.
- Security-class findings should not be marked resolved on static review alone — require a live rejection proof (reproduced exploit attempt blocked) plus a passing full regression suite before sign-off.

attributes.name: LLS Suppression — Bucket Resolution Strategy
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Prevents `LiveLoggingSystem` (LLS) from dominating bucket-entity resolution in the unified viewer. The primary root cause — an inverted `capturedBy` edge direction in the BFS traversal code in `ancestry.ts` — is fixed, eliminating incorrect LLS fallback in the majority of non-empty buckets. Option B2 suppression (`noiseAncestors` set) provides defense for residual edge cases driven by the data-level defect (missing semantic-content edges on Observation nodes).

## Architecture
- **Root cause (BFS traversal bug — fixed)**: the BFS walk in `ancestry.ts` was traversing `capturedBy` edges in the inverted direction; correcting the walk direction resolves the primary misresolution (was causing ~49/75 non-empty buckets to fall back to LLS)
- **Residual data defect (open)**: all Observation nodes carry only `capturedBy → LiveLoggingSystem`; semantic-content edges (`discusses`, `mentions`, `references`) are absent; when the data defect affects a bucket, even the corrected BFS terminates at LLS and Option B2 suppression applies
- **Strategy — Option B2**: post-BFS filter removes entries matching `noiseAncestors` when at least one non-noise resolution also exists; does **not** suppress LLS when it is the sole result
- **`noiseAncestors` set**: code-defined set of entity names/IDs treated as noise; supports adding future noise-tier ancestors without changing suppression logic; defined in the ancestry resolution layer, not as runtime config
- **S1 behavior**: when the post-filter result set is empty, suppression is lifted and LLS is preserved as the focal entity — prevents blank UI state in all-Observation buckets
- **S2 behavior**: when suppression collapses a multi-Digest bucket to exactly one Insight, the viewer auto-drills directly to that Insight (bypasses `BucketCardList`)
- **Q3 (bidirectionality)**: suppression also applies during `useNodeToBucketsIndex` reverse index construction — clicking the LLS graph node does not illuminate all ticks when suppression is active

## Key Files
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/graph/ancestry.ts` — BFS traversal (corrected `capturedBy` edge direction); Option B2 post-BFS filter; `noiseAncestors` set definition
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/store/viewer-store.ts` — `useNodeToBucketsIndex` reverse index; bidirectional suppression applied during index construction
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/panels/coding/LslTimelineStrip.tsx` — `onTickClick` invokes resolution with suppression active; S2 auto-drill dispatch
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/panels/SidePanel.tsx` — S1 fallback display path; `isSingleFocalMode` interacts with suppressed result sets
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/graph/ancestry.test.ts` — coverage for BFS direction, suppression logic, and `useNodeToBucketsIndex` mapping

## Usage
Suppression activates automatically during bucket-entity resolution on every tick click in `onTickClick`. No user-facing toggle. The corrected BFS walk direction handles the primary resolution case; Option B2 suppression handles residual fallback-to-LLS cases caused by the data-level defect. To add entities to the suppression set, update `noiseAncestors` in `ancestry.ts`. The ingest-side fix (adding semantic-content edges) remains open — see Knowledge Graph Semantic Edges insight.

## Troubleshooting
- **LLS still dominates most buckets despite fix being merged**: verify `ancestry.ts` contains the corrected `capturedBy` walk direction — if the direction was re-inverted, 49/75+ non-empty buckets will fall back to LLS
- **LLS appears when other ancestors are present (BFS direction is correct)**: data-level defect case (missing semantic-content edges); verify `noiseAncestors` filter executes after full BFS traversal with at least one non-noise result present
- **LLS absent when it is the sole ancestor**: S1 fallback guard missing — suppression must be lifted when the filtered result set is empty
- **Clicking LLS graph node illuminates all ticks**: Q3 bidirectionality not applied to `useNodeToBucketsIndex` construction; verify index build applies the same noise filter as forward resolution
- **Auto-drill fires on buckets with multiple Insights**: S2 single-Insight check too broad — exactly one resolved Insight required before drilling
- **Blank/empty panel on all-Observation buckets**: S1 zero-result restoration path absent

attributes.name: Shared LLM Adapter Library Extraction
attributes.description:
## Purpose
LLM proxy phase work is split across two independent git repositories. Closing any proxy-related phase requires coordinated commits and pushes to both: the `coding` repo (planning artifacts) and `_work/rapid-llm-proxy` (implementation). Neither push is meaningful in isolation — planning artifacts without implementation, or implementation without planning records, are both incomplete phase states.

## Architecture
- **`coding` repo**: holds `.planning/phases/`, `.planning/research/`, `STATE.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, `SUMMARY.md`, and all GSD phase planning artifacts; remote: `github.com/fwornle/coding.git`; **SSH transport only** (HTTPS will fail); direct commits and pushes to `main`
- **`_work/rapid-llm-proxy` repo**: fully separate git repository holding all proxy implementation files; remote: internal GHE instance; **HTTPS transport only** (SSH is not configured and will fail); independent commit history
- Both pushes must succeed and be explicitly confirmed before phase close-out is considered complete
- No cross-repo references or submodule links — repos are coordinated only by convention (phase IDs align across planning artifacts and implementation commits)

## Key Files
- `.planning/phases/` — planning artifacts in the `coding` repo
- `_work/rapid-llm-proxy/` — proxy implementation; separate git root
- `STATE.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, `SUMMARY.md` — phase tracking files in the `coding` repo

## Usage
- Required at every proxy-related phase close-out
- Operator must explicitly confirm both pushes succeeded before proceeding with the Phase Close-Out Protocol
- Transport protocol selection (SSH vs HTTPS) is repo-specific — the protocols are not interchangeable

## Troubleshooting
- **SSH failure on `rapid-llm-proxy`**: This repo requires HTTPS; update the remote URL to HTTPS format before retrying
- **HTTPS failure on `coding` repo**: This repo requires SSH; update the remote URL to SSH format before retrying
- **One push succeeds, one fails**: Phase close-out is incomplete — do not proceed until both repos are confirmed pushed
- **Diverged histories**: Each repo maintains an independent commit history; do not attempt to merge or cross-reference commits between repos

attributes.name: Live Backfill Pre-flight Procedure and Wave-Analysis Routing
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Constructs, enriches, and normalizes route-attribution records for Claude, Copilot, and OpenCode agents. Trace readers materialize per-call routing metadata into typed `RouteEvent` objects; a heuristic layer and goal-sentence extractor enrich those objects for downstream attribution pipeline consumption without invoking any LLM.

## Architecture
**Two cooperating layers:**

**Trace reader layer** — builds typed `RouteEvent` records from per-provider call context:
- `buildClaudeRouteTrace` — builds a typed route-trace record from Claude agent call context
- `buildCopilotRouteTrace` — builds a route-trace from Copilot call context; implements **dual-field tolerance**: accepts either `toolName` or `name` as the tool identifier, matching fixture variants where both field names appear in real call data
- **OpenCode SQLite reader** — read-only reader extracting route trace data from the SQLite-backed OpenCode call log; shares existing WAL/uid gates via additive export

**Heuristic enrichment layer** — enriches `RouteEvent` objects with goal-sentence extraction and attribution heuristics for downstream pipeline consumption; operates without any LLM invocation

## Key Files
- Route-trace reader modules — contain `buildClaudeRouteTrace` and `buildCopilotRouteTrace`
- OpenCode SQLite reader module — WAL/uid-gated, read-only

## Usage
- Consumed by the downstream attribution pipeline
- All enrichment is heuristic and LLM-free; suitable for high-throughput or offline processing
- OpenCode reader is strictly read-only and shares existing WAL/uid gates

## Troubleshooting
- If Copilot route traces are missing tool identifiers, verify the dual-field tolerance logic is reading both `toolName` and `name` fields from call context
- If OpenCode traces are incomplete or missing, check WAL/uid gate status on the SQLite reader
- Route attribution failures should be diagnosed at the trace reader layer first before investigating heuristic enrichment
- Goal-sentence extraction failures are contained within the heuristic layer and do not block `RouteEvent` materialization

- **OpenCode SQLite reader** — read-only reader extracting route trace data from the SQLite-backed OpenCode call log; shares existing WAL/uid gates via additive export

**Heuristic enrichment layer** — enriches `RouteEvent` objects with goal-sentence extraction and attribution heuristics for downstream pipeline consumption; operates without any LLM invocation

## Key Files
- Route-trace reader modules — contain `buildClaudeRouteTrace` and `buildCopilotRouteTrace`
- OpenCode SQLite reader module — WAL/uid-gated, read-only

## Usage
- Consumed by the downstream attribution pipeline
- All enrichment is heuristic and LLM-free; suitable for high-throughput or offline processing
- OpenCode reader is strictly read-only and shares existing WAL/uid gates

## Troubleshooting
- If Copilot route traces are missing tool identifiers, verify the dual-field tolerance logic is reading both `toolName` and `name` fields from call context
- If OpenCode traces are incomplete or missing, check WAL/uid gate status on the SQLite reader

attributes.description:
## Purpose
Controls which graph entities are admitted into the mention-candidate pool used during wave-analysis mention-classification. Candidates are assembled by `loadMentionCandidates` (filtering on `ontologyClass`) and resolved through `findByOntologyClass`, which applies OR-gate semantics. A widespread `ontologyClass` tagging error contaminates the pool and produces false mention edges.

## Architecture

**Candidate pool assembly (`loadMentionCandidates`):**
- Selects entities using `ontologyClass` as the filter key — not `entityType`
- Current pool: 802 nodes; intended to contain L1/L2/L3 records only
- Actual contamination: 74 Insights tagged `ontologyClass='Detail'` (instead of `'Insight'`), plus 16 Processes, 15 Observations, and 11 Containers with incorrect class tags — all admitted alongside legitimate L1/L2/L3 entries

**`findByOntologyClass` OR-gate semantics:**
- Resolves via `entityType OR ontologyClass` match — not strict class-only filtering
- `isActive` filter: entities without a `validUntil` timestamp unconditionally pass; all 100 current Insight entities lack `validUntil`, so all are always reachable
- Any analysis claiming the bridge reaches fewer than 100 Insights is a misreading of this OR-gate filter

**False-edge impact from contamination:**
- Contaminated pool generates self-referential `Insight→Insight` mention edges and false `Insight→Process` edges
- Total false-edge noise: ~1.2% of all edges — considered acceptable; `ontologyClass` correction deprioritized
- When running coverage analysis, filter to L1/L2/L3 records only to exclude self-referential noise from metrics

**Coverage metric:**
- Tracks Insights with zero mention-candidate coverage ("uncovered Insights")
- Pre-bridge baseline: 37 uncovered Insights; post-bridge execution: 25 uncovered — improvement confirmed from live pipeline changes (bridge execution + writer-path emission activation)

## Key Files
- `src/live-logging/ObservationConsolidator.js` — contains `loadMentionCandidates` (filters by `ontologyClass`); calls `findByOntologyClass`; Insight synthesis entry point
- `58-HUMAN-UAT.md` — SC#1 bridge scope verification and coverage improvement tracking

## Usage
The 802-node candidate pool is assembled at wave-analysis runtime. Coverage metrics (uncovered Insight count) verify that bridge execution and writer-path emission activation are taking effect. Filter coverage analysis to L1/L2/L3 records only to avoid inflating uncovered-Insight counts with self-referential noise. The `ontologyClass` data <USER_ID_REDACTED> fix (retagging 74 Insights from `'Detail'` to `'Insight'`) is tracked but deprioritized.

## Troubleshooting
- **Insights appearing in their own candidate pool**: 74 Insights carry `ontologyClass='Detail'`; they enter the pool and match against themselves; mitigate by filtering coverage analysis to L1/L2/L3 records; permanent fix requires retagging those 74 entities to `ontologyClass='Insight'`
- **False `Insight→Insight` or `Insight→Process` mention edges in graph**: caused by `ontologyClass` mistagging; current impact ~1.2% of total edges; deprioritized pending further real-world impact assessment
- **Bridge appears to reach fewer than 100 Insights**: verify OR-gate semantics in `findByOntologyClass` (`entityType OR ontologyClass`); confirm all Insights lack `validUntil` (so all pass `isActive`); all 100 Insights are reachable — any lower count is a filter or analysis error
- **Coverage metrics not improving after bridge execution**: confirm writer-path emission was activated before the bridge run; expected post-bridge baseline is ~25 uncovered (down from 37)
- **`loadMentionCandidates` admitting unexpected entity types**: the filter operates on `ontologyClass`, not `entityType`; entities with wrong `ontologyClass` values are admitted regardless of their structural type

attributes.name: Knowledge Graph Orphan Metrics and Stats API Reliability
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Provides the authoritative source for orphan node counts and graph composition statistics in the VKB knowledge graph. The `/api/v1/stats` endpoint (served by `mcp-server-semantic-analysis`) is the ground-truth source; UI-displayed orphan counts are derived from this endpoint but are subject to scope-filtering effects that cause the two figures to diverge.

## Architecture
- **Authoritative stats endpoint**: `/api/v1/stats` — returns `orphanCount`, `orphanRatio`, and related graph composition metrics; route declarations live in `integrations/mcp-server-semantic-analysis/src/sse-server.ts`
- **Stats computation**: implemented in km-core dependency modules; aggregates node counts by type and computes orphan ratio over the full graph; locate the relevant logic via `grep orphanCount` in km-core source
- **Known divergence source — scope filtering**: the UI orphan count is computed after applying active layer/scope filters, which can suppress ~33% of nodes (e.g., 1262 → 848); orphans outside the current scope are excluded from the UI figure, producing a count lower than `/api/v1/stats.orphanCount`
- **Known counting bug — header metrics**: header-level Evidence and Patterns counts report 0 while their corresponding layer filters report non-zero node counts (e.g., 815 and 33); this is a distinct bug from orphan-count divergence and independently undermines metric confidence
- **Phase 59 ORPHAN-04 criterion**: orphanCount ≤ 30 AND orphanRatio ≤ 3% — must be verified against the raw `/api/v1/stats` response, not the UI display, to avoid false satisfaction from scope-filter suppression
- **Service topology** (probed ports for stats endpoint liveness):
  - Port `8090` — candidate host for `/api/v1/stats`; role confirmed via `curl` probe
  - Port `5173` — Vite dev server (frontend UI)
  - Port `3848` — secondary service endpoint; role to be confirmed
  - Port `3033` — health dashboard API

## Key Files
- `integrations/mcp-server-semantic-analysis/src/sse-server.ts` — API route definitions; contains orphan-count endpoint routes and is the primary entry point for understanding stats routing
- `km-core` dependency source — stats aggregation and orphan computation logic; find via `grep -r orphanCount` within km-core modules
- `.data/exports/knowledge-export/general.json` — full graph export; use `jq` to enumerate specific orphan nodes by ID/name for manual ORPHAN-04 verification

## Usage
To verify ORPHAN-04: `curl <host>:<port>/api/v1/stats` against the confirmed live port and check `orphanCount` ≤ 30 and `orphanRatio` ≤ 3%. Do not rely on the UI-displayed orphan count without first confirming no scope filter is active. To enumerate the specific orphans: cross-reference the `orphanCount` figure with individual node IDs in `general.json`. If the ORPHAN-04 criterion appears satisfied at 7 orphans, enumerate those 7 nodes by name before committing to full discuss/plan work — scope-filter suppression may be excluding additional orphans.

## Troubleshooting
- **UI orphan count diverges from `/api/v1/stats.orphanCount`**: an active layer or scope filter is narrowing the counted node set; disable all filters or query the raw endpoint directly for the unfiltered figure
- **Header Evidence/Patterns metrics show 0 despite non-zero layer filter counts**: known counting bug independent of orphan metrics; do not use header counts as a proxy for node existence — query layer-specific endpoints or `general.json` directly
- **Node count drops ~33% between full view and filtered view**: server-side scope filter is suppressing out-of-scope nodes; this lowers the UI-visible orphan count and can produce a false-passing ORPHAN-04 result
- **ORPHAN-04 appears satisfied in UI but confidence is low**: query `/api/v1/stats` directly and enumerate all orphan nodes by name/ID from `general.json` before accepting the criterion as met
- **Live port for `/api/v1/stats` is unknown**: probe ports `8090`, `5173`, `3848`, and `3033` in order with `curl <host>:<port>/api/v1/stats`; the live port is the one returning a valid JSON stats payload rather than a connection error or HTML response
