attributes.name: km-core Knowledge Graph Hydration — JSON Export Priority and Build Safety
attributes.description:
## Purpose
The `hydrate()` function in `lib/km-core/src/store/persistence.ts` controls whether the in-memory knowledge graph loads from LevelDB cache or the canonical JSON export. Without a patch, `hydrate()` defaults to LevelDB, which may be stale — causing catastrophic graph collapse. The patch is build-fragile: `npm run build` regenerates the compiled dist artifact and discards any manual patch to that file, requiring both the TypeScript source and the compiled artifact to be patched independently after every build.

## Architecture
- **Unpatched behavior**: prefers LevelDB cache; stale cache produces collapse (observed: ~1270 nodes/1594 edges → 924 nodes/3 edges)
- **Patched behavior**: prefers `.data/exports/knowledge-export/general.json` as the authoritative load source
- **Build fragility**: `npm run build` compiles `persistence.ts` → `dist/store/persistence.js`; any manual patch to the dist file is overwritten; the source patch survives the build but the dist patch does not
- **Two required patch targets simultaneously**:
  - `lib/km-core/src/store/persistence.ts` — TypeScript source
  - `lib/km-core/dist/store/persistence.js` — compiled artifact; must be re-patched after every `npm run build`
- **Recovery sequence**: (1) re-apply patch to both files, (2) wipe stale LevelDB, (3) rehydrate from `general.json`, (4) restart `obs-api` and VKB
- **Healthy post-recovery graph state**: 816 nodes / 1262 edges; edge type distribution: `contains: 849`, `related_to: 202`, `capturedBy: 112`, `has_insight: 67`, `parent-child: 11`
- **Open writer-side issue**: `ObservationConsolidator`/`ObservationWriter` still actively emit `Observation` and `Digest` entities to km-core post-architectural-removal; filter these from the JSON export before loading until the writer-side fix lands

## Key Files
- `lib/km-core/src/store/persistence.ts` — `hydrate()` source; patch to prefer JSON over LevelDB
- `lib/km-core/dist/store/persistence.js` — compiled artifact; must also be patched after every `npm run build`
- `.data/exports/knowledge-export/general.json` — canonical JSON export; authoritative rehydration source

## Usage
After every `npm run build` in the km-core workspace, verify that `dist/store/persistence.js` still contains the JSON-preference patch before restarting `obs-api` or VKB. The patch has not been absorbed into the build process — manual post-build verification and re-patching of the dist file is required on every build. All Insights should be tagged `source='auto'` after a clean rehydration to clear any false "Manual" badges.

## Troubleshooting
- **Graph collapses after a build (nodes/edges drop dramatically)**: `npm run build` overwrote the dist patch; re-apply to `lib/km-core/dist/store/persistence.js`, wipe LevelDB, rehydrate from `general.json`, restart `obs-api` and VKB
- **Source patched but graph still collapses**: patching `persistence.ts` alone is insufficient if the dist was compiled before the patch — always patch `dist/store/persistence.js` directly regardless of source state
- **After rehydration, spurious `Observation`/`Digest` entities appear**: `ObservationConsolidator`/`ObservationWriter` are actively emitting these (writer-side root cause unresolved); filter them from the JSON export before loading
- **`obs-api` or VKB still reflecting stale/collapsed graph after rehydration**: both services hold in-memory state; restart both after rehydration to pick up the recovered graph
- **`isProject` static ESM import failure in `mcp-servers:semantic-analysis` container**: open unresolved issue introduced during Phase 57; container fails on `isProject` import; no confirmed workaround

- **Open writer-side issue**: `ObservationConsolidator`/`ObservationWriter` still actively emit `Observation` and `Digest` entities to km-core post-architectural-removal; filter these from the JSON export before loading until the writer-side fix lands

## Key Files
- `lib/km-core/src/store/persistence.ts` — `hydrate()` source; patch to prefer JSON over LevelDB
- `lib/km-core/dist/store/persistence.js` — compiled artifact; must also be patched after every `npm run build`
- `.data/exports/knowledge-export/general.json` — canonical JSON export; authoritative rehydration source

## Usage
After every `npm run build` in the km-core workspace, verify that `dist/store/persistence.js` still contains the JSON-preference patch before restarting `obs-api` or VKB. The patch has not been absorbed into the build process — manual post-build verification and re-patching of the dist file is required on every build. All Insights should be tagged `source='auto'` after a clean rehydration to clear any false "Manual" badges.

## Troubleshooting
- **Graph collapses after a build (nodes/edges drop dramatically)**: `npm run build` overwrote the dist patch; re-apply to `lib/km-core/dist/store/persistence.js`, wipe LevelDB, rehydrate from `general.json`, restart `obs-api` and VKB
- **Source patched but graph still collapses**: patching `persistence.ts` alone is insufficient if the dist was compiled before the patch — always patch `dist/store/persistence.js` directly regardless of source state
- **After rehydration, spurious `Observation`/`Digest` entities appear**: `ObservationConsolidator`/`ObservationWriter` are actively emitting these (writer-side root cause unresolved); filter them from the JSON export before loading
- **`obs-api` or VKB still reflecting stale/collapsed graph after rehydration**: both services hold in-memory state; restart both after rehydration to pick up the recovered graph
- **`isProject` static ESM import failure in `mcp-servers:semantic-analysis` container**: open unresolved issue introduced during Phase 57; container fails on `isProject` import; no confirmed workaround

attributes.name: Lower-Ontology Project Tagging Infrastructure
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Prevents writer agents from incorrectly overwriting the `ontologyClass` field on root-level entities (e.g., `CollectiveKnowledge`) with non-root types such as `"Detail"`. Misclassification silently truncates ancestry traces in the unified viewer's filter panels, causing the Online filter to stop at the project level rather than reaching the correct root. A one-shot repair script corrects any existing misclassification idempotently.

## Architecture
Three cooperating components:

- **`HIERARCHY_ROOTS` registry** (`lib/km-core/`): canonical exported list of top-level ontology class names. Acts as the reference set that all agents and guards consult when evaluating whether an entity is a hierarchy root.
- **Writer-side hard-root guard** (`integrations/mcp-server-semantic-analysis`): intercepts incoming `ontologyClass` write operations; rejects any attempt to overwrite an entity whose current class appears in `HIERARCHY_ROOTS`. Activated at runtime via bind-mount — when Docker rebuilds are unavailable, the guard is injected via volume mount.
- **Idempotent repair script**: one-shot script that scans all entities, identifies any root-level entity with an incorrect `ontologyClass`, and resets it to the correct root class. Safe to re-run.

## Key Files
- `lib/km-core/` — contains `HIERARCHY_ROOTS` registry export
- `integrations/mcp-server-semantic-analysis/` — writer-side guard implementation
- Repair script — one-shot; location project-specific

## Usage
- Guard is always-on once the MCP server is running with the correct bind-mount; no per-write configuration required.
- `HIERARCHY_ROOTS` must be updated whenever a new root ontology class is introduced; failure to update it leaves new roots unprotected.
- Run the repair script after any bulk import or migration that predates the guard's activation.

## Troubleshooting
- **Online filter stops at project level instead of root**: A root entity has been misclassified; run the repair script to identify and fix it.
- **Guard not rejecting bad writes**: Confirm the bind-mount is active (`docker inspect` the MCP server container); if the guard file is not mounted, writes bypass it silently.
- **`HIERARCHY_ROOTS` out of date**: If a new root class was added without updating the registry, writer agents can overwrite its `ontologyClass`; add the new class name to the registry export and restart the MCP server.

attributes.name: Digest Entity Graph Orphaning — ObservationConsolidator Write Path
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Digest entities produced by `ObservationConsolidator.js` were orphaned at the knowledge graph level: inserted via `kmStore.putEntity()` with no subsequent `kmStore.addRelation()` calls, leaving them as disconnected nodes with zero graph edges. Phase 59 ("digest-insight-writer-edge-repair") is the 5-plan, 3-wave repair track that materializes embedded metadata as typed graph relations, backfills 34 historical orphans, and provides a 24-hour soak harness for ongoing orphan-floor monitoring.

## Architecture
- **Write site**: `ObservationConsolidator.js` — `kmStore.putEntity(legacyDigestToEntity(...))` is the primary insertion call; `kmStore.addRelation()` was absent pre-repair, leaving all digest entities with zero edges
- **Pre-repair storage gap**: `observation_ids` and similar fields were stored as scalar metadata rather than typed graph relations
- **`writeInsight` return signature** (Plan 59-01): refactored from scalar `row.id` to `{ legacyId, mintedId }` object; both fields are required for Wave 2 consumer wiring that establishes typed graph edges
- **Phase 59 wave structure:**
  - Wave 1 — Writer/Consolidator edge metadata; includes `writeInsight` signature change and JSDoc update
  - Wave 2 — Consumer wiring and orphan repair; backfills 34 historical orphaned entities; depends on dual-ID return from Wave 1
  - Wave 3 — 24-hour soak harness and runbook
- **Orphan baseline**: `orphanCount=7` measured pre-phase via `GET :3848/api/v1/graph/orphans`; backfill target resolves 34 additional historical orphans

## Key Files
- `src/live-logging/ObservationWriter.js` — `writeInsight` implementation; return value changed from scalar `row.id` to `{ legacyId, mintedId }` in Plan 59-01
- `src/live-logging/ObservationWriter.test.js` — test assertions updated for object return; 12/12 passing post-Wave 1
- `ObservationConsolidator.js` — primary write site; calls `kmStore.putEntity(legacyDigestToEntity(...))`; `addRelation()` calls added in Wave 2
- `.planning/phases/59-digest-insight-writer-edge-repair/59-01-SUMMARY.md` — Plan 59-01 execution summary
- `.planning/phases/59-digest-insight-writer-edge-repair/59-02-PLAN.md` — full phase plan artifact (5 plans across 3 waves)

## Usage
- `ObservationConsolidator.js` is invoked during daily digest consolidation to persist observation entities to the knowledge graph via km-core on `:3848`
- `writeInsight` is called by the consolidator; its `{ legacyId, mintedId }` dual-ID return feeds Wave 2 consumer wiring, which issues the previously-missing `addRelation()` calls to connect entities into the graph
- Ongoing orphan-floor check: `GET http://localhost:3848/api/v1/graph/orphans`; orphan count rising above pre-phase baseline signals new unrepaired insertions

## Troubleshooting
- **Orphan count rising post-repair**: new consolidation runs may be calling `putEntity()` without a matching `addRelation()`; audit `ObservationConsolidator.js` for any `putEntity` call not followed by edge materialization
- **Callers broken by `writeInsight` signature change**: any consumer expecting a scalar ID must destructure the new object; locate affected callers with `grep -r "writeInsight" src/`
- **Test failures in `ObservationWriter.test.js`**: ensure assertions reference `result.legacyId` / `result.mintedId`, not the deprecated `row.id` scalar form
- **Backfill verification**: after Wave 2 lands, re-query `:3848/api/v1/graph/orphans` and confirm the count dropped by approximately 34 from the pre-phase baseline

attributes.name: Knowledge Graph Parent-Edge Structural Decoupling
attributes.description:
## Purpose
The `parent` node attribute and `contains` graph edges are independent, mutually-unenforced representations of hierarchical membership in the knowledge graph. A node can carry an inbound `contains` edge without a populated `parent` attribute, producing false orphan-class reports for nodes that are structurally connected.

## Architecture
- **`parent` attribute**: a scalar field stored directly on the entity node record; absence causes diagnostic tooling to classify the node as an orphan
- **`contains` edges**: stored as directed graph relations in the edge table; their presence does not populate or validate the `parent` attribute on the target node
- **No enforcement**: no constraint, trigger, or write-time rule links the two representations; divergence accumulates silently as nodes are written
- **Upper-ontology General team pool**: approximately 75 generic-concept nodes created before the lower-ontology rework sit outside Project subtrees; these nodes predate the `parent` attribute convention and are the primary population exhibiting this pattern
- **Two remediation strategies**:
  1. **Writer-side enforcement** — populate `parent` at entity write time from the source node of the creating `contains` edge; prevents future divergence
  2. **Consolidator-side backfill** — derive `parent` from existing `contains` edges during a consolidation pass; repairs existing nodes without changing the write path

## Key Files
- `~/Agentic/coding/src/live-logging/ObservationConsolidator.js` — candidate site for consolidator-side backfill; would derive `parent` from existing `contains` edges during consolidation
- `~/Agentic/coding/src/live-logging/ObservationWriter.js` — candidate site for writer-side enforcement; would populate `parent` at write time from edge source
- `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md` — references the lower-ontology rework phase, which is the planned scope for repairing the ~75-node General team pool

## Usage
`DynamicImporter` is the canonical documented example: it has an inbound `contains` edge from `ModuleLoader` but an empty `parent` field. When diagnosing orphan-class reports, always check for inbound `contains` edges before concluding true orphan status. Remediation for the ~75-node upper-ontology pool is deferred to a dedicated lower-ontology rework phase; do not apply ad-hoc individual node patches outside that phase.

## Troubleshooting
- **Node classified as orphan but has an inbound `contains` edge**: structural decoupling pattern — not a true orphan; `parent` was never populated from the edge; apply writer-side enforcement or consolidator-side backfill to repair
- **~75 nodes in the General team pool all show empty `parent`**: expected; these nodes predate the `parent` attribute convention; fix is scoped to the lower-ontology rework phase — do not patch individually before that phase begins
- **Orphan repair script (Phase 59-04) reporting unexpected orphan counts**: the 7-orphan / 179-dangling-ref baseline reflects the dry-run state; counts may shift after writer-side or consolidator-side remediation is applied — re-run the script after any structural change
- **Choosing between the two strategies**: writer-side enforcement prevents future divergence but only covers newly written nodes; consolidator-side backfill repairs existing nodes but requires a one-time pass; both strategies may be needed together

attributes.description:
## Purpose
Prevents writer agents from incorrectly overwriting the `ontologyClass` field on root-level entities (e.g., `CollectiveKnowledge`) with non-root types such as `"Detail"`. Misclassification silently truncates ancestry traces in the unified viewer's filter panels, causing the Online filter to stop at the project level rather than reaching the correct root. A one-shot repair script corrects any existing misclassification idempotently.

Three cooperating components:

- **`HIERARCHY_ROOTS` registry** (`lib/km-core/`): canonical exported list of top-level ontology class names. Acts as the reference set that all agents and guards consult when evaluating whether an entity is a hierarchy root.
- **Writer-side hard-root guard** (`integrations/mcp-server-semantic-analysis`): intercepts incoming `ontologyClass` write operations; rejects any attempt to overwrite an entity whose current class appears in `HIERARCHY_ROOTS`. Activated at runtime via bind-mount — when Docker rebuilds are unavailable, the guard is injected via volume mount.
- **Idempotent repair script**: one-shot script that scans all entities, identifies any root-level entity with an incorrect `ontologyClass`, and resets it to the correct root class. Safe to re-run.

## Key Files
- `lib/km-core/` — contains `HIERARCHY_ROOTS` registry export
- `integrations/mcp-server-semantic-analysis/` — writer-side guard implementation
- Repair script — one-shot; location project-specific

## Usage
- Guard is always-on once the MCP server is running with the correct bind-mount; no per-write configuration required.
- `HIERARCHY_ROOTS` must be updated whenever a new root ontology class is introduced; failure to update it leaves new roots unprotected.
- Run the repair script after any bulk import or migration that predates the guard's activation.

- **Online filter stops at project level instead of root**: A root entity has been misclassified; run the repair script to identify and fix it.

attributes.name: gsd-browser Operator Verification Tool
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Browser automation tool backed by a persistent background Chromium daemon, used to smoke-test web UIs — primarily the Unified Viewer and Coverage dashboard — and produce screenshot evidence for operator verification runbooks at phase acceptance gates. The primary mechanism for executing scenario-card checks and generating `{phase}-VERIFICATION.md` artifacts required to formally close a phase.

## Architecture
- **Background Chromium daemon**: long-running process handling all `navigate` and screenshot operations; liveness tracked via a PID file in the gsd-browser state directory.
- **Daemon lifetime independence**: the daemon can terminate independently of the target service or network connection; when down, all subsequent `gsd-browser` calls fail with a **process-state error** — not a network or service error.
- **Service isolation**: target service HTTP reachability and daemon liveness are fully independent failure domains; a service being up does not imply the daemon is up, and vice versa.

## Key Files
- PID file in gsd-browser state directory — daemon liveness tracking; location is gsd-browser state directory (exact path environment-specific)
- `{phase}-VERIFICATION.md` — output artifact; required for formal phase closure

## Usage
- Invoked during phase acceptance gates to execute scenario-card checks against live UI targets.
- Produces screenshot evidence and `{phase}-VERIFICATION.md` for operator review.
- Operator reviews screenshots as part of the verification runbook before approving phase close.

## Troubleshooting
- `gsd-browser` process-state errors mean the Chromium daemon is down — restart the daemon independently; do not troubleshoot the target service first.
- Always check daemon PID file before assuming a service failure: the two failure domains are independent.
- Blank or incorrect screenshots with no error: verify target service is separately reachable (HTTP check), then verify daemon is serving the correct URL.

attributes.name: gsd-browser Screenshot CLI
attributes.description:
## Purpose
`gsd-browser` is a CLI tool for programmatic browser screenshot capture and UI interaction, serving as the primary tooling for phase verification runbooks that validate rendered web UI integrity through screenshot checkpoints and inline DOM evaluation (e.g., `60-VERIFICATION.md` for Phase 60).

## Architecture
- **Screenshot command**: requires `--output <path>` and `--format <type>` flags; positional path arguments are **not** accepted
  - Correct: `gsd-browser screenshot --output <path> --format png`
  - Incorrect: `gsd-browser screenshot <path>`
- **Filter/checkbox state manipulation**: use the `set-checked` command; the `--ref` selector flag is **not supported** and will fail
- **DOM evaluation**: inline DOM evals (e.g., checking `RuntimeDiagnostics` visibility, `DOMAINS` section content) are performed as discrete checkpoint steps alongside screenshot capture
- No UI state persists between invocations; each checkpoint must establish required filter/UI state before capturing

## Key Files
- `.planning/phases/60-unified-viewer-rendering-ux-integrity/screenshots/` — Phase 60 screenshot output directory; must be scaffolded before first capture
- `.planning/phases/60-unified-viewer-rendering-ux-integrity/60-VERIFICATION.md` — visual smoke test runbook; checkpoint definitions, capture commands, and DOM eval results

## Usage
Used during phase verification to capture baseline and incremental screenshots across multiple checkpoints. Per-checkpoint workflow:
1. Apply UI state changes via `set-checked` (e.g., toggle filter checkboxes, enable debug mode)
2. Run `gsd-browser screenshot --output <path> --format png`
3. Record result and any inline DOM evals in `60-VERIFICATION.md` (or equivalent phase verification document)

attributes.name: obs-api Ontology Registry Sourcing Architecture
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Documents the obs-api ontology class sourcing architecture: a curated host-side directory (`.data/ontologies/obs-api/`) is wired into `scripts/observations-api-server.mjs` with fallback to the bundled `lib/km-core/ontology/` registry. The API serves 50 classes including L1 and L2 types needed by the unified viewer filter and writer-side validation.

## Architecture
- **Active load path**: `GraphKMStore` reads ontology class definitions from `.data/ontologies/obs-api/` at startup, with automatic fallback to the bundled `lib/km-core/ontology/` directory if the host directory is unavailable
- **Host directory contents**: merged `upper.json` (host classes + `LearningArtifact`) plus writer L1/L2 files and viewer L1/L2 files; validated by standalone pre-flight load before wiring
- **Class count**: API serves 50 classes — L1 (`Component`, `SubComponent`, `Detail`), L2 (10 Phase-57 classes), upper-level classes, and writer/viewer domain classes
- **Bundled-only classes**: `Digest`, `Insight`, `Observation` exist in the bundled registry but are absent from the host `upper.json`; writer-side validation for these classes depends on the bundled fallback path remaining active. `LearningArtifact` has been added to the host `upper.json` and is no longer bundled-only.
- **L0 synthesis**: the km-core API handler at port 12436 synthesizes `System` and `Project` L0 anchor classes via `HIERARCHY_ROOTS` + `extends` fallback; this path is independent of the ontology directory sourcing
- **Configuration point**: `scripts/observations-api-server.mjs` line 1336 — `ontologyDir` parameter for `GraphKMStore`

## Key Files
- `scripts/observations-api-server.mjs` — line 1336: `ontologyDir` configuration; currently set to `.data/ontologies/obs-api/` with fallback to bundled
- `.data/ontologies/obs-api/` — active curated ontology directory; contains merged `upper.json` and writer/viewer L1/L2 files
- `.data/ontologies/obs-api/upper.json` — merged L0/L1/L2 hierarchy including host classes and `LearningArtifact`
- `lib/km-core/ontology/` — bundled fallback registry; contains `Digest`, `Insight`, `Observation`; activated when host directory is unavailable

## Usage
obs-api reads ontology classes from `.data/ontologies/obs-api/` at startup; the bundled fallback activates if the host directory is missing. The merged `upper.json` must contain all classes needed for writer-side validation that are not covered by the bundled fallback. When adding new ontology classes, add them to `.data/ontologies/obs-api/` and confirm the class count increases in the API response. Do not remove the bundled fallback path — `Digest`, `Insight`, and `Observation` depend on it.

## Troubleshooting
- **L1/L2 group headers absent from viewer filter**: verify `.data/ontologies/obs-api/` exists and contains the expected L1/L2 files; if the directory is missing, obs-api falls back to the bundled registry which contains no viewer-specific L1/L2 classes
- **L0 group headers (`System`/`Project`) absent**: km-core API handler at port 12436 not running or `HIERARCHY_ROOTS` registry not compiled; this path is independent of the host ontology directory
- **`Digest`/`Insight`/`Observation` writer validation breaks**: these are absent from the host `upper.json`; they depend on the bundled fallback; do not disable or remove the fallback path
- **API serves fewer than 50 classes**: host directory missing, incomplete, or pre-flight load failed; check obs-api startup logs for directory load errors
- **Confirming which ontology path is active**: inspect line 1336 of `scripts/observations-api-server.mjs`; `.data/ontologies/obs-api/` = host (current default), `lib/km-core/ontology/` = bundled fallback

attributes.name: coding CLI — preToolUse Hook Configuration
attributes.description:
## Purpose
`coding/bin/coding` is the primary agent runner entry point for the `coding` project. It resolves the `claude` CLI binary via `PATH`, which is supplied by the `claude-code` Homebrew cask. Incomplete cask upgrades can leave a dangling symlink that silently breaks `coding/bin/coding` with no clear error message pointing at the root cause.

## Architecture
- **Resolution chain**: `coding/bin/coding` → `claude` lookup via `PATH` → `/opt/homebrew/bin/claude` (symlink managed by Homebrew) → `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/claude-code/<version>/claude` (actual binary)
- **Failure mode — incomplete cask extraction**: A Homebrew cask upgrade updates the `/opt/homebrew/bin/claude` symlink to point at the new version directory but may fail to extract the binary into `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/claude-code/<version>/`, leaving a dangling symlink; `coding/bin/coding` then fails to start because the resolved path does not exist
- **Manual symlink fix is insufficient**: The binary file itself is absent, not merely misdirected; correcting the symlink target without a reinstall still yields a missing file

## Key Files
- `coding/bin/coding` — agent runner entry point; requires `claude` on `PATH`
- `/opt/homebrew/bin/claude` — Homebrew-managed symlink; inspect with `ls -la /opt/homebrew/bin/claude`
- `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/claude-code/<version>/` — cask extraction directory; must contain the actual `claude` binary after a successful install

## Usage
`coding/bin/coding` is invoked directly to start any agent session. It must be able to exec `claude` before any session logic runs. The dependency is implicit (via `PATH`) rather than an explicit configured path.

## Troubleshooting
- **`coding/bin/coding` fails to start after a `claude-code` upgrade**: Run `ls -la $(which claude)` to check for a dangling symlink, then `ls /opt/homebrew/Caskroom/claude-code/` to confirm the binary is missing from the new version directory
- **Fix — dangling symlink after incomplete cask extraction**: `brew reinstall --cask claude-code`; this re-extracts the full cask and restores the binary
- **Fix — partial Homebrew state**: `brew cleanup claude-code && brew reinstall --cask claude-code` ensures stale artifacts are removed before reinstall
- **Verify resolution**: After reinstall, `claude --version` must succeed and `coding/bin/coding` should start normally in default mode
- **Distinguishing from PATH config issues**: If `which claude` resolves but `claude --version` fails with a "no such file" error, the cause is a dangling symlink, not a PATH misconfiguration

attributes.name: LSL Session Continuity Bootstrap
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Standardized multi-step procedure for loading recent LSL session files at the start of any new agent session to re-establish task state, in-progress work, and likely next steps — eliminating reliance on agent memory or external summaries. Also serves as the primary crash and interruption recovery mechanism: files from the interruption time window pinpoint exactly where prior work was cut off and what the next action was.

## Architecture
Multi-step execution — must run in strict order:

1. **Locate** `.specstory/history/` — an **independent git repo** separate from the outer `coding/` repo; auto-detection does not cross project boundaries; navigate there explicitly when operating outside `coding/`. Top level contains **only `README.md`**; all session files live under year subdirectories (e.g., `2026/`) — top-level-only scans find nothing.
2. **Sort by mtime** — recency is the primary and mandatory sort criterion; never sort alphabetically. Date-prefixed filenames make alphabetical sort deceptively close to correct but not equivalent.
3. **Select candidate files by recency and size** — the most recent files are the primary candidates; file size is used as a secondary signal of content richness.
4. **Fallback rule for sparse files**: if a selected file has fewer than ~500 lines of content, it is treated as too sparse to reconstruct context alone, and the procedure falls back to loading an additional older file to fill the gap (multiple files may be read together to cover a multi-hour activity window, e.g. two consecutive hourly files).
5. **Cross-reference the coding project** when the current working session is in a different project than `coding/`, since some context (e.g. workflow definitions, prior architectural decisions) is only recorded there.
- **Main session naming**: `YYYY-MM-DD_HHMM-HHMM_<hash>` (underscore separates date from time range; trailing short hash disambiguates concurrent sessions, e.g. `2026-07-09_0500-0600_c197ef.md`).

## Key Files
- `.specstory/history/README.md` — top-level marker file; the only file present outside year subdirectories.
- `.specstory/history/<year>/*.md` — actual LSL session transcript files, sorted/filtered per the procedure above.

## Usage
Run automatically or manually at the start of any new agent session (especially after a context-window reset, crash, or multi-hour gap) to reconstruct "where was I" without re-deriving it from scratch. Commonly loads 1-2 files covering a ~1-2 hour recent activity window; the procedure is treated as a validated, reusable session-startup workflow rather than a one-off investigation step.

## Troubleshooting
- If context reconstruction feels incomplete after loading the most recent file, check its line count — under ~500 lines likely means the session was short or sparse, and an additional older file should be loaded per the fallback rule.
- If no LSL files are found, verify you are inside `.specstory/history/<year>/` and not scanning only the top level (which contains just `README.md`).
- If session naming/timestamps don't align with expected recent activity, confirm `.specstory/history/` is being treated as its own independent git repo and not conflated with the outer `coding/` repo's file listing.

attributes.name: rapid-llm-proxy — Provider Fallback Chain
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Routes all four coding agents (`claude`, `copilot`, `opencode`, `mastra`) through `rapid-llm-proxy` at `http://localhost:12435` for uniform wire-level token measurement. Proxy routing is injected universally at launcher startup — no per-agent manual configuration is needed or appropriate.

## Architecture
- **Single intercept point**: `rapid-llm-proxy` at `http://localhost:12435`; all agent LLM traffic flows through it

| Agent | Routing Mechanism | Required Value |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:12435` |
| Copilot CLI | `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:12435/v1` |
| OpenCode | existing proxy config | no additional env var |
| Mastra | existing proxy config | no additional env var |

- **Canonical injection point**: `launch-agent-common.sh` sets all required env vars at startup for every supported agent type via `coding/bin/coding`
- **Sub-agent propagation**: Env vars propagate to spawned sub-agents through the hook layer, ensuring dynamically spawned agents also route through the proxy

## Key Files
- `coding/bin/coding` — primary launcher entry point; resolves and invokes `launch-agent-common.sh`
- `launch-agent-common.sh` — universal env-var injection block; the only correct place to add or modify agent routing
- `~/.claude/projects/-Users-<USER>-Agentic-coding/memory/reference_agent_proxy_routing_launcher.md` — persistent per-agent routing reference; recovers canonical routing state across sessions

## Usage
Invoked via `coding/bin/coding <agent-name>`. All proxy env vars are applied before the agent binary receives control. The persistent memory doc provides a durable routing map and should be consulted when reinitializing a session after a gap.

## Troubleshooting
- **Traffic bypassing proxy**: Verify `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` / `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` are present in the process environment after startup; inspect the injection block in `launch-agent-common.sh`
- **Sub-agents not measured**: Confirm env vars propagate through the hook layer — missing hook-layer propagation silently breaks sub-agent coverage without any error
- **OpenCode / Mastra silent routing failure**: These agents rely on their own existing proxy config rather than injected env vars; verify their config files point to `localhost:12435`, not a direct provider URL
- **Lost routing state across sessions**: Consult `memory/reference_agent_proxy_routing_launcher.md` for the canonical per-agent routing map before any re-initialization

attributes.name: Unified Viewer Frontend
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Renders the km-core knowledge graph as an interactive node graph with filter panels (including the Online filter for entity ancestry traces). Connects to obs-api at `:12436` for all graph data. `ApiClient.ts` mediates every fetch between the frontend and the obs-api REST layer.

## Architecture
- **Node fetch layer**: `listEntities()` in `ApiClient.ts` is the primary data fetch call; it carries a silent 1000-entity cap — when the graph exceeds 1000 nodes, the viewer renders whatever subset is returned, causing disconnected "island" artifacts where edges reference nodes that were not fetched. The cap is not surfaced as an error or warning.
- **Fix for node cap**: remove or raise the limit in `listEntities()` to request the full node set; rebuild `integrations/unified-viewer/dist/` after the change
- **Filter panels**: include the Online filter for ancestry trace display; ancestry correctness depends on both complete node fetch and correct `ontologyClass` assignments in km-core (see km-core Ontology Hierarchy Root Enforcement insight)
- **Data source**: all entity and edge data served by obs-api (`:12436`); viewer dist must be rebuilt after any `ApiClient.ts` or source change

## Key Files
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/ApiClient.ts` — `listEntities()` method; 1000-node fetch cap; primary data fetch entry point
- `integrations/unified-viewer/dist/` — compiled viewer artifacts; must be rebuilt after any source change; mtime used as rebuild confirmation signal
- obs-api at `:12436` — backend data source for all `listEntities()` and related calls

## Usage
Viewer is accessed via HTTP on its exposed Docker port. `listEntities()` is called on graph load and on filter interaction. Any knowledge graph exceeding 1000 nodes requires the cap to be removed before rendering is reliable. attributes.name: Observations Pipeline
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Historical (pre-June 2026) mechanism that progressively throttled and eventually suspended periodic LLM proxy "keepalive"/health-check pings during extended user inactivity (AFK), instead of pinging continuously regardless of activity state. Being investigated for restoration to eliminate wasted LLM proxy calls (and associated token/cost burn) during idle periods — a known ongoing issue affecting `observation-writer` and related components' overnight/AFK traffic.

## Architecture
- **Target backoff schedule being restored**: progressive interval widening on inactivity — `60s → 10min → 30min → full suspend` — rather than the current behavior of continuous fixed-interval pinging regardless of user activity.
- **Resume trigger**: the first detected user activity after suspension should immediately restart the ping cycle from the beginning (60s interval), rather than requiring a full session restart.
- **Relationship to other AFK-aware components**: this mirrors (and may directly be) the AFK back-off logic separately noted in `health-coordinator.js`'s `userActiveNow()` gate (~5s probe cycle) — the pre-June 2026 mechanism being investigated here may be the original/intended implementation that the current `health-coordinator` gate is a regression or partial reimplementation of.
- **Recovery approach**: purely historical/archaeological at this stage — investigation is proceeding by mining git log history, LSL session transcripts, and prior implementation records to recover the original design intent and code before any new implementation is written; no source code has been modified yet.

## Key Files
- Not yet identified — investigation is still in the historical-recovery phase; likely candidates include `health-coordinator.js` and/or `observation-writer` scheduling logic based on related known AFK-backoff work in adjacent components, but this has not been confirmed for this specific restoration effort.

## Usage
Investigation-only phase, triggered to address ongoing resource waste from continuous LLM proxy pinging during AFK periods (a known pattern also documented under `observation-writer` and `health-coordinator` Gate 1/Gate 2 suppression logic). No user-facing or operational usage yet since no code has landed.

## Troubleshooting
- Not yet applicable — no implementation exists yet to troubleshoot; consult this insight for background context on why a backoff/suspend mechanism is being reintroduced.
- If investigating continuous/overnight LLM proxy pings in the interim, cross-reference the `observation-writer Unexpected LLM Calls` and `health-coordinator` AFK back-off insights, which document the currently-regressed or partial suppression gates this restoration effort aims to fix or supersede.

attributes.name: LSL Resolver — resolve-observations-from-lsl.mjs
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Digest entities produced by `ObservationConsolidator.js` were orphaned at the knowledge graph level: inserted via `kmStore.putEntity()` with no subsequent `kmStore.addRelation()` calls, leaving them as disconnected nodes with zero graph edges. Phase 59 ("digest-insight-writer-edge-repair") is the 5-plan, 3-wave repair track that materializes embedded metadata as typed graph relations, backfills 34 historical orphans, and provides a 24-hour soak harness for ongoing orphan-floor monitoring.

## Architecture
- **Write site**: `ObservationConsolidator.js` — `kmStore.putEntity(legacyDigestToEntity(...))` is the primary insertion call; `kmStore.addRelation()` was absent pre-repair, leaving all digest entities with zero edges
- **Pre-repair storage gap**: `observation_ids` and similar fields were stored as scalar metadata rather than typed graph relations
- **`writeInsight` return signature** (Plan 59-01): refactored from scalar `row.id` to `{ legacyId, mintedId }` object; both fields are required for Wave 2 consumer wiring that establishes typed graph edges
- **Phase 59 wave structure:**
  - Wave 1 — Writer/Consolidator edge metadata; includes `writeInsight` signature change and JSDoc update
  - Wave 2 — Consumer wiring and orphan repair; backfills 34 historical orphaned entities; depends on dual-ID return from Wave 1
  - Wave 3 — 24-hour soak harness and runbook
- **Orphan baseline**: `orphanCount=7` measured pre-phase via `GET :3848/api/v1/graph/orphans`; backfill target resolves 34 additional historical orphans

## Key Files
- `src/live-logging/ObservationWriter.js` — `writeInsight` implementation; return value changed from scalar `row.id` to `{ legacyId, mintedId }` in Plan 59-01
- `src/live-logging/ObservationWriter.test.js` — test assertions updated for object return; 12/12 passing post-Wave 1
- `ObservationConsolidator.js` — primary write site; calls `kmStore.putEntity(legacyDigestToEntity(...))`; `addRelation()` calls added in Wave 2
- `.planning/phases/59-digest-insight-writer-edge-repair/59-01-SUMMARY.md` — Plan 59-01 execution summary
- `.planning/phases/59-digest-insight-writer-edge-repair/59-02-PLAN.md` — full phase plan artifact (5 plans across 3 waves)

## Usage
- `ObservationConsolidator.js` is invoked during daily digest consolidation to persist observation entities to the knowledge graph via km-core on `:3848`
- `writeInsight` is called by the consolidator; its `{ legacyId, mintedId }` dual-ID return feeds Wave 2 consumer wiring, which issues the previously-missing `addRelation()` calls to connect entities into the graph
- Ongoing orphan-floor check: `GET http://localhost:3848/api/v1/graph/orphans`; orphan count rising above pre-phase baseline signals new unrepaired insertions

## Troubleshooting
- **Orphan count rising post-repair**: new consolidation runs may be calling `putEntity()` without a matching `addRelation()`; audit `ObservationConsolidator.js` for any `putEntity` call not followed by edge materialization
- **Callers broken by `writeInsight` signature change**: any consumer expecting a scalar ID must destructure the new object; locate affected callers with `grep -r "writeInsight" src/`
- **Test failures in `ObservationWriter.test.js`**: ensure assertions reference `result.legacyId` / `result.mintedId`, not the deprecated `row.id` scalar form
- **Backfill verification**: after Wave 2 lands, re-query `:3848/api/v1/graph/orphans` and confirm the count dropped by approximately 34 from the pre-phase baseline

attributes.name: Phase Security Audit Workflow
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Post-phase-close security gate that extracts all declared STRIDE threats from sub-plan artifacts, dispatches `gsd-security-auditor` to verify every mitigation is present in implementation code (not rubber-stamped), and commits `{phase}-SECURITY.md` when the SECURED ✓ verdict clears. Runs as a fully standalone pass — separate from main execution, code review, and the Phase Close-Out Protocol.

## Architecture
- **Entrypoint**: `/gsd-secure-phase [phase]`
- **Workflow file**: `~/.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/secure-phase.md` — loaded in full before any action; governs all audit behavior.
- **Invocation timing**: Surfaced as "outstanding" at step 6 of the Phase Close-Out Protocol; must **not** be triggered during close-out — requires explicit operator dispatch only after step 6 fully completes.
- **Two-stage execution (strict ordering)**:
  1. *Stage 1* — Load `secure-phase.md`; verify gate-preserving logic is ready. No artifacts produced, no files modified.
  2. *Stage 2* — Extract STRIDE threats from sub-plan artifacts; dispatch `gsd-security-auditor` sub-agent; verify mitigations exist in implementation code; commit `{phase}-SECURITY.md` on SECURED ✓ verdict.

## Key Files
- `~/.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/secure-phase.md` — governing workflow file; must be loaded before any audit action
- `{phase}-SECURITY.md` — output artifact committed only on SECURED ✓ verdict

## Usage
Invoked explicitly by the operator via `/gsd-secure-phase [phase]` after Phase Close-Out Protocol step 6 completes. Never auto-triggered. The `gsd-security-auditor` sub-agent performs mitigation verification; this workflow orchestrates it.

## Troubleshooting
- **Invoked during close-out (not after)**: Invalid — abort and re-invoke only after step 6 of Phase Close-Out Protocol fully completes.
- **`secure-phase.md` not found**: Verify `~/.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/` directory exists and the file is present before invoking.
- **STRIDE threats not extracted**: Confirm sub-plan artifacts for the target phase exist and contain STRIDE threat declarations.
- **Audit rubber-stamps mitigations without deep verification**: Check `gsd-security-auditor` sub-agent prompt and injected toolset for verification depth.

attributes.name: GSD v7.2 Milestone State
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Provides a stateless resolver and structural validator for YAML experiment spec files within the experiments subsystem. Exports canonical constants and validation functions that all downstream experiment execution plans depend on for spec parsing, agent-identity resolution, and shell-safety enforcement.

## Architecture
- **Pure resolver** (SPEC-01): resolves a raw YAML experiment spec into a normalized internal representation; no side effects
- **Validator** (SPEC-02): validates experiment spec structure against the documented YAML schema; rejects malformed specs and unknown-agent references
- **Exported symbols**:
  - `KNOWN_AGENTS` — canonical list of recognized agent identifiers; consulted by validation to reject unrecognized agent references
  - `SHELL_META_RE` — regex for shell metacharacter detection; re-exported from this module as the single authoritative source across the experiments subsystem
  - Validation function(s) — primary entry points for spec validation by consumers
- **Downstream dependency**: downstream execution plans (77-02, 77-03) depend on this module being present and fully validated before they can execute; it is a hard Wave 1 gate

## Key Files
- `lib/experiments/experiment-spec.mjs` — primary module: resolver, validator, `KNOWN_AGENTS`, `SHELL_META_RE`, and all validation function exports
- Spec test suite (20 tests) — covers resolver and validator paths; located in the experiments test tree alongside the module

## Usage
- Imported by downstream experiment plans for spec loading and agent-identity validation before any experiment run is dispatched
- `KNOWN_AGENTS` is the authoritative reference whenever agent identity must be confirmed — do not define agent lists inline in consumers
- `SHELL_META_RE` should be imported from this module rather than redefined; all experiments subsystem consumers must use this single export
- An example YAML schema is documented within the module and serves as the authoring reference for new experiment specs

## Troubleshooting
- If downstream plans fail to resolve agent identity: verify `KNOWN_AGENTS` export from `lib/experiments/experiment-spec.mjs` contains the expected identifiers; do not patch agent lists in consumer code
- If spec validation rejects a YAML file: compare its structure against the example YAML schema bundled in the module
- Canonical test gate: **20/20 spec tests** must pass; any failure indicates a regression in resolver or validator logic — run the spec test suite directly against `lib/experiments/experiment-spec.mjs`
- SPEC-01 (resolver) and SPEC-02 (validator) are the two acceptance requirements tracked in `SUMMARY.md`; both must remain satisfied after any changes to the module

attributes.name: Consolidator-Insight Service
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Reconciles per-request context-turns measurements against timeline-measured totals for a given span, proving the two measurement surfaces agree (or explaining why they don't) rather than surfacing unexplained discrepancies to the user. Displayed inside the Cache Visualization Modal and per-turn span explainer.

## Architecture
- **Token-count reconciliation**: Per-request context-turn token counts are shown alongside timeline-measured row totals; these must match for the same source span (e.g., 3,615 tokens across 3 requests). Any residual delta is attributed to foreground/background rows added by Phase-75 wall-clock windowing that fall outside the per-request measurement window.
- **Turn-count reconciliation (distinct axis)**: The explainer's turn count (from `context-turns` records) and the timeline's turn count (from claude-code CLI worker turns) can legitimately differ — e.g., 3 vs. 5 — because they measure two different event populations, not the same stream measured twice. This difference is documented expected behavior, not a bug.
- **Two measurement surfaces**: `context-turns` records (per-request) and timeline rows (wall-clock windowed) are intentionally independent; the modal's job is to attribute any gap, not eliminate it.

## Key Files
- `context-turns.json` — source of per-request context-turns records for token/turn reconciliation
- Cache Visualization Modal and per-turn span explainer — UI surfaces where the explainer is rendered

## Usage
- Activated when a user inspects a span inside the Cache Visualization Modal or per-turn span explainer and needs to understand token or turn count differences between measurement surfaces
- Consumed by developers diagnosing apparent discrepancies in token accounting

## Troubleshooting
- **Token count mismatch**: Check for foreground/background rows added by Phase-75 wall-clock windowing — these fall outside the per-request measurement window and are the expected source of residual delta
- **Turn count mismatch**: Explainer count (from `context-turns`) and timeline count (from claude-code CLI worker) measuring different populations is expected and is NOT a bug; document as such rather than investigating further
- **Stale reconciliation data**: Verify `context-turns.json` is current for the span being inspected

attributes.name: OKB ApiClient — Dual-Backend Routing and Relation-Cap Honesty
attributes.description:
## Purpose
The OKB `ApiClient` is the API access layer for the Ontological Knowledge Browser. It routes requests to two distinct backends via an explicit `apiVersion` flag, enforces relation-cap honesty (callers always receive the pre-cap total alongside the capped result), provides client-side 1-hop node-expand, and raises a dedicated error type when OKM Express is unreachable. Validated by 23/23 unit tests and 6/6 E2E tests against live OKM Express on `:8090`.

## Architecture

attributes.name: LLM Proxy Worker Pool
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Governs the live-test gating mechanism, `node --test` runner output behavior, and known hang/deadlock patterns for the worker-pool integration test suite in `rapid-llm-proxy`. Patterns apply to any integration test that conditionally gates live execution behind a flag or environment variable.

## Architecture
**Live-mode gate — dual-check pattern (mandatory for all live-gated tests):**
- Every live-gated test must check **both** `process.argv.includes('--live')` (direct `node` invocation) **and** `process.env.LLM_PROXY_LIVE === '1'` (runner compatibility)
- Root cause of single-check failure: `node --test` spawns a child process per test file; trailing CLI args such as `--live` are **not forwarded**, so `process.argv` always evaluates `false` under the runner
- `integration-bridge.test.mjs` — canonical reference implementation of the dual-check pattern
- `worker-pool-live.test.mjs` — confirmed compliant with dual-check pattern after Phase 62 fix

**Phase 62 UAT Results (live-confirmed, all runnable SCs passed):**
- SC-1 (stable-PID): PASSED
- SC-2 (cold-pool): confirmed indirectly
- SC-3 (no-spawn-on-direct): PASSED
- SC-4 (escape-hatch): PASSED; warm <3s sanity: PASSED
- SC-5 (cancel-seam via `control_request{interrupt}`): unit-verified only; real-stream termination deferred to Phase 63

**`node --test` output behavior:**
- All test output is buffered and emitted as a batch at test completion, not streamed in real time
- Long-running live tests (>30s) appear hung in CI; this is normal — do not interpret silence as deadlock
- Use `--test-reporter=tap` or direct `node` invocation for real-time output

**Known hang/deadlock patterns:**
- Stdio deadlock: avoid synchronous reads from worker stdout while writing to stdin; use async event-driven patterns only
- Worker slot starvation: pool smaller than concurrent request count causes indefinite queue with no timeout at the queue layer

## Key Files
- `tests/integration/worker-pool-live.test.mjs` — live UAT suite; dual-check gate confirmed
- `tests/integration/integration-bridge.test.mjs` — canonical dual-check reference implementation
- `reference_node_test_argv_live_gate.md` — persistent reference doc for the argv/env-var gate pattern
- `.planning/phases/62-*/62-HUMAN-UAT.md` — Phase 62 live UAT findings and SC evidence

## Usage
- **Direct invocation**: `node tests/integration/worker-pool-live.test.mjs --live`
- **Via `node --test` runner**: `LLM_PROXY_LIVE=1 node --test tests/integration/worker-pool-live.test.mjs`
- Both modes are equivalent; dual-check gate ensures consistent skip/run behavior regardless of invocation path

## Troubleshooting
- **Live tests silently skip under `node --test`**: `LLM_PROXY_LIVE=1` is missing from env; `--live` arg is stripped by the runner and never reaches the test file
- **Output appears frozen**: `node --test` buffers all output; switch to direct `node` invocation for real-time feedback on long-running suites
- **Cancel-seam SC fails**: `control_request{interrupt}` does not terminate real streams; Phase 63 will implement SIGTERM-based cancellation; do not expect interrupt protocol to work in live mode until then

attributes.name: Multi-Repo Git Coordination — LLM Proxy
attributes.description:
## Purpose
LLM proxy phase work is split across two independent git repositories. Closing any proxy-related phase requires coordinated commits and pushes to both: the `coding` repo (planning artifacts) and `_work/rapid-llm-proxy` (implementation). Neither push is meaningful in isolation — planning artifacts without implementation, or implementation without planning records, are both incomplete phase states.

## Architecture
- **`coding` repo**: holds `.planning/phases/`, `.planning/research/`, `STATE.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, `SUMMARY.md`, and all GSD phase planning artifacts; remote: `github.com/fwornle/coding.git`; **SSH transport only** (HTTPS will fail); direct commits and pushes to `main`
- **`_work/rapid-llm-proxy` repo**: fully separate git repository holding all proxy implementation files; remote: internal GHE instance; **HTTPS transport only** (SSH is not configured and will fail); independent commit history
- Both pushes must succeed and be explicitly confirmed before phase close-out is considered complete
- No cross-repo references or submodule links — repos are coordinated only by convention (phase IDs align across planning artifacts and implementation commits)

## Key Files
- `.planning/phases/` — planning artifacts in the `coding` repo
- `_work/rapid-llm-proxy/` — proxy implementation; separate git root
- `STATE.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, `SUMMARY.md` — phase tracking files in the `coding` repo

## Usage
- Required at every proxy-related phase close-out
- Operator must explicitly confirm both pushes succeeded before proceeding with the Phase Close-Out Protocol
- Transport protocol selection (SSH vs HTTPS) is repo-specific — the protocols are not interchangeable

## Troubleshooting
- **SSH failure on `rapid-llm-proxy`**: This repo requires HTTPS; update the remote URL to HTTPS format before retrying
- **HTTPS failure on `coding` repo**: This repo requires SSH; update the remote URL to SSH format before retrying
- **One push succeeds, one fails**: Phase close-out is incomplete — do not proceed until both repos are confirmed pushed
- **Diverged histories**: Each repo maintains an independent commit history; do not attempt to merge or cross-reference commits between repos

attributes.name: Plan-Phase Workflow
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Enforces XML element completeness on plan task definitions as a blocking pre-execution integrity gate within `gsd-execute-phase`. A single structurally invalid task definition prevents the entire phase from entering execution dispatch.

## Architecture
- **Validation trigger**: Runs inside `gsd-execute-phase` before any sub-agent is spawned — the first step of the pre-execution integrity gate sequence
- **Required element**: Every `checkpoint:human-verify` task definition must contain an explicit `<action>` XML element; absence is a hard structure validation failure
- **Failure scope**: One invalid task definition fails the entire phase gate; all wave sub-agents are held until the plan is corrected and re-validation passes
- **Recovery path**: When a planning agent is interrupted mid-write (e.g., watchdog timeout), affected task definitions remain partially written on disk; the correct fix is targeted in-place XML addition — no plan regeneration required
- **Partial-write detection**: Plans interrupted mid-write are identified by missing required XML elements in otherwise complete task definitions

## Key Files
- Plan task definition XML files — validated for `<action>` element presence before any dispatch
- `gsd-execute-phase` skill — hosts this validator as its first pre-dispatch gate step

## Usage
- Runs automatically as the first gate within `gsd-execute-phase` before any sub-agent is dispatched
- Applies to all `checkpoint:human-verify` task definitions in the current phase's plan set
- Downstream gates (GSD Plan Verification Gate) do not run until this validator passes

## Troubleshooting
- **Missing `<action>` element**: Add the element in-place to the affected task definition; do not regenerate the entire plan
- **Partial-write artifacts from watchdog interruption**: Identify affected definitions by locating truncated XML structures; apply targeted in-place XML addition
- **Gate blocking all waves on a single bad task**: Only the invalid definition needs correction — other plans in the phase are unaffected and do not require changes

attributes.name: gsd-plan-phase Skill — Phase Planning Orchestration
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Wave-based execution orchestrator for locked, fully-verified GSD phases. Loads per-phase plan artifacts, constructs a dependency-ordered DAG, dispatches isolated sub-agents per plan with fresh context budgets, and enforces pre-execution integrity gates before any sub-agent is spawned. A mandatory pre-execution context reset prevents planning-session state from polluting execution.

## Architecture
**Invocation:** `/gsd-execute-phase [phase] [--wave N] [--gaps-only] [--interactive]`

**Flag parsing — literal token matching only:**
| Flag | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `--wave N` | Execute only wave N |
| `--gaps-only` | Execute only plans with `gap_closure: true` in frontmatter; all others skipped |
| `--interactive` | Interactive execution mode |
| *(no flags)* | Full-phase execution |

Abbreviations (`--gap`) and `=` syntax (`--wave=2`) are silently unrecognized and fall back to full-phase execution.

**Execution sequence (all steps complete before any sub-agent is spawned):**
1. Mandatory pre-execution context reset — clears planning-session state
2. Load per-phase plan artifacts from disk
3. Construct dependency-ordered DAG
4. Pre-execution integrity gate enforcement (see GSD Plan Verification Gate insight)
5. Dispatch isolated sub-agents per plan, each with a fresh context budget

## Key Files
- Per-phase plan artifact files (disk) — loaded at step 2; must be current and committed before invocation
- `gsd-plan-checker` integrity gate — enforced at step 4

## Usage
Invoked by operator after `gsd-plan-phase` output passes the plan verification gate. Wave-scoped invocations (`--wave N`) re-enter mid-phase; `--gaps-only` targets only gap-closure plans. Sub-agents are fully isolated per plan — no shared state between concurrent dispatches.

## Troubleshooting
- **`--gaps-only` silently ignored**: Confirm exact spelling (`--gaps-only`, not `--gap` or `--gaps`); abbreviations fall back to full-phase execution without warning.
- **`--wave=2` not recognized**: Use space-separated form `--wave 2`; `=` syntax is unrecognized.
- **Planning state contaminating execution**: Confirm mandatory context reset completed before sub-agents were spawned. If contamination is suspected, abort, reset context manually, and re-invoke.
- **Sub-agent dispatched with stale plan**: Verify plan artifacts on disk are current before invocation; re-run `gsd-plan-phase` if plans were modified post-gate.

attributes.name: GSD New-Milestone Skill
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Creates and formalizes new GSD milestones by capturing design proposals — existing substrate, sequencing, hard constraints, and blocking prerequisites — into a canonical set of planning artifacts. Avoids re-deriving already-established context by consuming investigation artifacts produced before invocation. Distinct from `gsd-audit-milestone`, which is the pre-closure assessment tool.

## Architecture
**Prerequisite validation (before invocation):**
- Inspect relevant data artifacts (e.g., `.data/experiments/`) to confirm scope does not duplicate existing milestone work
- Scope the proposal relative to the prior milestone's phase range and open work

**Execution sequence:**
1. Load established context: existing substrate, prior milestone state, validated investigation findings
2. Capture design: sequencing constraints, hard requirements, blocking prerequisites in ordered sequence
3. Emit all five planning artifacts under `.planning/`
4. Post-creation questioning gate: validates scope and confirms prior milestone's closure strategy before phase planning begins

**Output artifacts (all under `.planning/`):**
| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `PROJECT.md` | Project description and goals |
| `research/` | Research notes and design documents |
| `REQUIREMENTS.md` | Formal requirements |
| `ROADMAP.md` | Phase roadmap |
| `STATE.md` | Initial execution state |

**Distinction from `gsd-audit-milestone`:** `gsd-new-milestone` creates milestones; `gsd-audit-milestone` is the pre-closure orchestrator that traces requirements to implementation evidence as input to `complete-milestone`.

## Key Files
- `.planning/PROJECT.md` — project description and goals
- `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md` — formal requirements
- `.planning/ROADMAP.md` — phase roadmap
- `.planning/STATE.md` — initial execution state
- `.planning/research/` — design research artifacts

## Usage
- Used to bootstrap a new milestone from a validated design concept
- Inputs: prior investigation artifacts (e.g., `.data/experiments/`) + prior milestone's phase/state context
- Output feeds into a post-creation questioning gate before phase planning begins
- Required whenever a new major initiative needs formal milestone tracking under the GSD workflow

## Troubleshooting
- **Prior milestone stuck at `status: executing`**: Invocation can proceed regardless; prior milestone's closure strategy is resolved at the post-creation questioning gate, not as a blocker to invocation
- **Risk of scope duplication**: Validate against existing artifact directories and prior milestone scope before invoking — the skill does not auto-detect overlap
- **Incomplete artifact set after invocation**: All five output artifacts must be committed; if any are missing, the skill did not complete cleanly — commit missing artifacts or re-run
- **Confused with `gsd-audit-milestone`**: These are distinct — new-milestone creates, audit-milestone assesses for closure; applying the wrong one at the wrong gate produces incorrect outputs and may stall the phase pipeline

- **Prior milestone stuck at `status: executing`**: Invocation can proceed regardless; prior milestone's closure strategy is resolved at the post-creation questioning gate, not as a blocker to invocation
- **Risk of scope duplication**: Validate against existing artifact directories and prior milestone scope before invoking — the skill does not auto-detect overlap
- **Incomplete artifact set after invocation**: All five output artifacts must be committed; if any are missing, the skill did not complete cleanly — commit missing artifacts or re-run
- **Confused with `gsd-audit-milestone`**: These are distinct — new-milestone creates, audit-milestone assesses for closure; applying the wrong one at the wrong gate produces incorrect outputs and may stall the phase pipeline

attributes.name: Documentation Diagram Style Guide
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Enforces consistent standards for all PlantUML and Mermaid diagram artifacts across the project. Governs file placement, naming conventions, PlantUML authoring requirements, Mermaid usage restrictions, PNG generation, and pre-commit validation. A constraint monitor actively enforces placement rules and surfaces violations as health dashboard alerts.

## Architecture
**File placement (constraint-monitored):**
- `.puml` source files → `docs/puml/` exclusively; files placed elsewhere trigger a health dashboard alert.
- Generated PNGs → `docs/images/` exclusively — a **separate tree** from `docs-content/images/` (the MkDocs-served image root for the published site). Misplacing files between these two trees is the primary cause of missing images in the built site.
- The `semantic-analysis_generate_plantuml_diagrams` tool writes to its own default location, **not** `docs/puml/`; explicit post-generation relocation to `docs/puml/` is mandatory before committing.

**Naming conventions:**
- Strict kebab-case throughout — applies to both `.puml` sources and generated PNGs.
- No incremental suffixes: `-v2`, `-new`, `-final`, and similar variants are prohibited. The canonical name is the only valid name; updates replace the file in place.

**PlantUML authoring requirements:**
- Mandatory `!include _standard-style.puml` at the top of every `.puml` file.
- Component stereotypes must be applied consistently.
- PNG generation via the `plantuml` CLI only — no other generation paths.

**Mermaid usage restrictions:**
- Mermaid diagrams are **inline-only** within Markdown files.
- Standalone Mermaid diagram files are prohibited — all Mermaid content must be embedded directly in its host `.md` file.

**Pre-commit validation checklist:**
- Run the validation workflow before committing any documentation changes.
- Check: `.puml` files are in `docs/puml/`, PNGs are in `docs/images/`, names are kebab-case with no suffix variants, every `.puml` includes `_standard-style.puml`, no standalone Mermaid files exist.

## Key Files
- `docs/puml/` — canonical location for all `.puml` source files
- `docs/images/` — canonical location for all generated PNGs (project artifact tree)
- `docs-content/images/` — MkDocs-served image root for the published site (separate tree; do not conflate with `docs/images/`)
- `_standard-style.puml` — mandatory include for all PlantUML diagrams

## Usage
Applies to all contributors and agents producing diagram or documentation artifacts. The constraint monitor runs continuously and reports placement violations to the health dashboard. Any architecture diagrams produced must accurately reflect confirmed system behavior (e.g., token capture and caching behavior per adapter type) — the style guide governs form, not content accuracy.

## Troubleshooting
- **Image missing from built site**: Almost always a tree-confusion error — file landed in `docs/images/` instead of `docs-content/images/` (or vice versa). Check which tree MkDocs is serving (`docs_dir` in `mkdocs.yml` points to `docs-content`).
- **Health dashboard placement alert**: A `.puml` file exists outside `docs/puml/` or a PNG exists outside `docs/images/`. Locate and move the offending file; the alert clears on next constraint-monitor scan.
- **Diagram not updating**: A suffix variant (e.g., `diagram-v2.puml`) was created instead of replacing the canonical file. Delete the suffix variant, update the canonical file, and regenerate the PNG.
- **Tool-generated `.puml` in wrong location**: After running `semantic-analysis_generate_plantuml_diagrams`, manually move the output to `docs/puml/` before staging — the tool does not respect the project placement convention.

attributes.name: Worker-Pool Integration Tests — Live Mode and Output Behavior
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Governs the live-test gating mechanism, `node --test` runner output behavior, and known hang/deadlock patterns for the worker-pool integration test suite in `rapid-llm-proxy`. Patterns apply to any integration test that conditionally gates live execution behind a flag or environment variable.

## Architecture
**Live-mode gate — dual-check pattern (mandatory for all live-gated tests):**
- Every live-gated test must check **both** `process.argv.includes('--live')` (direct `node` invocation) **and** `process.env.LLM_PROXY_LIVE === '1'` (runner compatibility)
- Root cause of single-check failure: `node --test` spawns a child process per test file; trailing CLI args such as `--live` are **not forwarded**, so `process.argv` always evaluates `false` under the runner
- `integration-bridge.test.mjs` — canonical reference implementation of the dual-check pattern
- `worker-pool-live.test.mjs` — confirmed compliant with dual-check pattern after Phase 62 fix

**Phase 62 UAT Results (live-confirmed, all runnable SCs passed):**
- SC-1 (stable-PID): PASSED
- SC-2 (cold-pool): confirmed indirectly
- SC-3 (no-spawn-on-direct): PASSED
- SC-4 (escape-hatch): PASSED; warm <3s sanity: PASSED
- SC-5 (cancel-seam via `control_request{interrupt}`): unit-verified only; real-stream termination deferred to Phase 63

**`node --test` output behavior:**
- All test output is buffered and emitted as a batch at test completion, not streamed in real time
- Long-running live tests (>30s) appear hung in CI; this is normal — do not interpret silence as deadlock
- Use `--test-reporter=tap` or direct `node` invocation for real-time output

**Known hang/deadlock patterns:**
- Stdio deadlock: avoid synchronous reads from worker stdout while writing to stdin; use async event-driven patterns only
- Worker slot starvation: pool smaller than concurrent request count causes indefinite queue with no timeout at the queue layer

## Key Files
- `tests/integration/worker-pool-live.test.mjs` — live UAT suite; dual-check gate confirmed
- `tests/integration/integration-bridge.test.mjs` — canonical dual-check reference implementation
- `reference_node_test_argv_live_gate.md` — persistent reference doc for the argv/env-var gate pattern
- `.planning/phases/62-*/62-HUMAN-UAT.md` — Phase 62 live UAT findings and SC evidence

## Usage
- **Direct invocation**: `node tests/integration/worker-pool-live.test.mjs --live`
- **Via `node --test` runner**: `LLM_PROXY_LIVE=1 node --test tests/integration/worker-pool-live.test.mjs`
- Both modes are equivalent; dual-check gate ensures consistent skip/run behavior regardless of invocation path

## Troubleshooting
- **Live tests silently skip under `node --test`**: `LLM_PROXY_LIVE=1` is missing from env; `--live` arg is stripped by the runner and never reaches the test file
- **Output appears frozen**: `node --test` buffers all output; switch to direct `node` invocation for real-time feedback on long-running suites
- **Cancel-seam SC fails**: `control_request{interrupt}` does not terminate real streams; Phase 63 will implement SIGTERM-based cancellation; do not expect interrupt protocol to work in live mode until then

attributes.name: OntologyFilter Component — Unified Viewer
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Provides the Ontology Class filter panel in the Unified Viewer, enabling show/hide of graph nodes by ontological classification in an expandable L0→L1→L2 hierarchy. All L1 classes are independently deselectable; toggling a class removes exactly its declared own-node count from the rendered graph.

## Architecture
**Data layer (backend is always authoritative):**
- API emits the complete hierarchy: 1 L0 root, 3 L1 nodes, 10 L2 nodes (14 total filter items)
- All filter defects are frontend-only; re-probing the API confirms hierarchy shape but cannot diagnose state or rendering bugs

**State model — `[]` sentinel:**
- Empty array `[]` is the sentinel for "all items visible" — never "none selected"
- Per-item checkbox handlers in `OntologyFilter.tsx` correctly expand `[]` to the full 14-item list before adding or removing a specific class — this is the **canonical correct materialization pattern** for all filter components

**Group-level operations (all/none buttons):**
- All/none toggle for the Ontology Class category is handled by `selectGroup`/`deselectGroup` in `FilterRail.tsx`, not in `OntologyFilter.tsx`
- Those handlers bypass `[]` materialization — the group-toggle bug lives in `FilterRail.tsx`; per-item logic in `OntologyFilter.tsx` is correct

## Key Files
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/components/OntologyFilter.tsx` — L0→L1→L2 hierarchy rendering; per-item checkbox state handlers; correct materialization pattern
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/components/FilterRail.tsx` — group-level all/none handlers (`selectGroup`, `deselectGroup`); contains the group-toggle sentinel-bypass bug
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/store/viewer-store.ts` — Zustand store backing all filter state

## Usage
- Rendered as a panel within the Unified Viewer sidebar
- State is read/written directly through `viewer-store.ts`; no local component state for filter visibility
- Per-item materialization in this file is the reference pattern to replicate when fixing `FilterRail.tsx`

## Troubleshooting
- **Per-item checkbox correct but all/none does not work**: bug is in `FilterRail.tsx` `selectGroup`/`deselectGroup`, not in `OntologyFilter.tsx` — do not modify this file to fix group-toggle behavior
- **Hierarchy item count mismatch**: re-probe the API to confirm 14 nodes (1 L0 + 3 L1 + 10 L2); if the API is correct, fault is in frontend rendering or state
- **L1 class not independently deselectable**: verify the class is represented as a distinct member of the 14-item materialized list; check that `[]` expansion in the per-item handler produces all 14 entries

attributes.name: gsd-execute-phase Skill — Phase Execution Orchestration
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Wave-based execution orchestrator for locked, fully-verified GSD phases. Loads per-phase plan artifacts, constructs a dependency-ordered DAG, dispatches isolated sub-agents per plan with fresh context budgets, and enforces pre-execution integrity gates before any sub-agent is spawned. A mandatory pre-execution context reset prevents planning-session state from polluting execution.

## Architecture
**Invocation:** `/gsd-execute-phase [phase] [--wave N] [--gaps-only] [--interactive]`

**Flag parsing — literal token matching only:**

| Flag | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `--wave N` | Execute only wave N (space separator required) |
| `--gaps-only` | Execute only plans with `gap_closure: true` in frontmatter; all others skipped |
| `--interactive` | Interactive execution mode |
| *(no flags)* | Full-phase execution |

Abbreviations (`--gap`) and `=` syntax (`--wave=2`) are silently unrecognized and fall back to full-phase execution.

**Execution sequence — all steps complete before any sub-agent is spawned:**
1. Mandatory pre-execution context reset
2. Load and validate all plan artifacts for the specified phase
3. Construct dependency-ordered DAG from plan frontmatter
4. Run pre-execution integrity gates (see GSD Plan Verification Gate insight)
5. Dispatch sub-agents wave-by-wave per DAG order

## Key Files
- `.planning/phases/[phase]/` — plan artifacts loaded at execution start
- Sub-agent dispatch mechanism — spawns isolated agents per plan with fresh context budgets

## Usage
- Invoked by operator or orchestration layer to execute a locked, gate-verified GSD phase
- Requires all plan artifacts committed to disk and passing the verification gate before invocation
- `--gaps-only` filters to gap-closure plans only; all other plans in the phase are skipped entirely

## Troubleshooting
- **`--wave=2` or `--gap` not recognized**: use `--wave 2` and `--gaps-only` with exact spacing; non-literal forms fall back to full-phase execution silently
- **Sub-agents dispatched before gates pass**: context reset or gate enforcement is misconfigured; gates must complete before any dispatch
- **Wrong plans executing under `--gaps-only`**: verify `gap_closure: true` is set in plan frontmatter for the intended plans

attributes.name: rapid-llm-proxy — Build Process and Repository Structure
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Prevents machine-generated runtime artifacts and unrelated concurrent in-progress work from mixing with hand-edited deliverables in version history. Applies symmetrically to both the `coding` and `rapid-llm-proxy` repositories, keeping each phase's deliverables independently auditable.

## Architecture
Every changeset follows exactly **two logical commit units**, staged and committed separately:

**Commit 1 — Feature deliverables** (hand-edited, intentional decisions):
- Launcher/permissions config: `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
- Source: `performanceSlice.ts`, `timeline.tsx`, `stop-adapter-registry.mjs`
- Proxy implementation: `server.mjs` (target-phase wire-tap hunks only), `token-usage.ts`

**Commit 2 — Chore** (machine-generated): lock files, generated type stubs, compiled output

**Hunk-level staging for concurrent WIP isolation**:
- A single file (e.g., `server.mjs`) routinely contains hunks from multiple concurrent in-flight phases
- Use `git add -p` to stage only the target-phase hunk; leave all other phases' hunks unstaged for independent handling
- A pre-commit `git status` inventory is mandatory to identify all concurrent WIP before any staging begins

**Gitignore enforcement**: `dist/` is gitignored in `rapid-llm-proxy`, preventing compiled output from ever appearing as staging candidates.

## Key Files
- `server.mjs` (rapid-llm-proxy) — proxy implementation; expected to contain concurrent WIP from multiple phases; always stage with `git add -p`, never `git add .`
- `token-usage.ts` (rapid-llm-proxy) — token attribution module; typically a wholly new file per feature phase, safe to stage in full
- `.gitignore` (rapid-llm-proxy) — must include `dist/` to suppress compiled artifact churn from the working tree

## Usage
Applied on every commit in both repositories. Pre-staging checklist: (1) run `git status` to inventory all modified/untracked files, (2) identify current-phase changes vs. other in-flight WIP, (3) use `git add -p` for any file shared across phases, (4) commit feature deliverables first, then chore artifacts as a separate follow-up commit.

## Troubleshooting
- **Unrelated WIP accidentally staged**: `git restore --staged <file>` or `git reset HEAD <file>`; verify with `git diff --cached` before committing
- **Only part of a file belongs to the current phase**: `git add -p <file>` to walk hunks interactively; skip any hunk not belonging to the current phase
- **`dist/` appearing in `git status`**: Add `dist/` to `rapid-llm-proxy/.gitignore` if absent — never stage compiled output
- **Concurrent WIP lost after staging**: Check `git diff` (unstaged changes) and `git stash list`; unstaged hunks survive safely as long as `git checkout -- <file>` or `git clean` is not run
