- **Unrelated WIP accidentally staged**: `git restore --staged <file>` or `git reset HEAD <file>`; verify with `git diff --cached` before committing
- **Only part of a file belongs to the current phase**: `git add -p <file>` to walk hunks interactively; skip any hunk not belonging to the current phase
- **`dist/` appearing in `git status`**: Add `dist/` to `rapid-llm-proxy/.gitignore` if absent — never stage compiled output
- **Concurrent WIP lost after staging**: Check `git diff` (unstaged changes) and `git stash list`; unstaged hunks survive safely as long as `git checkout -- <file>` or `git clean` is not run

attributes.name: System Health Dashboard — Observations Page Polling
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Ensures Radix `TooltipContent` renders within the viewport when tooltip triggers appear inside a Dialog component. Without a Portal escape hatch, the CSS `transform` on Dialog's overlay/container creates a new containing block that breaks Radix's built-in collision detection and viewport-aware repositioning, causing content to spill to the bottom-left of the screen.

## Architecture
- **Root cause**: any ancestor element with CSS `transform` (including Dialog overlays) creates a new containing block; Radix's collision detection assumes `TooltipContent` is positioned relative to the viewport root — this assumption silently fails inside a transformed subtree
- **Fix**: the shared `TooltipContent` primitive wraps content in a `Portal`, mounting it directly under `document.body` and escaping the Dialog's transformed subtree entirely; collision padding is added alongside to provide safe margins from viewport edges
- **Fix scope**: applied once at the shared primitive level — all tooltip-in-dialog usages across the dashboard inherit correct behavior automatically; no per-instance changes are required

## Key Files
- `integrations/system-health-dashboard/src/components/ui/tooltip.tsx` — shared `TooltipContent` primitive; the canonical export containing the Portal wrapper and collision padding configuration

## Usage
Used wherever tooltips appear in the system health dashboard. All dashboard consumers import `TooltipContent` from this shared primitive; the Portal wrapper is transparent to callers. Any future tooltip-in-dialog usage automatically benefits from correct off-screen protection with no additional configuration.

## Troubleshooting
- **Tooltip still renders off-screen**: confirm the `Portal` wrapper is present in `tooltip.tsx`'s `TooltipContent`; inspect the DOM to verify the tooltip node mounts under `<body>` rather than inside the Dialog subtree
- **Off-screen in non-Dialog contexts**: check for other ancestor elements with CSS `transform`, `perspective`, or `will-change: transform` — any of these create a new containing block and trigger the same positioning failure
- **Regression after Radix upgrade**: re-verify that the upgraded `TooltipContent` API still accepts the manual Portal wrapper; newer Radix versions may introduce a first-class `container` or portal prop that should replace the manual wrapper

attributes.name: Coverage Dashboard — Claim-Type Color Semantics
attributes.description:
## Purpose
The Coverage page in `system-health-dashboard` visualizes per-project claim verification status using a strict, unambiguous color-to-state mapping. Tiles deep-link to individual insight records using the native km-core UUID `id` as the canonical public identifier. All tile rendering, legend swatches, project-header badge, and deep-link href logic is co-located in a single file.

## Architecture
- **Single rendering file**: all Coverage page visual logic lives in `src/pages/coverage.tsx` within `integrations/system-health-dashboard/`
- **Canonical tile state → color mapping:**
  - `pending` → grey (verifiable; verifier has not yet run — grey is **reserved exclusively** for this state)
  - `unverifiable` / `no claims` → beige/tan (`totalClaims = 0` or non-repo content); explicit high-contrast Tailwind text/background overrides applied; **intentionally distinct from grey** to prevent visual ambiguity with pending
  - `hallucinated` → distinct non-grey color (claims reference code absent from git HEAD history)
  - `verified` → green/positive color (claims confirmed against current repo state)
- **Deep-link**: tile `href` uses the km-core UUID `id` field as the canonical public insight identifier; 117 insights across projects have been deduplicated to use native UUID keys; `legacyId` must not appear in any deep-link path
- **Refresh behavior**: Coverage "Refresh" re-reads cached insight metadata only; does NOT re-execute the verifier pass

## Key Files
- `integrations/system-health-dashboard/src/pages/coverage.tsx` — all tile rendering, legend swatches, project badge, and deep-link href logic

## Usage
Tile states are derived from stored `metadata.codeVerification` fields in km-core records; the Coverage page does not compute them live. A known pending operator check remains: browser-based end-to-end verification of the Coverage tile → deep-link → correct insight record flow has not yet been visually confirmed.

## Troubleshooting
- Tile shows wrong color → check stored `verificationRatio` and `codeVerification` fields in the km-core record; re-run the verifier pass to update them; "Refresh" alone is insufficient
- Deep-link routes to wrong insight or 404s → verify the tile `href` uses the km-core UUID `id` field, not `legacyId`; confirm the insight record exists with that UUID in km-core
- Grey tile appears for a claim that should be `unverifiable` → check if `totalClaims = 0`; if so it should render beige/tan; inspect Tailwind class overrides in `coverage.tsx`
- To verify the deep-link flow end-to-end, use `gsd-browser` to navigate to the Coverage page, click a tile, and confirm the correct insight record loads

attributes.name: GSD Phase Verification File Integrity
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Binary integrity gate that sits between `gsd-plan-phase` output and `gsd-execute-phase` dispatch. Ensures all plan artifacts are audited for source coverage, structural integrity, verify-command correctness, and wave-level file-overlap safety before any code changes land. Plans either pass (execution proceeds immediately) or enter a correction loop — no artifacts are modified during gate enforcement.

## Architecture
Strict gate sequence — non-negotiable order:
1. `gsd-plan-phase` produces the full plan set; **all plan files must be committed to disk** before the gate runs.
2. `gsd-plan-checker` (sonnet-class sub-agent) audits in a single pass across three criteria:
   - **Source coverage**: every plan cites actual `file:line` references — not improvised or assumed paths.
   - **Plan integrity**: threat models, read-first references, and design constraints present per validity gates.
   - **File-overlap analysis**: plans assigned to different waves must not target the same file.
3. **Pass** → execution dispatches immediately to `gsd-execute-phase`.
4. **Fail** → correction loop: plans flagged for revision; gate re-runs after corrections; no code changes land until gate clears.

## Key Files
- Phase plan artifact files (phase-specific, written to disk by `gsd-plan-phase`) — must all be present before gate runs
- `gsd-plan-checker` sub-agent — sonnet-class; performs the single-pass audit

## Usage
Runs automatically between `gsd-plan-phase` completion and `gsd-execute-phase` dispatch. Not operator-invoked directly. Re-runs automatically after each correction cycle until all three criteria pass.

## Troubleshooting
- **Fails on source coverage**: Plan cites assumed or fabricated paths — run an `explore` sub-agent to find actual `file:line` references.
- **Fails on file-overlap**: Two plans in different waves target the same file — reassign one to the other wave or serialize them.
- **Fails on plan integrity**: Threat model, read-first references, or design constraints missing — add required sections per validity gate spec.
- **Gate runs before plans are on disk**: Verify all plan files are written before gate invocation; check the plan directory with `ls`.

attributes.name: PERF-03 Dashboard Latency Observability
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Delivers median/p50 visibility into `claude-code/sonnet` fallback-path latency on the Token Usage dashboard tile, with threshold-colored badges and per-model row breakdowns. All infrastructure ships and renders correctly. PERF-03 is classified **partial** (not gap): implementation is complete and test-verified; the only unmet criterion is a confirmed design/spec gap between what the threshold was calibrated for and what the dashboard actually measures. Deferred as tech debt at v7.3 closure.

## Architecture
**Infrastructure (all live and rendering correctly):**
- Per-call latency events written to `token-usage.db` (SQLite, proxy-side) by `rapid-llm-proxy`
- Token Usage dashboard tile: median/p50 column, threshold-colored badges, per-model row breakdowns — all functional
- `/api/token-usage/recent` — endpoint surfacing latency records consumed by the dashboard tile

**Threshold/metric mismatch (root cause of PERF-03 partial status):**
- ≤3s green-badge threshold was calibrated for **warm-pool spawn/auth overhead delta** (worker pool eliminates 0–14s of that cost — a real, measurable speedup)
- Dashboard actually measures **total end-to-end latency**, dominated by LLM generation time — not spawn cost
- Real-traffic `claude-code/sonnet` medians: **~123s** (observed range: 20–261s); generation noise completely swamps the pool's overhead savings
- Worker pool speedup is genuine but **orthogonal** to total-latency measurements; the two metrics are independent
- UAT result: **0 passed / 2 failed** (both tests against `/api/token-usage/recent`); root cause is design/spec gap, not a rendering bug

**Resolution options (deferred):**
- **Option A**: Recalibrate threshold to reflect total-latency reality (green band at ~120s+)
- **Option B**: Redefine measured metric to worker-pool overhead delta only (measure warm vs. cold call delta, not total duration)

## Key Files
- `.planning/phases/66-dashboard-latency-observability/66-HUMAN-UAT.md` — UAT session record with both failed test cases, observed latency data, and full root-cause analysis
- `token-usage.db` — SQLite store for per-call latency events (proxy-side, written by `rapid-llm-proxy`)
- `/api/token-usage/recent` — API endpoint surfacing latency data to the dashboard tile

## Usage
- Dashboard tile auto-renders on the Token Usage page; `/api/token-usage/recent` is polled by the frontend
- PERF-03 acceptance re-evaluation is deferred to a future milestone; a user decision is required on which metric the badge should target before acceptance criteria can be written

## Troubleshooting
- **"Badge tests fail even though tile renders"** → confirm which metric the badge threshold is calibrated for; ≤3s is only valid for warm-pool overhead delta, not total E2E latency
- **"Worker pool speedup not visible in dashboard"** → expected behavior; pool eliminates spawn/auth overhead (0–14s) but total latency is dominated by generation time (~123s median); these are separate, non-comparable metrics
- **"How to re-evaluate PERF-03"** → decision required before writing new acceptance criteria: choose Option A (reset threshold ≥120s) or Option B (redefine metric to overhead delta); both require a new phase
- **"Tile median regression signal is ambiguous"** → explicitly disable the worker pool to get a clean cold-path baseline before reading the tile median as a regression signal

attributes.name: ClaudeWorker and WorkerPool — rapid-llm-proxy Worker Pool Architecture
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Replaces per-call `claude` CLI spawns in `rapid-llm-proxy` with a pool of persistent `ClaudeWorker` subprocesses communicating over newline-delimited JSON stdio. Reduces spawn overhead and enables context reuse across requests through LRU prompt-pool caching. Wired into `server.mjs` via a surgical dispatcher edit alongside the existing provider fallback chain.

## Architecture
**`ClaudeWorker` (subprocess wrapper):**
- Persistent process wrapping the Claude CLI; bidirectional newline-delimited JSON stdio
- **Per-request timeout (CR-01) is mandatory**: prevents a hung subprocess from permanently blocking a worker slot; every dispatched request must carry an independent timeout guard

**`WorkerPool` (router):**
- Lazy-spawn: worker instances created on first demand, not at pool init (WLIFE-01 — cold-start live test still pending)
- **GUARD-01 escape hatch — two-layer enforcement**: `LLM_PROXY_DISABLE_WORKER_POOL` is checked at both the dispatcher level and a secondary enforcement point; either check can disable the pool independently
- LRU prompt-pool caching for context reuse across requests

**Lifecycle states (WLIFE-01..04):** fully documented in the lifecycle state-machine diagram:
- WLIFE-01: lazy spawn on first demand
- WLIFE-02..04: subsequent in-flight and teardown transitions (see lifecycle diagram for full sequence)

**Integration:** wired into `server.mjs` via a surgical dispatcher edit alongside — not replacing — the existing provider fallback chain (see rapid-llm-proxy Provider Fallback Chain insight)

**Architecture diagrams (style-guide conforming):**
- `docs/puml/claude-worker-pool-architecture.puml` — two-tier dispatch + pool internals; PlantUML note: `Map<key, ClaudeWorker[]>` in component labels requires the quoted label form in source
- `docs/puml/claude-worker-pool-lifecycle.puml` — state-machine sequence covering WLIFE-01..04
- Both cross-referenced from `docs/puml/llm-cli-proxy-architecture.puml` (current v7.3 proxy architecture state)

## Key Files
- `rapid-llm-proxy/proxy-bridge/server.mjs` — integration point; surgical dispatcher edit; GUARD-01 check lives here
- `docs/puml/claude-worker-pool-architecture.puml` — architecture reference diagram source
- `docs/puml/claude-worker-pool-lifecycle.puml` — lifecycle state-machine reference diagram source
- `docs/images/claude-worker-pool-architecture.png` — rendered architecture PNG (~169 KB)
- `docs/images/claude-worker-pool-lifecycle.png` — rendered lifecycle PNG (~169 KB)

## Usage
Active in rapid-llm-proxy as the primary Claude-CLI dispatcher. The integration test suite (see Worker-Pool Integration Tests insight) governs live-mode gating via the dual-check pattern (`process.argv` + `LLM_PROXY_LIVE` env var). The GUARD-01 escape hatch allows operators to disable the pool and revert to per-call spawn mode without code changes.

## Troubleshooting
- **Hung worker slot**: CR-01 per-request timeout not set — mandatory on every call path; add an independent timeout guard to the dispatched request
- **Cold-start failure at WLIFE-01**: lazy-spawn path is verify-only at this stage; cold-start live test is pending; diagnose by checking for subprocess spawn errors in proxy logs
- **Disable worker pool**: set `LLM_PROXY_DISABLE_WORKER_POOL` env var before starting the proxy — checked at two enforcement layers; falls back to per-call spawn immediately
- **Diagram PlantUML parse error**: `Map<key, ClaudeWorker[]>` bare in a component label breaks angle-bracket parsing; use quoted label form in `.puml` source (see Documentation Diagram Style Guide insight)

attributes.name: GSD complete-milestone Workflow
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Formally closes a GSD milestone after all phases and human UAT are complete. Archives phase planning artifacts into versioned milestone records, collapses the active roadmap, deletes the active requirements file for a clean slate, records deferred cross-milestone debt in `STATE.md`, updates `PROJECT.md`, and creates a canonical git tag. All irreversible operations are gated behind a mandatory pre-flight audit verification step.

## Architecture
**Invocation**: `/gsd-complete-milestone v{version}` — `mode: yolo` suppresses per-step confirmation prompts; `create_tag=true` enables git tag creation (silently skipped if absent).

**8-step strictly ordered execution sequence (steps 5–8 are irreversible):**
1. **Audit status verification** — reads `.planning/v{version}-MILESTONE-AUDIT.md`
   - Absent audit file → **hard stop**; redirect to `/gsd-audit-milestone`

attributes.name: GSD v7.3 Milestone State
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Permanent reference record for GSD v7.3 milestone scope, closure outcomes, and phase index constraints. v7.3 covered LLM Proxy Performance — replacing per-call `claude` CLI spawns with a persistent worker pool to reduce steady-state latency from ~10–14 s to ~2–3 s. **Status: Archived and fully closed.** Phase index boundary (indices ≤ 66 permanently reserved) must be enforced in all future planning.

## Architecture
- **Milestone record**: `.planning/PROJECT.md` — v7.3 archived; v7.4 succeeded it, v7.5 is now active
- **Phase range**: Phases 62–66 exclusively v7.3; indices ≤ 66 must never be reused for new work
- **Archive artifacts produced at closure**:
  - `.planning/milestones/` — versioned copies of `ROADMAP.md` and `REQUIREMENTS.md` at closure time
  - Active `ROADMAP.md` — collapsed to one-line summary entries with links into `.planning/milestones/`
  - Active `REQUIREMENTS.md` — deleted at closure to provide a clean slate for v7.4
  - `PROJECT.md` — updated with accomplishments sourced from phases 62–66 `SUMMARY.md` files

## Key Files
- `.planning/PROJECT.md` — milestone-level log; v7.3 entry is archived here
- `.planning/milestones/` — versioned milestone snapshots
- `.planning/phases/62–66/` — v7.3 phase artifacts (read-only historical record)

## Usage
Consulted when: (a) verifying phase index allocations for new phases, (b) auditing the worker-pool architecture introduced in v7.3, or (c) tracing the provenance of latency-reduction infrastructure used downstream.

## Troubleshooting
- New phase accidentally assigned index ≤ 66: renumber immediately — these indices are permanently reserved and must not be reused.
- Archived milestone data missing from `PROJECT.md`: check `.planning/milestones/` for the versioned snapshot taken at v7.3 closure.

attributes.name: GSD audit-milestone Workflow
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Pre-closure orchestrator that formally assesses a milestone's definition of done by tracing all requirements to implementation evidence, running cross-phase integration checks, assessing open tech debt, and writing a structured audit report. Its output artifact is the mandatory input consumed by `complete-milestone`'s step-1 pre-flight gate — the milestone cannot be closed without it.

## Architecture
Execution sequence (strict order):
1. Load all phase `VERIFICATION.md` files across the milestone's phase range
2. Map each requirement to its implementing phase(s) and evidence source
3. **Temporal gap detection**: compare completed plans against the last integration pass; if gap-closure plans were added after the prior audit, conditionally spawn a `gsd-integration-checker` sub-agent to validate new value chains end-to-end
4. Assess open tech debt items — both pre-existing and milestone-generated
5. Write the structured audit report artifact

## Key Files
- `{phase}/VERIFICATION.md` — per-phase evidence files consumed in step 1
- `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md` — requirements traced in step 2
- Audit report artifact — written to the milestone's planning directory; exact filename set by the orchestrator at runtime

## Usage
Run once per milestone, after all phases in scope are executed and verified. The resulting report is a required input to `complete-milestone` step 1; attempting closure without it fails the pre-flight gate. If new gap-closure plans were added post-audit, re-run to trigger the integration-checker sub-agent.

## Troubleshooting
- `complete-milestone` pre-flight fails "missing audit report": run `/gsd-audit-milestone` first and confirm the report artifact is committed.
- Integration-checker sub-agent not spawned when expected: confirm gap-closure plans have `gap_closure: true` in frontmatter and their timestamps post-date the prior audit.
- Requirement mapped to wrong phase: cross-check `VERIFICATION.md` evidence — re-run if phase summaries were updated after the last audit.

attributes.name: Git Commit Staging — Config vs Runtime Artifact Separation
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Prevents machine-generated runtime artifacts and unrelated concurrent in-progress work from mixing with hand-edited deliverables in version history. Applies symmetrically to both the `coding` and `rapid-llm-proxy` repositories, keeping each phase's deliverables independently auditable.

## Architecture
Every changeset follows exactly **two logical commit units**, staged and committed separately:

**Commit 1 — Feature deliverables** (hand-edited, intentional decisions):
- Launcher/permissions config: `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
- Source: `performanceSlice.ts`, `timeline.tsx`, `stop-adapter-registry.mjs`
- Proxy implementation: `server.mjs` (target-phase wire-tap hunks only), `token-usage.ts`

**Commit 2 — Chore** (machine-generated): lock files, generated type stubs, compiled output

**Hunk-level staging for concurrent WIP isolation**:
- A single file (e.g., `server.mjs`) routinely contains hunks from multiple concurrent in-flight phases
- Use `git add -p` to stage only the target-phase hunk; leave all other phases' hunks unstaged for independent handling
- A pre-commit `git status` inventory is mandatory to identify all concurrent WIP before any staging begins

**Gitignore enforcement**: `dist/` is gitignored in `rapid-llm-proxy`, preventing compiled output from ever appearing as staging candidates.

## Key Files
- `server.mjs` (rapid-llm-proxy) — proxy implementation; expected to contain concurrent WIP from multiple phases; always stage with `git add -p`, never `git add .`
- `token-usage.ts` (rapid-llm-proxy) — token attribution module; typically a wholly new file per feature phase, safe to stage in full
- `.gitignore` (rapid-llm-proxy) — must include `dist/` to suppress compiled artifact churn from the working tree

## Usage
Applied on every commit in both repositories. Pre-staging checklist: (1) run `git status` to inventory all modified/untracked files, (2) identify current-phase changes vs. other in-flight WIP, (3) use `git add -p` for any file shared across phases, (4) commit feature deliverables first, then chore artifacts as a separate follow-up commit.

## Troubleshooting
- **Unrelated WIP accidentally staged**: `git restore --staged <file>` or `git reset HEAD <file>`; verify with `git diff --cached` before committing
- **Only part of a file belongs to the current phase**: `git add -p <file>` to walk hunks interactively; skip any hunk not belonging to the current phase
- **`dist/` appearing in `git status`**: Add `dist/` to `rapid-llm-proxy/.gitignore` if absent — never stage compiled output
- **Concurrent WIP lost after staging**: Check `git diff` (unstaged changes) and `git stash list`; unstaged hunks survive safely as long as `git checkout -- <file>` or `git clean` is not run

attributes.name: System Health Dashboard — Observations Page
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Renders live observation data using a dual-mechanism fetch strategy: a 30-second polling interval for regular background refresh, and a visibility-change event listener that fires an immediate refetch when the browser tab regains focus. Together these prevent the stale-data failure mode where polling alone would leave the page showing outdated data after a period of tab inactivity.

## Architecture
- **30-second polling loop**: interval-based refresh runs continuously while the page is mounted; provides the baseline data-freshness guarantee.
- **Visibility-change focus-refetch handler**: listens for `document.visibilityState` transitions; fires an immediate out-of-cycle refetch when the page transitions from `hidden` → `visible`; operates independently and does not reset or interrupt the running polling interval.
- Both mechanisms are co-registered in `observations.tsx` and run in tandem throughout the full page lifecycle.
- The two mechanisms are intentionally independent: the focus-refetch fires immediately on tab focus; the 30-second polling interval continues on its own schedule regardless.

## Key Files
- `observations.tsx` — page component; co-registers both the 30-second polling interval and the `visibilitychange` event listener

## Usage
Displayed in the System Health Dashboard UI. Automatically keeps observation data fresh during active use, and immediately refreshes stale data whenever the user returns to the tab.

## Troubleshooting
- If data appears stale after returning to the tab, verify the `visibilitychange` event listener is registered in `observations.tsx` and that it fires a fetch on `hidden` → `visible` transitions.
- If the polling interval stops after a tab-focus event, confirm the focus-refetch handler does not inadvertently cancel or reset the polling interval — they must be independent.
- Simultaneous firing of both mechanisms on tab focus is expected behavior and not a bug.

attributes.name: GSD v7.4 Milestone State
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Documents confirmed caching behavior per agent backend and the resulting measurement asymmetry in the performance dashboard. Cache metadata availability varies structurally by backend — not all zero-cache observations are capture gaps. Defines reconciliation requirements across the proxy capture layer, token-adapter ingestion, and dashboard query layer before cross-agent cache comparisons are valid.

## Architecture
**`cache_read` token semantic:**
- `cache_read` tokens are re-transmitted over the wire on every API call — the full cached prefix is always included in the request body.
- Provider billing is ~0.1× because Anthropic caches the *computation* (KV prefix cache keyed on prefix content hash), not the byte transmission.
- This is a provider-side computation cache, not a data-transmission optimization.

**Per-agent measurement status:**

| Agent | Cache Capture | Route | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude | Full (reads + writes per turn) | Wire-tap at `/v1/messages` | Confirmed |
| Other agents | Status varies | — | Full per-agent table partially confirmed; consult active investigation for non-Claude agents |

- **Three-layer reconciliation requirement**: Proxy capture layer → token-adapter ingestion → dashboard query layer must all be aligned before cross-agent cache comparisons are trustworthy.

## Key Files
- Proxy capture layer (path not confirmed) — wire-taps `/v1/messages` for Claude agent token metadata.
- Token adapter (path not confirmed) — ingests captured metadata into the dashboard data store.
- Dashboard query layer — surfaces per-agent cache data; asymmetry is visible here first.

## Usage
Consulted when diagnosing zero-cache observations in the performance dashboard. Determines whether a zero value reflects a genuine cache miss, a capture gap, or a structural measurement limitation for a given backend. Required reading before drawing cross-agent cache performance conclusions.

## Troubleshooting
- **Zero cache values for Claude agent**: Likely a genuine cache miss or proxy capture gap — check wire-tap at `/v1/messages` is active and capturing metadata for the session in question.
- **Zero cache values for non-Claude agents**: May be structural (backend does not expose cache metadata) rather than a capture gap — confirm per-agent measurement status before investigating further.
- **Cross-agent cache comparisons appear inconsistent**: Reconcile all three layers (proxy, adapter, query) before drawing conclusions; asymmetry is by design for backends that do not expose cache metadata.

attributes.name: Mastracode — Model Selection and Provider Configuration
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Controls which LLM model and provider Mastracode routes requests through at session initialization. Four independent, silent failure modes can cause requests to bypass `rapid-proxy-mastra` and fall through to OpenAI (`openai/gpt-5.5`) or Anthropic built-in OAuth paths. The canonical fix requires registering a custom *model pack* — not merely a custom provider — and ensuring `modeDefaults`, `activeModelPackId`, and `customModelPacks` all align in `settings.json`.

## Architecture
**Runtime selection hierarchy (highest → lowest precedence):**
1. `modeDefaults` in `settings.json` — the only reliable persistence mechanism
2. `activeModelPackId` + `customModelPacks` registration in `settings.json`
3. `MASTRACODE_MODEL_ID` env var — transient hint only; overridden whenever `modeDefaults` is empty
4. Bundle hardcoded `defaultModelId` — `openai/gpt-5.5` at bundle lines 2167/2212 for "build" mode, activated via the `LEGACY_VARIED_MODELS` fallback path

**Four silent failure modes:**
1. **Wrong env var name** — `MASTRA_MODEL` is ignored; correct name is `MASTRACODE_MODEL_ID`
2. **Empty models array** — custom provider with `models: []` is silently skipped by `parseCustomProviders` during initialization; `getCustomProviderId` never returns it
3. **Env var override** — even with the correct env var set, an empty `modeDefaults` triggers `LEGACY_VARIED_MODELS`, applying the bundle's hardcoded `defaultModelId`
4. **`/models` command silent overwrite** — selecting any built-in pack (Anthropic/OpenAI) via `/models` calls `getAvailableModePacks()`, which surfaces only built-in packs and **silently overwrites both `modeDefaults` and `activeModelPackId`**, clearing all custom proxy configuration

**Custom model pack shape** (correct registration in `settings.json`):
```json
{
  "customModelPacks": [
    { "name": "RapidProxyMastra", "models": { "build": "rapid-proxy-mastra/claude-haiku-4-5", "plan": "...", "fast": "..." }, "createdAt": "..." }
  ],
  "activeModelPackId": "custom:RapidProxyMastra",
  "modeDefaults": { "build": "rapid-proxy-mastra/claude-haiku-4-5" }
}
```
All three fields must be co-present and consistent; a mismatch in any one silently falls through to a lower-precedence path.

## Key Files
- `/Users/<USER_ID_REDACTED>/Agentic/coding/config/agents/mastra.sh` — exports `MASTRACODE_MODEL_ID` and populates the `rapid-proxy-mastra` provider's `models` array; env var alone is insufficient without `modeDefaults`
- `settings.json` — authoritative config; contains `modeDefaults`, `activeModelPackId`, and `customModelPacks`; all three must be aligned
- Mastracode bundle lines 2167/2212 — hardcoded `defaultModelId: "openai/gpt-5.5"` for "build" mode; activated via `LEGACY_VARIED_MODELS` fallback whenever `modeDefaults` is absent

## Usage
Mastracode reads `settings.json` at session startup to determine the active model pack and per-mode defaults. The `/models` slash command updates `modeDefaults` **only within the context of the currently active pack** — if a built-in pack is active or selected, `/models` will silently replace custom settings.

**Correct setup order:**
1. Add the custom model pack entry to `customModelPacks` in `settings.json`
2. Set `activeModelPackId: "custom:RapidProxyMastra"`
3. Set `modeDefaults` to match the pack's model assignments for each mode
4. Ensure `mastra.sh` exports `MASTRACODE_MODEL_ID` with a non-empty `models` array for the `rapid-proxy-mastra` provider

## Troubleshooting
- **Requests routing to `openai/gpt-5.5`** — `modeDefaults` is empty; `LEGACY_VARIED_MODELS` fallback applied the bundle's hardcoded default. Check and repopulate all three `settings.json` fields.
- **Requests routing through Anthropic OAuth instead of proxy** — a built-in Anthropic pack was selected via `/models`, silently clearing `activeModelPackId` and `modeDefaults`; must re-register the custom pack and reset all three fields.
- **Custom provider not appearing at startup** — confirm `models` array in the `rapid-proxy-mastra` provider block in `mastra.sh` is non-empty; an empty array causes `parseCustomProviders` to skip it entirely.

metadata.topic: Mastracode — Model Selection and Provider Configuration
metadata.summary:
## Purpose
Controls which LLM model and provider Mastracode routes requests through at session initialization. Four independent, silent failure modes can cause requests to bypass `rapid-proxy-mastra` and fall through to OpenAI (`openai/gpt-5.5`) or Anthropic built-in OAuth paths. The canonical fix requires registering a custom *model pack* — not merely a custom provider — and ensuring `modeDefaults`, `activeModelPackId`, and `customModelPacks` all align in `settings.json`.

## Architecture
**Runtime selection hierarchy (highest → lowest precedence):**
1. `modeDefaults` in `settings.json` — the only reliable persistence mechanism
2. `activeModelPackId` + `customModelPacks` registration in `settings.json`
3. `MASTRACODE_MODEL_ID` env var — transient hint only; overridden whenever `modeDefaults` is empty
4. Bundle hardcoded `defaultModelId` — `openai/gpt-5.5` at bundle lines 2167/2212 for "build" mode, activated via the `LEGACY_VARIED_MODELS` fallback path

**Four silent failure modes:**
1. **Wrong env var name** — `MASTRA_MODEL` is ignored; correct name is `MASTRACODE_MODEL_ID`
2. **Empty models array** — custom provider with `models: []` is silently skipped by `parseCustomProviders` during initialization; `getCustomProviderId` never returns it
3. **Env var override** — even with the correct env var set, an empty `modeDefaults` triggers `LEGACY_VARIED_MODELS`, applying the bundle's hardcoded `defaultModelId`
4. **`/models` command silent overwrite** — selecting any built-in pack (Anthropic/OpenAI) via `/models` calls `getAvailableModePacks()`, which surfaces only built-in packs and **silently overwrites both `modeDefaults` and `activeModelPackId`**, clearing all custom proxy configuration

**Custom model pack shape** (correct registration in `settings.json`):
```json
{
  "customModelPacks": [
    { "name": "RapidProxyMastra", "models": { "build": "rapid-proxy-mastra/claude-haiku-4-5", "plan": "...", "fast": "..." }, "createdAt": "..." }
  ],
  "activeModelPackId": "custom:RapidProxyMastra",
  "modeDefaults": { "build": "rapid-proxy-mastra/claude-haiku-4-5" }
}
```
All three fields must be co-present and consistent; a mismatch in any one silently falls through to a lower-precedence path.

## Key Files
- `/Users/<USER_ID_REDACTED>/Agentic/coding/config/agents/mastra.sh` — exports `MASTRACODE_MODEL_ID` and populates the `rapid-proxy-mastra` provider's `models` array; env var alone is insufficient without `modeDefaults`
- `settings.json` — authoritative config; contains `modeDefaults`, `activeModelPackId`, and `customModelPacks`; all three must be aligned
- Mastracode bundle lines 2167/2212 — hardcoded `defaultModelId: "openai/gpt-5.5"` for "build" mode; activated via `LEGACY_VARIED_MODELS` fallback whenever `modeDefaults` is absent

## Usage
Mastracode reads `settings.json` at session startup to determine the active model pack and per-mode defaults. The `/models` slash command updates `modeDefaults` **only within the context of the currently active pack** — if a built-in pack is active or selected, `/models` will silently replace custom settings.

**Correct setup order:**
1. Add the custom model pack entry to `customModelPacks` in `settings.json`
2. Set `activeModelPackId: "custom:RapidProxyMastra"`
3. Set `modeDefaults` to match the pack's model assignments for each mode
4. Ensure `mastra.sh` exports `MASTRACODE_MODEL_ID` with a non-empty `models` array for the `rapid-proxy-mastra` provider

## Troubleshooting
- **Requests routing to `openai/gpt-5.5`** — `modeDefaults` is empty; `LEGACY_VARIED_MODELS` fallback applied the bundle's hardcoded default. Check and repopulate all three `settings.json` fields.
- **Requests routing through Anthropic OAuth instead of proxy** — a built-in Anthropic pack was selected via `/models`, silently clearing `activeModelPackId` and `modeDefaults`; must re-register the custom pack and reset all three fields.
- **Custom provider not appearing at startup** — confirm `models` array in the `rapid-proxy-mastra` provider block in `mastra.sh` is non-empty; an empty array causes `parseCustomProviders` to skip it entirely.
- **Env var not taking effect** — `MASTRACODE_MODEL_ID` is transient; it is bypassed whenever `modeDefaults` is non-empty or the `LEGACY_VARIED_MODELS` path fires. Do not rely on it as the sole configuration mechanism.
- **Verification** — send a minimal test message ("Hi!") and inspect the provider field in the response metadata to confirm routing; cross-check `settings.json` for all three alignment fields.

attributes.name: Token Aggregator Experiment
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Read-only parameterized token aggregation utility over `rapid-llm-proxy`'s `token-usage.db` SQLite database. Enables safe, lock-free querying of total token consumption and call counts attributed to a specific task ID, without competing with the live proxy for write access.

## Architecture
- Single exported function: `aggregateByTaskId(taskId, dbPathOverride?)`
- `readonly=true` enforced at DB open time — the module never acquires write locks; safe to run concurrently with a live `rapid-llm-proxy` instance
- Queries `token_usage` rows where `task_id` matches the supplied argument; returns aggregate token count and call count
- Graceful zero-return when the target DB file does not exist — treated as a non-error condition by design
- Optional `dbPathOverride` parameter decouples the module from the default DB path for test isolation
- Lives under `lib/experiments/` — scoped as an experiment-phase utility, not a production library export

## Key Files
- `lib/experiments/token-aggregator.js` (or equivalent) — main module; exports `aggregateByTaskId`
- `token-usage.db` — SQLite database maintained by `rapid-llm-proxy`; this module accesses it read-only

## Usage
- Called with a `taskId` string to retrieve total token consumption and call count for that task
- `dbPathOverride` parameter used in tests to point at a fixture database instead of the live proxy DB
- Not exposed as a public API — internal to experiment-phase work only

## Troubleshooting
- **Returns zero unexpectedly**: Verify `task_id` values in `token-usage.db` match the supplied argument exactly (case-sensitive); confirm the proxy has written at least one record; use `dbPathOverride` to point explicitly at the live DB path if the default path resolution is suspect
- **DB lock contention**: Should not occur given `readonly=true`; if observed, another process is opening the DB in exclusive mode — identify and correct it
- **DB file not found**: Returns zero gracefully — not an error condition; verify `rapid-llm-proxy` has been run and has written token records before querying

attributes.name: Experiment Store & Ontology Foundation
attributes.description:
## Purpose
The `/api/experiments/runs` endpoint exposes run metadata for run-selection dropdowns and comparison panels. The human-readable goal sentence is derived during LLM judging and stored on the run entity as `e.description`, but only surfaces in API responses when explicitly included in the `query.mjs` entity projection.

## Architecture
- During LLM judging (`judge.mjs`), goal text is read from archived spans and written onto the run entity as `e.description`
- `query.mjs` controls which fields of the run entity are projected into the API response; without an explicit `e.description` projection, the endpoint returns only `task_hash`, `task_id`, `score`, and related numeric/identifier fields — no goal text
- The `goal_sentence` identifier exists exclusively inside `judge.mjs` archival and scoring logic; it does not propagate automatically to the query layer
- **Fix:** `e.description` must be explicitly added to the run entity projection in `query.mjs` to surface goal text in API responses
- The `goal_achieved` numeric score and the goal sentence are independent fields; the score can be present even when the sentence is absent

## Key Files
- `lib/experiments/judge.mjs` — LLM judging; reads goal text from archived spans, writes to run entity as `e.description`
- `lib/experiments/query.mjs` — run entity projection; controls all fields returned by `/api/experiments/runs`; `e.description` must be explicitly declared here

## Usage
- Consumed by run-selection dropdowns and comparison panels in the performance dashboard
- Goal sentence enables human-readable labeling of runs alongside the numeric `goal_achieved` score
- Called at dashboard load and when users navigate to run-selection or comparison views

## Troubleshooting
- **Goal text absent from UI but numeric score present:** `e.description` is missing from the entity projection in `query.mjs` — add it
- **No `goal` field in API response at all:** expected behavior before the projection fix; verify `query.mjs` includes `e.description`
- **502 on `/api/experiments/runs`:** upstream proxy/server issue; confirm `vkb-server` is running before diagnosing field projection logic
- **`goal_sentence` grep returns no query-layer results:** correct — the identifier is confined to `judge.mjs`; the projected field name in `query.mjs` and the API is `e.description` (or its mapped output key)

attributes.name: GSD Multi-Worktree Merge Procedure
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Repeatable procedure for merging multiple parallel worktree branches into `main` after a GSD phase wave completes. Enforces wave atomicity (no partial-wave merges), validates committed completion signals before granting merge eligibility, and prevents uncommitted worktree changes from being silently lost during merge.

## Architecture

**Wave atomicity constraint:**
- All plans in a wave must pass self-checks before any branch is merged — no partial-wave merges permitted
- A single failing self-check holds the entire wave; fix in the branch's worktree, re-verify, then resume
- A fully verified plan may be isolated as "eligible for merge" while awaiting remaining plans — wave atomicity holds as long as all plans complete before the wave closes; sequential merges within a wave are valid

**Completion signal — committed `SUMMARY.md` is the canonical readiness indicator:**
- A `SUMMARY.md` present on disk but **not committed** is NOT a valid completion signal — file existence alone is insufficient
- The commit must be visible on the executor's worktree branch (`git log --oneline <branch>`) before merge eligibility is granted

**Backstop monitoring pattern (canonical synchronization mechanism):**
- For each parallel executor in a wave, a monitor is armed on that executor's worktree branch specifically to detect committed `SUMMARY.md` files
- The backstop provides a **guaranteed** completion signal independent of agent-return notifications; agent-return events are treated as potentially unreliable and must never be the sole completion indicator
- The orchestrator does not advance to the next wave (or trigger post-wave merges) until **all** executors in the current wave have committed their `SUMMARY.md`, as confirmed by the backstop — not by agent-return events
- This ensures safe synchronization across parallel executors even when one or more agent-return events are dropped or delayed

**Merge execution:**
- Each eligible branch is merged to `main` after full wave completion is confirmed via backstop
- Uncommitted worktree changes are silently discarded at merge time — verify clean worktree state before merging

## Key Files
- `.planning/STATE.md` — canonical current-phase pointer; updated only by the phase close-out protocol
- `.planning/ROADMAP.md` — phase registry; never modified during plan execution
- `{phase}/{plan}-SUMMARY.md` — per-plan completion signal; must be committed to the plan's worktree branch, not merely written to disk

## Usage
Invoked by the GSD `claude` orchestrator after all executors in a wave are dispatched. The orchestrator arms one backstop monitor per executor worktree branch before yielding. Wave-N merge is unblocked immediately once all Wave-N SUMMARY.md commits are detected; Wave-N+1 spawns follow the merge.

## Troubleshooting
- **Wave appears done but orchestrator has not advanced**: check whether each executor's `SUMMARY.md` is actually committed — `git log --oneline <branch>` must show the commit, not just `git status`
- **Backstop not firing**: confirm the monitor targets the correct branch per executor; branch name must match the executor plan ID exactly (e.g., `77-02`, `77-03`)
- **Partial-wave merge made in error**: revert the merged commit from `main`, restore the branch, and re-run the full wave after all plans pass self-checks
- **Uncommitted worktree changes at merge time**: run `git status` in every worktree before issuing merge commands; stage and commit or stash anything relevant first

attributes.name: Health Coordinator — Proxy Watchdog
attributes.description:
## Purpose
`scripts/health-coordinator.js` is the central watchdog daemon that monitors the `llm-cli-proxy` service and triggers automatic restarts when the proxy becomes stale after network transitions. Eliminates manual intervention for the common case of a network switch leaving the proxy in a degraded state. The proxy can also stop independently — including during acceptance testing runs — and does not always self-recover; when this occurs, diagnostic verification must precede any resumption of forward development work.

## Architecture
- **Network-switch detection**: Monitors network state transitions; on detection, evaluates whether the `llm-cli-proxy` process has become stale and issues a restart command if staleness is confirmed.
- **Auto-restart sequence**: Proxy self-recovers without user action after a detected network switch; the restart incurs a measurable **kickstart window** before the proxy is fully responsive again.
- **Kickstart window constraint**: Downstream services (e.g., `ObservationWriter` retry budget) must be calibrated to span this window, or writes are silently dropped during restart transitions.
- **Independent failure mode**: The proxy can stop outside of network-switch events (e.g., during acceptance testing). In this mode, the watchdog may not auto-recover; the service must be manually diagnosed and restarted before any dependent workflows resume.
- **Diagnostic-first protocol**: When resuming development after a detected proxy outage, service health verification is the mandatory first step — proceeding to implementation before the proxy is confirmed healthy risks further data loss or cascading failures.

## Key Files
- `scripts/health-coordinator.js` — watchdog daemon; contains network-switch detection, proxy liveness evaluation, and auto-restart sequencing.

## Usage
Runs as a background daemon. All services routing LLM calls through `llm-cli-proxy` depend on this watchdog for uptime continuity. The proxy is a hard dependency for: observation consolidation (`ObservationConsolidator`), observation writing (`ObservationWriter`), and any agent workflow that issues LLM completions.

## Troubleshooting
- **Proxy stopped during acceptance testing**: Do not resume forward development work until proxy state is confirmed healthy. Run diagnostic verification of the `llm-cli-proxy` service first, then restart if needed, and wait for the kickstart window to complete before proceeding.
- **Proxy stale after network switch**: The health coordinator should auto-detect and restart automatically. If it does not, manually trigger a restart and allow the kickstart window to elapse before testing downstream connectivity.
- **Kickstart window — downstream write failures**: If `ObservationWriter` drops records after a proxy restart, the retry budget is undersized relative to the kickstart window. Increase the retry count × delay product to fully span the restart interval.
- **Confirming proxy state**: Check the process list for the `llm-cli-proxy` process and validate with a test completion request to the proxy endpoint before marking recovery complete.

attributes.name: gsd-discuss-phase Skill — Phase Context Document Authoring
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Facilitates structured consultation to lock implementation decisions for a target phase before any planning begins. Scouts existing code surfaces and prior-phase patterns, surfaces undecided integration areas ("gray areas") for progressive resolution, and writes `{phase}-CONTEXT.md` with all decisions anchored to `file:line` references. Prevents `gsd-plan-phase`, `gsd-phase-researcher`, and `gsd-planner` from re-litigating already-resolved questions or producing assumption-based recommendations.

## Architecture
- **Invocation**: `/gsd-discuss-phase [phase]` — optional `--power` flag activates enhanced scouting mode for deeper codebase analysis
- **Workflow file**: `~/.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/discuss-phase.md` — lazy-loaded on demand; must be loaded in full before any action; enforces defined consultation steps rather than improvised behavior
- **Mode detection**: queries `gsd-sdk` (`gsd-sdk query config-get workflow.discuss_mode`) to determine scouting depth before beginning consultation
- **Gray area resolution**: undecided integration points are surfaced iteratively; each gray area is resolved and anchored before proceeding to the next
- **Output**: `{phase}-CONTEXT.md` — all implementation decisions anchored to `file:line` references; treated as immutable by all downstream GSD skills

## Key Files
- `~/.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/discuss-phase.md` — workflow definition governing consultation steps; must be loaded before any consultation action
- `{phase}-CONTEXT.md` — output artifact; locked decision document consumed as the sole authoritative source by `gsd-plan-phase`

## Usage
- First mandatory step in the GSD phase workflow; `gsd-plan-phase` must not be invoked until this document is written and locked
- `--power` flag recommended for phases with significant new code surfaces, cross-phase dependencies, or large numbers of unresolved gray areas
- Once locked, `{phase}-CONTEXT.md` is read-only; downstream skills treat it as immutable

## Troubleshooting
- **Planning produces assumption-based recommendations**: `{phase}-CONTEXT.md` is missing or incomplete; re-run `gsd-discuss-phase` to completion before invoking planning
- **Gray areas re-litigated during planning**: `gsd-plan-phase` did not load `{phase}-CONTEXT.md`; verify the file exists, is non-empty, and is referenced at the start of the planning invocation
- **Workflow file not loaded error**: `discuss-phase.md` must be fully loaded before any consultation step begins; confirm `~/.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/discuss-phase.md` is present and accessible

attributes.name: Route-Trace Readers — Phase 72 Route Attribution
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Constructs, enriches, and normalizes route-attribution records for Claude, Copilot, and OpenCode agents. Trace readers materialize per-call routing metadata into typed `RouteEvent` objects; a heuristic layer and goal-sentence extractor enrich those objects for downstream attribution pipeline consumption without invoking any LLM.

## Architecture
**Two cooperating layers:**

**Trace reader layer** — builds typed `RouteEvent` records from per-provider call context:
- `buildClaudeRouteTrace` — builds a typed route-trace record from Claude agent call context
- `buildCopilotRouteTrace` — builds a route-trace from Copilot call context; implements **dual-field tolerance**: accepts either `toolName` or `name` as the tool identifier, matching fixture variants where both field names appear in real call data
- **OpenCode SQLite reader** — read-only reader extracting route trace data from the SQLite-backed OpenCode call log; shares existing WAL/uid gates via additive export

**Heuristic enrichment layer** — enriches `RouteEvent` objects with goal-sentence extraction and attribution heuristics for downstream pipeline consumption; operates without any LLM invocation

## Key Files
- Route-trace reader modules — contain `buildClaudeRouteTrace` and `buildCopilotRouteTrace`
- OpenCode SQLite reader module — WAL/uid-gated, read-only

## Usage
- Consumed by the downstream attribution pipeline
- All enrichment is heuristic and LLM-free; suitable for high-throughput or offline processing
- OpenCode reader is strictly read-only and shares existing WAL/uid gates

## Troubleshooting
- If Copilot route traces are missing tool identifiers, verify the dual-field tolerance logic is reading both `toolName` and `name` fields from call context
- If OpenCode traces are incomplete or missing, check WAL/uid gate status on the SQLite reader
- Route attribution failures should be diagnosed at the trace reader layer first before investigating heuristic enrichment
- Goal-sentence extraction failures are contained within the heuristic layer and do not block `RouteEvent` materialization

attributes.name: Measurement Orchestrator — Route Writes, Heuristics, and Goal Derivation
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Orchestrates the full measurement-stop close pipeline: token aggregation, six flat heuristics, freeform goal derivation, idempotent route node writes, and LLM judge scoring. Materializes per-run routing decisions, outcome metrics, and scores into the experiment store on `/gsd close`. Exposes two idempotent recompute CLIs for retroactive correction without touching live data. Stop/close requests route exclusively through `vkb-server`'s `/api/experiments/*` endpoints.

## Architecture
Four integrated subsystems wired through `measurement-stop.mjs`:

**Route node writes (idempotent):**
- `/gsd close` writes exactly one Route node per run with a `tookRoute` edge; idempotency guard checks for an existing Route node before writing — re-running close never produces a duplicate
- Untraceable runs: all six heuristics must write `null` (not `0`) when source data is absent — explicit null guard required in derivation logic

**Six flat measurement heuristics:**
- Derived from run telemetry; null-guarded for absent source data; written alongside the Route node

**Goal derivation:**
- Freeform goal text derived from run context; written as a node property during close

**Judge-based success scoring:**
- `runJudge` (in `lib/experiments/judge.mjs`) invoked per close for per-run score recomputation
- Score written via `score-write.mjs` (`writeScore` idempotent; explicit override via `applyOverride`)

**API routing (decided):**
- Measurement stop/close routes through `vkb-server`'s `/api/experiments/*` endpoints — `vkb-server` is the canonical experiment API owner
- `api-routes.js` in `vkb-server` wires the stop/close path; no additional `server.js` changes required
- **Open architectural decision:** whether the dashboard Stop button invokes the full close pipeline directly via this API route, or defers to a host-side CLI call

## Key Files
- `measurement-stop.mjs` — close-path orchestrator; entry point for all stop/close pipeline stages
- `api-routes.js` (vkb-server) — wires dashboard stop/close through `/api/experiments/*` endpoints
- `lib/experiments/judge.mjs` — `runJudge` LLM judge implementation
- `lib/experiments/score-write.mjs` — `writeScore` (idempotent) and `applyOverride` (explicit override path)

## Usage
- Triggered on `/gsd close` or via dashboard Stop button; full pipeline fires: token aggregate → six heuristics → goal derivation → route node write → judge score → score write
- Two idempotent recompute CLIs available for retroactive correction without touching live data
- `PATCH /api/experiments/scores/:taskId` exposes the override endpoint for score correction workflows

## Troubleshooting
- Duplicate Route nodes: should not occur due to idempotency guard; if seen, inspect the guard in `measurement-stop.mjs`
- Heuristics writing `0` instead of `null` for missing data: verify explicit null guard in derivation logic
- Stop pipeline not firing from dashboard: check route registration in `api-routes.js`; confirm `vkb-server` is reachable
- Dashboard Stop button invocation mode (direct API vs. CLI) is unresolved; until confirmed, treat direct API call as the default path

attributes.name: Observation Pipeline — ETM Stuck Loop and KG-Anchor Write Failures
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Documents all failure modes where the ETM observation pipeline stalls, crash-loops, or produces silent observation gaps while a process appears alive or is absent. Every mode freezes the dashboard observation count without an explicit error signal; diagnosis always requires active cross-layer count comparison or direct log inspection.

## Architecture
**Three sequential pipeline stages:**
1. **ETM capture** (`~/Agentic/coding/scripts/enhanced-transcript-monitor.js`): launchd-managed singleton; ships observations exclusively via the obs-api proxy contract (`:12436`) — no DB-bypass paths exist; hosts the **resubmission driver**, an infinite-retry engine that re-queues any exchange not yet flagged complete; hangs indefinitely (wedged-but-alive) when obs-api is unreachable
2. **obs-api consolidation** (`:12436`): SQLite-backed authoritative store; a crash here leaves ETM in a blocking fetch loop; SIGKILL + restart is the standard recovery
3. **KG-anchor writes** (downstream of obs-api): failures are silent — observation count in obs-api appears normal while KG entities go stale

**Failure mode catalogue:**
- **Wedged-but-alive**: ETM running but obs-api unreachable; resubmission driver loops indefinitely; observation count frozen with no error log
- **obs-api crash**: ETM enters blocking fetch loop; observation delivery halts until obs-api is restarted
- **KG-anchor silent failure**: Downstream write failures do not propagate upstream; requires explicit KG vs. obs-api count comparison to detect
- **Respawn storm / singleton collision deadlock**: launchd with `KeepAlive: true` treats every singleton-defer exit (code 0) as a crash and relaunches every ~15s; each short-lived spawn advances the transcript cursor without accumulating enough exchanges to fire observations; colliding heartbeats keep the stale holder alive, blocking the auto-reclaim path — hundreds of collision attempts per day with zero observations generated; structural fix is `KeepAlive: {SuccessfulExit: false}` paired with the exit-code contract (see LSL Infrastructure insight)

## Key Files
- `~/Agentic/coding/scripts/enhanced-transcript-monitor.js` — ETM daemon; singleton enforcement, exit-code contract constants, resubmission driver
- `launchd/com.coding.etm.plist` — launchd plist; must use `KeepAlive: {SuccessfulExit: false}` to prevent respawn storms
- `scripts/install-etm-launchd.sh` — daemon installer (lint → copy → bootout → bootstrap → verify)
- `memory/project_etm_singleton_stall_reclaim.md` — reference for singleton stall scenarios and reclaim procedures

## Usage
The dashboard observation count is the primary liveness signal. Cross-layer count comparison — ETM cursor position vs. obs-api stored count vs. KG entity count — is the standard diagnostic method for any gap. The Jest regression suite (`31` tests) covers exit-code contract behavior and should be run after any changes to `enhanced-transcript-monitor.js`.

## Troubleshooting
**Respawn storm**: `pgrep -f enhanced-transcript-monitor` shows repeated short-lived PIDs; kill all simultaneously, then `launchctl kickstart` one clean instance; verify zero collision entries within 12s. Confirm plist has `KeepAlive: {SuccessfulExit: false}`.
**Wedged-but-alive**: Check obs-api reachability at `:12436`; SIGKILL obs-api process and restart; ETM resubmission driver will resume automatically once obs-api is back.
**Silent KG gaps**: Compare obs-api stored observation count against KG entity count; re-trigger anchor writes if diverged.
**Stale holder blocking reclaim**: A holder with valid heartbeat but zero observation output blocks new instances; manual simultaneous kill required. Pending hardening: reclaim logic should trigger on zero-observation activity window, not heartbeat staleness alone.
**Observation count frozen with no errors**: Run cross-layer count comparison first; do not assume ETM is the bottleneck — obs-api crash or KG-anchor failure can produce identical symptoms.

attributes.name: Observation Pipeline — Observation-Writer Idle Probe Escalation
attributes.description:
## Purpose
The observation-writer contains a strong-probe recovery path that misinterprets idle periods as pipeline stalls and escalates to ~1,000/hr synthetic LLM probes. This path bypasses all existing rate gates and is entirely independent of the health-coordinator's `userActiveNow()` idle gate. It is the dominant remaining idle-state API burn source; no fix is currently applied.

## Architecture
- **Strong-probe stream**: fires `prompt_preview: "say OK"` synthetic probes every ~3.6–5 s when the pipeline appears idle; measured at ~1,000/hr — 5–10× the pre-escalation overnight baseline of 107–204/hr
- **Trigger mechanism**: the recovery path interprets any idle or low-activity period as a pipeline stall and fires on every tick (~5 s); the specific stall-detection branch within the observation-writer source has not yet been isolated
- **Rate gate bypass**: this path does not route through the standard 5-min or 30-min throttle gates — all existing rate-limiting logic is bypassed
- **Independence**: entirely independent of the health-coordinator's `userActiveNow()` idle gate; that gate does not suppress strong probes

## Key Files
- Observation-writer source (exact path not yet confirmed) — contains the stall-detection and strong-probe dispatch logic; the specific escalating branch has not yet been isolated

## Usage
- Runs continuously as part of the observation pipeline
- Under normal active conditions: baseline ~107–204 probes/hr
- Under idle conditions with escalation active: ~1,000/hr

## Troubleshooting
- **High API burn during idle periods**: Strong-probe escalation is active; the stall-detection branch in the observation-writer must be located and gated on a meaningful activity signal
- **`userActiveNow()` gate not suppressing probes**: This is expected — strong probes bypass the health-coordinator idle gate entirely; a separate gate within the observation-writer is required
- **No fix currently applied**: Isolate the escalating stall-detection branch in the observation-writer source before attempting a fix

attributes.name: VKB Unified-Viewer Graph Rendering — Phase 60 Open Issues
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Tracks discrete bugs in the Phase 60 VKB knowledge graph rendering pipeline within the unified-viewer. Bugs affect ontology filter routing, relation-type deduplication, edge legend accuracy, and D3 canvas layer isolation. Issues are addressed sequentially in queue order (#6 → #9).

## Architecture
**Open issue queue (sequential, #6 first):**
- **#6 — Ontology filter routing gap (A/B variant)**: Two distinct filter code paths both exhibit the same routing gap; requires parallel investigation of both A and B paths — fixing only one leaves the gap in the other.
- **#7 — Duplicate relation types**: Duplicate or conflicting relation-type definitions cause incorrect edge rendering or deduplication failures when building the D3 canvas edge set.
- **#8 — Edge legend–canvas mismatch**: The edge-type legend displayed in the UI does not match the actual edge types rendered on the D3 canvas; legend data source diverges from the canvas edge-type set.
- **#9**: Details not confirmed in available sources.

## Key Files
- Unified-viewer VKB rendering module (specific paths not confirmed in current sources).

## Usage
- Phase 60 active work; issues must be resolved in queue order (#6 → #9) to prevent cascading conflicts between fixes.
- D3 canvas and edge legend are separate data paths — fixes to one do not automatically correct the other.

## Troubleshooting
- **#6**: Both A and B filter code paths require investigation; identify which bucket routing conditions diverge.
- **#7**: Deduplicate relation-type definitions before rebuilding the canvas edge set to avoid deduplication failures at render time.
- **#8**: Compare the legend's data source directly against the edge-type set passed to the D3 renderer — they must derive from the same source.

metadata.scope: The active open issue queue for the unified-viewer's VKB knowledge graph rendering pipeline, covering filter correctness, data integrity, legend accuracy, and layer isolation in the D3 canvas.

attributes.name: Observation Pipeline — ETM Stuck Loop and KG-anchor Write Failures
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Documents all failure modes where the ETM observation pipeline stalls, crash-loops, or produces silent observation gaps while the process appears alive or is absent. Every mode freezes the dashboard observation count without an explicit error signal; diagnosis always requires active cross-layer count comparison or direct log inspection.

## Architecture
**Three sequential pipeline stages:**
1. **ETM capture** (`~/Agentic/coding/scripts/enhanced-transcript-monitor.js`): launchd-managed singleton; ships observations exclusively via the obs-api proxy contract (`:12436`) — no DB-bypass paths exist; hosts the **resubmission driver**, an infinite-retry engine that re-queues any exchange not yet flagged complete; hangs indefinitely (wedged-but-alive) when obs-api is unreachable
2. **obs-api consolidation** (`:12436`): SQLite-backed authoritative store (`observations.db`); a SIGKILL crash here leaves ETM in a blocking fetch loop; restart is the standard recovery
3. **KG-anchor writes** (downstream): failures here do not surface upstream; observations may be committed to SQLite while remaining absent from the knowledge graph

**Failure modes by observable symptom:**
- **ETM wedged-but-alive** (obs-api unreachable): ETM process alive, launchd healthy, zero new observations; obs-api is down or SIGKILL'd; fix: restart obs-api
- **`promptSet=0` / zero extraction**: ETM alive and polling but extracting no observations from the current session transcript; indicates transcript path mismatch, cursor misalignment, or a singleton deadlock (see "ETM Singleton Arbitration and Reclaim")
- **Singleton deadlock / silent cursor advancement**: launchd respawning new ETM instances every ~15 s (`KeepAlive + ThrottleInterval=15`); each new instance fails the singleton guard and exits — but advances the fire cursor before doing so, marking exchanges as processed without emitting observations; see "ETM Singleton Arbitration and Reclaim" for root cause and fix
- **KG-anchor write lag**: obs-api count healthy but downstream cold-store JSON falls behind; see "Cold-Store Exporter — Write Lag"

## Key Files
- `~/Agentic/coding/scripts/enhanced-transcript-monitor.js` — ETM capture daemon; singleton host; resubmission driver
- `observations.db` — SQLite authoritative store (owned by obs-api at `:12436`)
- `singleton-reclaim.mjs` — reclaim logic for stale ETM singleton holders; wired into STALL-DETECT watchdog
- `.data/exports/knowledge-export/general.json` — cold-store snapshot (downstream of obs-api)

## Usage
Primary diagnosis entry point: compare live `observations.db` row count against the dashboard display count. If counts diverge, cross-check ETM launchd status, obs-api process liveness, and obs-api logs in sequence. For singleton deadlock, check PID count and whether cursor position has advanced past exchanges with no corresponding `observations.db` rows.

## Troubleshooting
- **Dashboard count frozen, ETM alive**: Query `observations.db` directly; if count matches dashboard, problem is downstream (KG / cold-store); if also frozen, check obs-api liveness
- **obs-api SIGKILL'd**: Restart obs-api; ETM will resume once its blocking fetch loop unblocks
- **`promptSet=0`**: Verify transcript path, inspect cursor state file, then check for singleton deadlock (multiple ETM PIDs, or no new observations since a specific timestamp despite launchd activity)
- **Silent gaps + rapid launchd start/exit cycles**: Singleton deadlock; `pkill -f enhanced-transcript-monitor` to atomically clear all instances; launchd restarts exactly one clean instance within the ThrottleInterval
- **Observation-export JSON**: Inspect to trace where data flow breaks; compare against `observations.db` count to isolate whether the gap is in capture, consolidation, or export

## Purpose
Documents all failure modes where the ETM observation pipeline stalls, crash-loops, or produces silent observation gaps while the process appears alive or is absent. Every mode freezes the dashboard observation count without an explicit error signal; diagnosis always requires active cross-layer count comparison or direct log inspection.

## Architecture
**Three sequential pipeline stages:**
1. **ETM capture** (`~/Agentic/coding/scripts/enhanced-transcript-monitor.js`): launchd-managed singleton; ships observations exclusively via the obs-api proxy contract (`:12436`) — no DB-bypass paths exist; hosts the **resubmission driver**, an infinite-retry engine that re-queues any exchange not yet flagged complete; hangs indefinitely (wedged-but-alive) when obs-api is unreachable
2. **obs-api consolidation** (`:12436`): SQLite-backed authoritative store (`observations.db`); a SIGKILL crash here leaves ETM in a blocking fetch loop; restart is the standard recovery
3. **KG-anchor writes** (downstream): failures here do not surface upstream; observations may be committed to SQLite while remaining absent from the knowledge graph

**Failure modes by observable symptom:**
- **ETM wedged-but-alive** (obs-api unreachable): ETM process alive, launchd healthy, zero new observations; obs-api is down or SIGKILL'd; fix: restart obs-api
- **`promptSet=0` / zero extraction**: ETM alive and polling but extracting no observations from the current session transcript; indicates transcript path mismatch, cursor misalignment, or a singleton deadlock (see "ETM Singleton Arbitration and Reclaim")
- **Singleton deadlock / silent cursor advancement**: launchd respawning new ETM instances every ~15 s (`KeepAlive + ThrottleInterval=15`); each new instance fails the singleton guard and exits — but advances the fire cursor before doing so, marking exchanges as processed without emitting observations; see "ETM Singleton Arbitration and Reclaim" for root cause and fix
- **KG-anchor write lag**: obs-api count healthy but downstream cold-store JSON falls behind; see "Cold-Store Exporter — Write Lag"

## Key Files
- `~/Agentic/coding/scripts/enhanced-transcript-monitor.js` — ETM capture daemon; singleton host; resubmission driver
- `observations.db` — SQLite authoritative store (owned by obs-api at `:12436`)
- `singleton-reclaim.mjs` — reclaim logic for stale ETM singleton holders; wired into STALL-DETECT watchdog
- `.data/exports/knowledge-export/general.json` — cold-store snapshot (downstream of obs-api)

## Usage
Primary diagnosis entry point: compare live `observations.db` row count against the dashboard display count. If counts diverge, cross-check ETM launchd status, obs-api process liveness, and obs-api logs in sequence. For singleton deadlock, check PID count and whether cursor position has advanced past exchanges with no corresponding `observations.db` rows.

## Troubleshooting
- **Dashboard count frozen, ETM alive**: Query `observations.db` directly; if count matches dashboard, problem is downstream (KG / cold-store); if also frozen, check obs-api liveness
- **obs-api SIGKILL'd**: Restart obs-api; ETM will resume once its blocking fetch loop unblocks
- **`promptSet=0`**: Verify transcript path, inspect cursor state file, then check for singleton deadlock (multiple ETM PIDs, or no new observations since a specific timestamp despite launchd activity)
- **Silent gaps + rapid launchd start/exit cycles**: Singleton deadlock; `pkill -f enhanced-transcript-monitor` to atomically clear all instances; launchd restarts exactly one clean instance within the ThrottleInterval
- **Observation-export JSON**: Inspect to trace where data flow breaks; compare against `observations.db` count to isolate whether the gap is in capture, consolidation, or export

attributes.name: Health Coordinator — Idle Gate
attributes.description:
## Purpose
`health-coordinator.js` maintains two independent synthetic-probe suppression gates that minimize unnecessary LLM API calls during idle or active-work periods. Gate 1 (main ~5s probe cycle) is currently regressed and fires unconditionally. Gate 2 (real-traffic pre-check) has been hardened and achieves near-zero synthetic calls during consolidation bursts. The primary visible symptom of the Gate 1 regression is hourly `"say OK"` LLM proxy health-check pings continuing uninterrupted through multi-day AFK periods, burning tokens with no user benefit.

## Architecture
- **Gate 1 — `userActiveNow()` (~5s main probe cycle)**
  - Evaluated before every coordinator probe cycle; returning `false` suppresses all probes for that tick, including hourly LLM proxy health-check pings (`prompt_preview: "say OK"`)
  - **Correct signal**: last-modified time (`mtime`) of the active session transcript file; `transcriptPath` is available in the heartbeat payload at line ~410
  - **Currently regressed**: reads `lastBeat` freshness (line ~405) instead — reflects ETM daemon liveness, not user activity; probe cycle fires unconditionally while the ETM daemon is alive regardless of how long the user has been AFK
  - **Fix path**: restore `transcriptPath`-based `mtime` comparison in `userActiveNow()`; the heartbeat payload already carries `transcriptPath` at line ~410
- **Gate 2 — real-traffic pre-check**
  - Covers both the 60s auto-heal FSM and the cheap probe path
  - Extended with a liveness-proof check and concurrency guards; substantially closes idle-period probe leakage on this path
  - Operates independently of Gate 1 — Gate 2 functioning correctly does not compensate for the Gate 1 regression

## Key Files
- `health-coordinator.js` — contains both gates; `userActiveNow()` function (~line 405) is the regressed entry point; `transcriptPath` from heartbeat payload at ~line 410 is the correct AFK signal source

## Usage
Gate 1 is evaluated on every ~5s coordinator tick. Gate 2 is evaluated before the 60s auto-heal FSM and cheap-probe path. Both gates are internal to `health-coordinator.js` and require no external configuration. The coordinator runs as a persistent background service.

## Troubleshooting
- **Symptom**: hourly `"say OK"` LLM proxy pings continue during extended AFK periods → Gate 1 (`userActiveNow()`) is firing `true` unconditionally
- **Diagnosis**: check line ~405 in `health-coordinator.js` — if it reads `lastBeat` rather than the transcript file's `mtime`, the regression is present
- **Fix**: replace the `lastBeat`-based freshness check with a `fs.statSync(transcriptPath).mtimeMs` comparison; `transcriptPath` is already available from the heartbeat payload at line ~410
- **Gate 2 unaffected**: if only hourly pings are leaking (not the full 5s burst cycle), Gate 2 is healthy and only Gate 1 needs remediation

attributes.name: Unified Viewer — Integration Test Failure Clusters
attributes.description:
## Purpose
Documents the five root-cause clusters behind 21 failing integration tests in the unified-viewer. Clusters 1–4 are stale assertions from intentional product-rename and palette changes; cluster 5 (`useNodeToBucketsIndex`) is a potential real runtime defect requiring separate investigation.

## Architecture
**Five failure clusters (21 total):**
1. **Product rename (~6 failures)**: Assertions reference old names `Coding` / `OKB`; current product names are `VKB` / `VOKB`. Pure string-constant test maintenance — no production defect.
2. **Edge opacity (~5 failures)**: Assertions expect opacity `0.6`; palette was intentionally updated to `0.35`. Update the expected value.
3. **Color fallback (~2 failures)**: Assertions expect amber `#f59e0b`; the VKB-reference rewrite deliberately replaced the fallback with slate-grey `#94a3b8` for unmapped ontology classes. Stale assertions.
4. **`vokb-palette` snapshot mismatch (~1 failure)**: Stored snapshot reflects the pre-rewrite palette state. Requires snapshot regeneration after confirming the current palette is correct.
5. **`useNodeToBucketsIndex` undefined returns (~4 failures)**: Hook returns `undefined` under certain call patterns; root cause unconfirmed and distinct from the stale-assertion clusters. Linked to the broader color-fallback / grey-legend investigation as a potential shared pipeline defect.

## Key Files
- `UnifiedViewer.tsx` — color and legend pipeline; source of the color-fallback change (cluster 3)
- `vokb-palette.ts` — palette definitions; source of opacity change (cluster 2) and snapshot baseline (cluster 4)
- `useNodeToBucketsIndex` — bucket-index hook exhibiting undefined-return defect (cluster 5)

## Usage
- Integration test suite covers the unified-viewer rendering pipeline end-to-end
- Clusters 1–4 require only assertion updates to reflect current intentional behavior — no code changes needed
- Cluster 5 requires root-cause investigation before its assertions can be safely updated

## Troubleshooting
- **Product name failures**: grep test files for `"Coding"` / `"OKB"` and replace with `"VKB"` / `"VOKB"`
- **Opacity failures**: update expected opacity from `0.6` to `0.35` in affected test assertions
- **Color-fallback failures**: update expected fallback from `#f59e0b` to `#94a3b8`
- **Snapshot mismatch**: run the test runner with `--updateSnapshot` after verifying the current `vokb-palette` state is intentional
- **`useNodeToBucketsIndex` undefined**: instrument the call site to capture which inputs produce `undefined`; verify the bucket index is fully constructed before the hook executes; check whether ontology-class distribution queries confirm which classes are reaching the hook with missing index entries
